# @moku-labs/editor — full reference

> Editor, devtools and MCP layer for @moku-labs/game, built on @moku-labs/core. Three Moku cores in one package: `editor-agent` (game page), `editor-server` (Bun), `editor-tools` (tools page). One registry of sources and commands feeds the in-game overlay, the tools page and headless tests. The tools page's Render workspace (Mission control) reads one source at a time: the local preview or a phone connected from the editor, by wire (Android, adb) or on the network. The editor reaches the game only through `@moku-labs/game/inspect` and `@moku-labs/game/control` plus the game's `.dev` modules.

This file is the complete machine-readable reference. Every `Config`, `Api` and event payload type below is copied verbatim from `src/config.ts`, `src/plugins/registry/protocol/`, `src/plugins/hub/protocol/`, `src/plugins/connect/protocol/`, `src/plugins/perf/protocol/`, `src/plugins/recorder/protocol.ts` and `src/plugins/<name>/types.ts`. The short overview is `llms.txt`; the human overview is `README.md`; detail per plugin is `src/plugins/<name>/README.md`.

Contents:

1. Package and entry points
2. The three cores (`src/config.ts` verbatim)
3. Wire protocol types (verbatim), with the device link, the tools link and the connect module
3b. perf protocol types (verbatim)
4. Error codes
5. Event catalog
6. Configuration reference (type, default, description)
7. Plugins: Config, Api and constants verbatim (22 plugins)
8. Dependency graph and init order
9. Multi-plugin usage examples
10. Writing a custom plugin for each core
11. Wire methods

---

## 1. Package and entry points

- Name: `@moku-labs/editor`, MIT, ESM only (`"type": "module"`).
- Peer dependencies: `@moku-labs/game >= 0.15.0` and `typescript >= 5.5`, both required. The bin's engine page needs `@moku-labs/game/cli` `preparePage` and `watchKeys` (0.13.1). The server opens the game's project index (`@moku-labs/game/project`), which needs `typescript`. Without them the index is off and every view that needs a code location says `Project index is off: <reason>` (see the next item).
- Project index (D-38 … D-48): the server core's `files` plugin opens the project index of its root on start and keeps it fresh with its watch; the tools page asks it through the files-channel `find { key }` (lines read from disk at the call) and reads the key maps from the published `editor.project` state (`link.project()`, event `link:project`). The index is the only source of code locations: Flow node and flow files, the Code tab, Used by, the picked element's JSX and style block, projections, text styles, the asset manifest. A key the index does not know shows `Not in the project index: <key>`; no guess, no crawl. The index needs no `bunfig.toml` (that is only for the hot swap plugin). Moves and edits by agents while the editor is open are followed: open tabs, Used by, Code tab lines, caches.
- Breaking (project index): removed the node → file rule exports (`nodeFile`, `flowFile`, `kebab`, `parseOverrides`, `SOURCE_ROOTS`, `SOURCE_OVERRIDES_PATH`, types `SourceOverrides`) and the protocol file `source-files.ts`; the configs `flowView.stylesFile`, `gameView.manifestPaths`, `gameView.sourceSearch`, `renderView.manifestPaths`; `.moku/editor/files.json` is ignored; the graph node `file` field (F-H2) is gone; `UsedBy.usedIn` is new; `StyleEditCode` gains `"broken"` (no style write while the file does not parse) and `"index-off"` (no style write while the index is off); a key built in a loop answers the element line. `@moku-labs/game >= 0.7.0` and `typescript >= 5.5` are required.
- Breaking (editor UI cleanup, D-65 … D-69): Reference mode is gone (`workspace.reference()`, `setReference()`, the event `workspace:reference`, key R, the Esc layer `reference`, the top-bar toggle and its ⋯ row, gameView's `data-moku-*` proxy layer); the element picker (the Select button of the Game toolbar, ⇧⌘C, I, the area drag) is the one way to pick. `workspace` gains `copyOnSelect()` and `setCopyOnSelect(on)`, and `Prefs` gains `copyOnSelect`: a picker click writes the reference and copies its line only while the preference is on (the default; the "Copy Ref" switch of the Game toolbar); with it off the click only selects the element and writes nothing (D-70, D-72). The top bar starts with `span[data-mark]` (was `span[data-logo]`). The Flow Inspector has the tabs Info and Code: the Styles tab, the palette group "Styles" (`PaletteGroup` has no `"Styles"`) and the config key `flowView.styleSaveDelayMs` are removed. A series no longer opens the contact sheet when it ends. `gameView` gains `editStyle`, `clearEdits`, `edits` and `copyEdits`; the protocol gains `StyleEdit`, `StyleValue` and `SelectionInfo.edits`.
- Doors: game 0.4 replaced `game.rect` with `game.locate` (input `{ key?: string; target?: json }`, answers `Rect | undefined`) and makes `game.capture` answer `{ png: string, legend? }` instead of the data URL itself. The calibration of gameView and renderView reads `{ key }` from `game.locate` when the manifest lists it, else from `game.rect` (`rectSourceOf` in `panels/shared/scene`); with neither, nothing is read, nothing is warned, and the picker says "This game reports no element rects". The capture plugin takes a data URL or an object with a string `png` (`pictureOf`); anything else is still "game.capture gave no picture".
- `files` in the package: `dist`, `LICENSE`, `README.md`, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`. `"sideEffects": false`.
- Production builds: import the agent only inside `if (__MOKU_GAME_DEV__) { await import("@moku-labs/editor/agent") … }`. With the flag defined `false` the bundle keeps no editor code (0 B); with `true` the agent (perf with Mission control's feeds, recorder, the overlay with its three subset Barlow faces, bridge, capture) adds 299,859 B minified (122,297 B gzip), bounded at 124 KB gzip (124,000 B; raised from 120 KB by the owner for Mission control's feeds: the phone only reads, the tools page builds the marks, the pass chains and the history). The agent core in `src/agent.ts` and every agent plugin are created `/* @__PURE__ */`. See README "Production builds" and `tests/integration/agent-bundle.test.ts`.
- Debug builds (engine spec 10): `moku-game build --debug[=read] [--editor host:port]` and `moku-game native build android --debug` put `@moku-labs/editor/agent/page` on a page with `__MOKU_GAME_DEV__` `false` and `__MOKU_GAME_AGENT__` `true`; engine 0.15.1 sets `__MOKU_GAME_CONTROL__` `true` on `--debug` (every command; `--debug=full` is an alias) and `false` on `--debug=read` (read and cosmetic commands); on 0.15.0 `--debug` had no control and `--debug=full` added it. The page agent runs behind the inline guard `__MOKU_GAME_DEV__ || __MOKU_GAME_AGENT__`: a debug page keeps it (299,807 B, 123,404 B gzip), a release page (both `false`) drops it (0 B of editor code; the whole entry is 155 B, 141 B gzip). The store check of a release build looks for `/__editor/hello` and `[moku-editor]`. The phone tools need the engine release with the build flags, the renderer monitor and the `debug` plugin (0.15.0, the peer floor); the pass owners, filters and draws, the `shader` and `problem` events, the sample's object counts and render targets, the app id and control on `--debug` need 0.15.1, the engine the editor is developed and tested against (on 0.15.0 those blocks are absent and read not measured).
- Phones (README "On a phone"): device mode is turned on by `moku-editor perf`, or from the dev tools page by the server's `connect` plugin (Render's Connect panel: `connect.wire` for Android by wire, `connect.network` for the LAN listener); a phone pairs (by wire at once, on the network by a four-digit code typed in the terminal or the tools page), runs as an ordinary agent session with `SessionInfo.device`, and ships its recorder log while it records, which the collector writes to `.moku/perf/`. No iOS debug build exists yet, so an iPhone cannot link.
- One active source (spec 11): the tools core's `activeSource` keeps one source per page, the local preview or a phone or another page; it pauses the local preview (`game.pause` on this page's own frame session) before link chooses a phone and resumes it after. Render's Mission control (renderView) reads only that source: a 2-minute frame timeline built on the tools page from perf's feeds (`editor.perf.frames`, `editor.perf.events`, `editor.perf.passes`, `editor.perf.detail`, `editor.perf.second`, `editor.recorder`), the cards, the Connect panel, Record and Monitoring.
- Memory sources: a phone's JS heap comes from the computer, CDP over USB (connect attaches `Runtime.getHeapUsage` through `adb forward` for a wired phone a tools page watches); an Android WebView's `performance.memory` is frozen (10.68 MB on a Galaxy A26 while the real heap swings 27–57 MB) and is never shown as the phone's heap. Wired telemetry (GPU clock and busy %, CPU and memory per process, JS heap samples, inferred GCs) is published once a second as `editor.deviceTelemetry`; the collector writes it as `telemetry` lines while the phone records.
- Recording is off by default: `recorder.autoStart` is `false`; the overlay's Record tab, Render's Record and an agent (`editor.record { on?, label?, mark? }`) start, stop and mark the same log, and `startedBy` (`RecordOrigin`) says who started it.
- Dependencies: `@moku-labs/common`, `@moku-labs/core`, `elkjs`, `preact`.
- Engines: node >= 24, bun >= 1.4.2. The server core and the bin need Bun (`Bun.serve`, HTML imports).
- Bin: `moku-editor` → `./dist/bin.mjs` (source `src/plugins/pages/bin.ts`). Without an html file, in a moku-game folder (`index.ts` + `config.ts`), it serves the engine page: `preparePage` of `@moku-labs/game/cli` with the editor's page agent, the engine's keys watch (`watchKeys` of the same `cli`, in the parent bin until the child exits), then a re-run under `<root>/.moku/bunfig.toml` (see "Engine page" in section 6). It serves with Bun hot reload on (D-23); `--no-hmr` turns it off. `moku-editor mcp` is the stdio MCP server for Claude Code; `moku-editor mcp-config` prints its setup; `moku-editor perf [--lan] [--port] [--out] [--every] [--no-ui]` measures phones, with `perf mark`, `perf summary` and `perf compare` (see "Bin" in section 6).

| Import | File | Exports |
|---|---|---|
| `@moku-labs/editor` | `src/index.ts` | Protocol types (`Json`, `Manifest`, `BuildInfo`, `BuildProfile`, `CommandRefusal`, `CommandVia`, `OverlayMarker`, `LinkStatus`, `EditorChannel`, `RunResult`, `WireError`, `SessionInfo`, `ToolsBoot`, `FileEntry`, …), protocol helpers (`checkInput`, `toWireValue`, `encode`, `decode`, `request`, `notification`, `success`, `failure`, `isRequest`, `isResponse`, `isNotification`, `isFailure`, `isJson`, `wireError`, `isWireError`, `toWireError`, `fromWireError`, `isRetryable`, `bareMessage`, `isReloading`, `isHotSwapEntry`, `errorCode`, `ERROR_PREFIX`, `ProtocolError`, `parseProjectState`, `parseFoundList`, `projectDelta`, `firstDefinition`, `anchorKey`, `refusalOf`, `isAllowed`), project types (`ProjectState`, `ProjectFound`, `ProjectAnchor`, `ProjectDelta`, `ProjectChange`, `ProjectMove`, `FindParams`), `definePanel`, `SourceValue`, `CompactTools`, `PanelInput`, `PanelSpec`, `PanelTools`, `PanelValues`, `SourceRef`. Runtime-free: no plugin, no core. `perf/protocol`, `perf/graph` and `collector/report` are not root exports (their types are `Perf.*` and `Collector.*`). |
| `@moku-labs/editor/agent` | `src/agent.ts` | `createApp`, `createPlugin`, `bridgePlugin`, `capturePlugin`, `channelPlugin`, `overlayPlugin`, `perfPlugin`, `recorderPlugin`, `registryPlugin`, namespaces `Bridge`, `Capture`, `Channel`, `Overlay`, `Perf`, `Recorder`, `Registry`. |
| `@moku-labs/editor/agent/page` | `src/agent-page.ts` | Default export only: `editorAgent`, a `PageAgent<Registry.GameLike>` of `@moku-labs/game/app` (D-49). The engine's dev page and a debug build call it after the game started with `{ app, name, modules }`. Behind the inline guard `__MOKU_GAME_DEV__ || __MOKU_GAME_AGENT__` (neither flag: it starts nothing) it stops a previous `globalThis.editor`, then `createApp({ plugins: [bridgePlugin, capturePlugin], pluginConfigs: { registry: { game: app, name, modules } } })`, sets `globalThis.editor` and starts it. No side effect on import. |
| `@moku-labs/editor/server` | `src/server.ts` | `createApp`, `createPlugin`, `collectorPlugin`, `connectPlugin`, `filesPlugin`, `hubPlugin`, `pagesPlugin`, namespaces `Collector`, `Connect`, `Files`, `Hub`, `Pages`. |
| `@moku-labs/editor/tools` | `src/tools.ts` | `createApp`, `createPlugin`, `linkPlugin`, `activeSourcePlugin`, `workspacePlugin`, `panelsPlugin`, `flowViewPlugin`, `gameViewPlugin`, `renderViewPlugin`, `stateViewPlugin`, `filesViewPlugin`, `consoleViewPlugin`, namespaces `Link`, `ActiveSource`, `Workspace`, `Panels`, `FlowView`, `GameView`, `RenderView`, `StateView`, `FilesView`, `ConsoleView`. |

Default plugins per core (from the entries):

```ts
// src/agent.ts — dependency order: channel and perf require registry; recorder requires perf;
// overlay requires registry, channel, perf and recorder.
// Pure: a bundle that uses neither createApp nor createPlugin drops the agent core.
const framework = /* @__PURE__ */ createAgentCore(agentCoreConfig, {
  plugins: [registryPlugin, channelPlugin, perfPlugin, recorderPlugin, overlayPlugin]
});
// opt-in: bridgePlugin, capturePlugin (passed in createApp({ plugins }))

// src/server.ts — plugin order (D-03, spec 11 § 1): files ← hub ← connect ← collector ← pages.
// connect requires hub (device mode, editor methods); collector is idle until hub's device listener
// reports a phone (hub:device); pages depends on collector and hooks its per-plugin collector:session.
createServerCore(serverCoreConfig, { plugins: [filesPlugin, hubPlugin, connectPlugin, collectorPlugin, pagesPlugin] });

// src/tools.ts — activeSource requires link; workspace requires link and activeSource; panels requires
// link and workspace; every view requires link and panels (all but stateView also workspace; renderView
// also activeSource). No view depends on another view.
createToolsCore(toolsCoreConfig, {
  plugins: [
    linkPlugin, activeSourcePlugin, workspacePlugin, panelsPlugin,
    flowViewPlugin, gameViewPlugin, renderViewPlugin, stateViewPlugin, filesViewPlugin, consoleViewPlugin
  ]
});
```

---

## 2. The three cores (`src/config.ts`, verbatim)

~~~ts
/**
 * Global config of the agent core (the game page). Empty: every option belongs to a plugin.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const config: AgentConfig = {};
 * ```
 */
export type AgentConfig = Record<never, never>;

/**
 * Global config of the server core (Bun). Empty: every option belongs to a plugin.
 */
export type ServerConfig = Record<never, never>;

/**
 * Global config of the tools core (the tools page). Empty: every option belongs to a plugin.
 */
export type ToolsConfig = Record<never, never>;

/**
 * Global events of the agent core. An event lives here only when its listener cannot depend on its
 * emitter:
 * - `bridge:status`: the bridge is opt-in; the default overlay hooks it without depending on it (R2).
 * - `overlay:changed`: its listener, the recorder, is a dependency of the overlay; a per-plugin
 *   event would need recorder → overlay, a cycle.
 * - `overlay:connect`: its listener, the bridge, is opt-in and ordered after every default; the
 *   overlay must not depend on it (decision "bridge pulls from recorder").
 *
 * `recorder:status` (recorder), `registry:command` (registry) and the server's `collector:session`
 * (collector) are per-plugin events of their emitters, hooked through `depends`; they are not
 * declared here.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * ctx.emit("bridge:status", { status: { kind: "live", frame: 12 }, session: "s-7f3a" });
 * ctx.emit("overlay:connect", { address: "192.168.1.5:47600" });
 * ```
 */
export type AgentEvents = {
  /**
   * The bridge link changed kind, session or device link. `link` is present in device mode only: no
   * computer, connecting (with the pairing code), live over adb or the LAN, the computer's engine,
   * last seen.
   */
  "bridge:status": { status: LinkStatus; session?: string; link?: DeviceLink };
  /** The overlay window changed mode or tab (the recorder logs it as a `devtools` monitor event; `overlay` is the game's). */
  "overlay:changed": OverlayChanged;
  /** The Link tab asks for a device link to this address (`host:port`); the opt-in bridge hooks it. */
  "overlay:connect": { address: string };
};

/**
 * Global events of the server core (contracts §4). Unchanged: `collector:session` is the collector's own
 * per-plugin event, and `hub:device` the hub's; neither is declared here.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * ctx.emit("files:written", { path: "nodes/merge.ts", bytes: 812, kind: "code" });
 * ```
 */
export type ServerEvents = {
  /** A game session opened (`open: true`) or closed (`open: false`, with a reason). */
  "hub:session": HubSession;
  /** A file was written inside the project root (text or capture). */
  "files:written": FilesWritten;
  /** The project index of the files root opened, changed or went off (hub publishes it). */
  "files:project": ProjectState;
};

/**
 * Global events of the tools core (R4, R9): notices and one-way intents between the tools
 * plugins. Request/response stays in the plugin apis. No view depends on another view.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * ctx.emit("workspace:open-file", { path: "nodes/merge.ts", line: 12 });
 * ```
 */
export type ToolsEvents = {
  /** The link status or the chosen session changed. */
  "link:status": { status: LinkStatus; session?: string };
  /** A new project-index state arrived; views drop what the delta names. */
  "link:project": { state: ProjectState; delta: ProjectDelta };
  /** The shown workspace changed. */
  "workspace:changed": { ws: WorkspaceId };
  /** A command run from the tools page settled (top bar, palette, key or a panel's tools.run). */
  "workspace:ran": RanEvent;
  /** The applied density changed (a choice, or `auto` crossing 820 px of window width). */
  "workspace:density": { density: Density };
  /** Open a file in the Files workspace (filesView hooks it). */
  "workspace:open-file": { path: string; line?: number };
  /** Focus a node in the Flow workspace (flowView hooks it). */
  "workspace:select-node": { id: string };
  /** Focus the edge taken at a frame (flowView hooks it). */
  "workspace:focus-frame": { frame: number };
  /** Select an element in the render tree (renderView hooks it). */
  "workspace:reveal": { ref: ElementRef };
  /** Inspect an element in the Game workspace (gameView hooks it, R9). */
  "workspace:inspect": { ref: ElementRef };
  /** Open a series contact sheet by its index.json path (gameView hooks it). */
  "workspace:open-sheet": { index: string };
};

/**
 * Public API type of a plugin instance, read from its phantom carrier. Mirrors the kernel's
 * non-exported `ExtractPluginApi`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * type Link = ApiOf<typeof linkPlugin>; // the LinkApi type of src/plugins/link/types.ts
 * ```
 */
export type ApiOf<Plugin> = Plugin extends { readonly _phantom: { readonly api: infer PluginApi } }
  ? PluginApi
  : never;

/**
 * Structural type of `ctx.require`, for domain contexts that resolve their own dependencies. The
 * bound repeats the kernel's plugin shape, so the kernel's generic `require` is assignable to it.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * type WorkspaceCtx = { readonly require: Require };
 * ```
 */
export type Require = <
  Plugin extends {
    readonly name: string;
    readonly spec: unknown;
    readonly _phantom: {
      readonly config: unknown;
      readonly state: unknown;
      readonly api: unknown;
      readonly events: Record<string, unknown>;
    };
  }
>(
  plugin: Plugin
) => ApiOf<Plugin>;

/**
 * The core plugins every core registers: `ctx.log` and `ctx.env` on every plugin context.
 */
export type CorePlugins = [typeof logPlugin, typeof envPlugin];

/**
 * Core config of the agent core (the game page).
 */
export const agentCoreConfig = /* @__PURE__ */ createCoreConfig<
  AgentConfig,
  AgentEvents,
  CorePlugins
>("editor-agent", { config: agentConfig, plugins: [logPlugin, envPlugin] });

/**
 * Core config of the server core (Bun).
 */
export const serverCoreConfig = /* @__PURE__ */ createCoreConfig<
  ServerConfig,
  ServerEvents,
  CorePlugins
>("editor-server", { config: serverConfig, plugins: [logPlugin, envPlugin] });

/**
 * Core config of the tools core (the tools page).
 */
export const toolsCoreConfig = /* @__PURE__ */ createCoreConfig<
  ToolsConfig,
  ToolsEvents,
  CorePlugins
>("editor-tools", { config: toolsConfig, plugins: [logPlugin, envPlugin] });

/**
 * Creates an agent plugin bound to the agent core's Config and Events. Types infer from the spec.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * export const registryPlugin = createAgentPlugin("registry", { config, createState, api });
 * ```
 */
export const createAgentPlugin = agentCoreConfig.createPlugin;

/**
 * Creates a server plugin bound to the server core's Config and Events. Types infer from the spec.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * export const filesPlugin = createServerPlugin("files", { config, createState, api });
 * ```
 */
export const createServerPlugin = serverCoreConfig.createPlugin;

/**
 * Creates a tools plugin bound to the tools core's Config and Events. Types infer from the spec.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * export const linkPlugin = createToolsPlugin("link", { config, createState, api });
 * ```
 */
export const createToolsPlugin = toolsCoreConfig.createPlugin;

/**
 * Creates the agent framework from its core config. Used by `src/agent.ts` only.
 */
export const createAgentCore = agentCoreConfig.createCore;

/**
 * Creates the server framework from its core config. Used by `src/server.ts` only.
 */
export const createServerCore = serverCoreConfig.createCore;

/**
 * Creates the tools framework from its core config. Used by `src/tools.ts` only.
 */
export const createToolsCore = toolsCoreConfig.createCore;
~~~

Each core registers `logPlugin` and `envPlugin` from `@moku-labs/common/browser`: `ctx.log` (leveled events, sinks) and `ctx.env` exist on every plugin context. Plugins log through `ctx.log`, never `console.*`.

An event is global (declared here) only when its listener cannot depend on its emitter: `overlay:changed` (the recorder, its listener, is a dependency of the overlay) and `overlay:connect` (the bridge, its listener, is opt-in). `registry:command`, `recorder:status`, `hub:device`, `connect:telemetry`, `collector:session`, `activeSource:changed` and `activeSource:connect-requested` are per-plugin events of their emitters (`register<T>()` in the plugin's `events`), hooked by the plugins that list the emitter in `depends` (section 5).

---

## 3. Wire protocol types (`src/plugins/registry/protocol/`, verbatim)

The protocol is runtime-free and imports nothing outside itself. It is re-exported from the package root. `project.ts` holds the project-index helpers: `parseProjectState(value)` and `parseFoundList(value)` (strict checked copies, `undefined` for a bad value), `projectDelta(held, next)` (what a view drops: `all: true` after a revision gap, for the first state or an off state; else the lists of `next.change`), `firstDefinition(state, key)` (the first def path of a key, `undefined` when off or unknown) and `anchorKey(ref, path)` (the `style:` or `textStyle:` key of a style block). The project types (`ProjectAnchor`, `ProjectFound`, `ProjectMove`, `ProjectChange`, `ProjectState`, `ProjectDelta`, `FindParams`) mirror the game's `@moku-labs/game/project` types field by field without importing them. `ElementRef` and `PageRect` from `src/plugins/panels/shared/scene/types.ts` (payloads of `workspace:reveal` and `workspace:inspect`). `devices.ts` holds the device presets and their helpers (`DeviceSpec`, `DevicePresetId`, `Orientation`, `DeviceSize` are below); `overlay-host.ts` holds `HOST_ATTRIBUTE`, the DOM marker of the in-game overlay host. `hash.ts` holds `commandsHash(manifest)` (D-37): the commands sorted by id, the JSON of `[id, effect, input]` per command with `input` keys sorted, joined with `\n`, FNV-1a 32-bit, 8 lowercase hex chars; titles and sources do not count. The hub stamps it on `SessionInfo.manifestHash`; the MCP bridge rebuilds its door tools only when it moves. It is in the protocol barrel, not exported from the package root. A refused command (`allowed: false`) hashes as `[id, effect, input, reason]`, so a read-only build's hash differs from the dev page's. `build.ts` holds the build rule: `refusalOf(profile, effect)` (dev and full run every effect, read runs `read` and `cosmetic`, none runs nothing; answers `"read-only"`, `"dev-only"` or `undefined`) and `isAllowed(descriptor)` (`allowed !== false`); both are root exports. `errors.ts` adds `errorCode.readOnly` and `errorCode.devOnly` (both -32009, reasons `read_only` and `dev_only`). The device types of `SessionInfo.device` and `PublishParams.engine` are imported type-only from `hub/protocol`, and the published `devices` (`DeviceDirectory`) and `deviceTelemetry` (`DeviceTelemetry`) of `PublishParams` type-only from `connect/protocol` (both below). `CommandVia` names who ran a command: `"overlay"`, `"tools"` and `"mcp"` (from the hub's run stamp), `"bridge"` (a hub that does not say who), `"local"`.

~~~ts
/**
 * A JSON value, the way it travels on the wire.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const value: Json = { path: "board/awaitIntent", frame: 1840, tainted: false };
 * ```
 */
export type Json = null | boolean | number | string | Json[] | { [key: string]: Json };

/**
 * The kind of one input field of a source or a command.
 */
export type InputKind = "string" | "number" | "boolean" | "json";

/**
 * The input of a source or a command: field name to kind; a kind ending in `?` is optional.
 * Structurally identical to the game's InputSchema.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const step: InputSchema = { frames: "number", deltaMs: "number?" };
 * ```
 */
export type InputSchema = Readonly<Record<string, InputKind | `${InputKind}?`>>;

/**
 * The input value a schema describes; identical definition to the game's InputOf.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * type Step = InputOf<{ frames: "number"; deltaMs: "number?" }>; // { frames: number; deltaMs?: number | undefined }
 * ```
 */
export type InputOf<S extends InputSchema> = Flat<
  { -readonly [K in RequiredKeys<S>]: ValueOf<S[K]> } & {
    -readonly [K in Exclude<keyof S, RequiredKeys<S>>]?: ValueOf<S[K]> | undefined;
  }
>;

/**
 * How often a source value changes: every frame, on each commit, on each graph edge.
 */
export type Changes = "frame" | "commit" | "edge";

/**
 * What a command does to the game.
 */
export type Effect = "read" | "route" | "cosmetic" | "cheat" | "raw";

/**
 * A source the way the manifest describes it (no functions).
 */
export type SourceDescriptor = {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly title: string;
  readonly input: InputSchema;
  readonly changes: Changes;
  /**
   * `false` when the game does not have this source: its door threw on the probe (the game plugin
   * behind it is missing). Reads and watches answer -32008 `not_installed`. Absent = available.
   */
  readonly available?: false;
  /** What the door threw on the probe; present only with `available: false`. */
  readonly reason?: string;
};

/**
 * The overlay marker of a game command (engine spec 12 H4.4): a switch or a button on the
 * overlay's Game tab.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const marker: OverlayMarker = "toggle";
 * ```
 */
export type OverlayMarker = "toggle" | "button";

/**
 * Why the page's build refuses a command: `"read-only"` (a plain `--debug` build runs read and
 * cosmetic commands only), `"dev-only"` (a page without the debug or dev flags runs none).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const refusal: CommandRefusal = "read-only";
 * ```
 */
export type CommandRefusal = "read-only" | "dev-only";

/**
 * The build profile of a game page, from its build flags: `"dev"` (the dev server), `"full"`
 * (`--debug=full`), `"read"` (`--debug`), `"none"` (no flag: a release page or a test without stubs).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const profile: BuildProfile = "read";
 * ```
 */
export type BuildProfile = "dev" | "full" | "read" | "none";

/**
 * The build of a game page: its profile, and the build id, engine fingerprint and app id when the
 * page has them (`__MOKU_GAME_BUILD__`, `__MOKU_GAME_ENGINE__`, `__MOKU_GAME_APP__`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const build: BuildInfo = { profile: "read", id: "debug-20261016T090000Z", engine: "0.15.1+2b7c11", appId: "com.mokulabs.timber.debug" };
 * ```
 */
export type BuildInfo = {
  readonly profile: BuildProfile;
  readonly id?: string;
  readonly engine?: string;
  /**
   * The app id the build wrote (`__MOKU_GAME_APP__`, the same value as the PerfLog header's
   * `app.id`): the bundle identifier, with the `.debug` suffix of a native debug install. Absent on
   * an engine that writes none (0.15.0) and on a page without a native identifier.
   */
  readonly appId?: string;
};

/**
 * Who ran a command: the overlay's Game tab, the tools page, an agent through MCP, a hub that does
 * not say who (`"bridge"`: an editor server from before the hub stamped `from`), or an in-process
 * caller (a test, the game's own code, `channel.run` without a source). The bridge turns the hub's
 * `from` into it (spec 07 Delta 2026-10-16 B1). Agent-side only; never on the wire.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const via: CommandVia = "mcp"; // the recorder's editor.record names the log "started by agent"
 * ```
 */
export type CommandVia = "overlay" | "bridge" | "tools" | "mcp" | "local";

/**
 * A command the way the manifest describes it (no functions). An agent from before the build
 * profile sends no `allowed`: read it as allowed.
 */
export type CommandDescriptor = {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly title: string;
  readonly input: InputSchema;
  readonly effect: Effect;
  /** Shows the command on the overlay's Game tab. Absent: not shown. */
  readonly overlay?: OverlayMarker;
  /** Whether this page's build runs the command (advice; the engine's run decides). */
  readonly allowed?: boolean;
  /** Why the build refuses it; present only with `allowed: false`. */
  readonly reason?: CommandRefusal;
};

/**
 * What a game page offers the editor: sent by the bridge in `hello`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const manifest: Manifest = { game: "merge-game 0.0.0", page: "http://127.0.0.1:3000/", embedded: true, sources: [], commands: [] };
 * ```
 */
export type Manifest = {
  /** Display name, e.g. "merge-game 0.0.0". */
  readonly game: string;
  /** location.href of the game page. */
  readonly page: string;
  /** True when the page runs inside the tools page frame. */
  readonly embedded: boolean;
  readonly sources: readonly SourceDescriptor[];
  readonly commands: readonly CommandDescriptor[];
  /** Reserved for code-loaded game panels; unused this change. */
  readonly panels?: readonly { readonly id: string; readonly module: string }[];
  /**
   * Set by the bridge in its hello when it restored the checkpoint it stored before Bun's full
   * reload (R6): `bookmark` is the JSON text of the restored `game.bookmark` value, `frame` the
   * frame of the page that took it. Absent on every other hello.
   */
  readonly restored?: { readonly bookmark: string; readonly frame: number };
  /** The page's build: profile, build id and engine fingerprint. Absent from an older agent. */
  readonly build?: BuildInfo;
};

/**
 * Where the game stands after a command.
 */
export type RunState = { readonly path: string; readonly frame: number; readonly tainted: boolean };

/**
 * The answer of a command: its value and the run state.
 */
export type RunResult = { readonly value: Json; readonly state: RunState };

/**
 * One heartbeat of a game page. `heap` is the JS heap of the page in MB, rounded to 0.1, and
 * only present where the browser reports it (Chromium's `performance.memory`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const beat: Heartbeat = { frame: 1840, paused: false, at: 1790000000000, heap: { usedMb: 12.8, limitMb: 4095.8 } };
 * ```
 */
export type Heartbeat = {
  readonly frame: number;
  readonly paused: boolean;
  /** Epoch ms of the beat. */
  readonly at: number;
  readonly heap?: { readonly usedMb: number; readonly limitMb: number };
};

/**
 * Params of the game-channel `tap` notification: one pointerdown on the game page. `x` and `y`
 * are page CSS px of the game document (`clientX`, `clientY`); `at` is the page's
 * `performance.now()`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const tap: Tap = { x: 206, y: 640, at: 15234.5 };
 * ```
 */
export type Tap = { readonly x: number; readonly y: number; readonly at: number };

/**
 * The link state shown everywhere (design-context §6 B1, F3). A `lost` with `reloading: true` is
 * an expected reload (U7): a server restart (close 1012), a reload the editor started, or a game
 * that said bye before its reload. The views show it in a neutral tone until the game is back, or
 * as a plain `lost` once link's `reloadGraceMs` ran out.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const status: LinkStatus = { kind: "live", frame: 1840 };
 * const reloading: LinkStatus = { kind: "lost", reason: "socket_closed", lastFrame: 1825, retryInMs: 1000, reloading: true };
 * ```
 */
export type LinkStatus =
  | { kind: "connecting" }
  | { kind: "live"; frame: number }
  | { kind: "paused"; frame: number }
  | { kind: "silent"; since: number; lastFrame: number }
  | { kind: "lost"; reason: string; lastFrame: number; retryInMs: number; reloading?: true }
  | { kind: "empty" };

/**
 * The channel every panel reads through: in process (`app.channel`, the agent channel of the game
 * page) or remote (`app.link`, the tools link to the editor server). The base of `ChannelApi` and
 * `LinkApi`. Errors reject as wire errors: -32601 `unknown_id`, -32602 `invalid_input`, the
 * command's own error; the remote link adds its transport reasons (`timeout`, `link_closed` …).
 */
export type EditorChannel = {
  /**
   * Reads a source now.
   *
   * @param id - The source id, e.g. "game.position".
   * @param input - The source input; omit it for a source without input.
   * @returns A promise of the wire value. It never throws synchronously.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // A panel shows where the game stands.
   * await app.channel.read("game.position"); // { path: "home", … }
   * await app.channel.read("game.history", { last: 1 }); // [{ path: "home", outcome: "play", … }]
   * ```
   */
  read(id: string, input?: Json): Promise<Json>;
  /**
   * Follows a source: delivers the current value first, then every change.
   *
   * @param id - The source id.
   * @param input - The source input; `undefined` means none, but the argument is required.
   * @param onValue - Called with each value.
   * @returns An idempotent stop.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The state view follows the position until the view closes.
   * const stop = app.channel.watch("game.position", undefined, position => show(position));
   * stop();
   * ```
   */
  watch(id: string, input: Json | undefined, onValue: (value: Json) => void): () => void;
  /**
   * Runs a command. The in-process channel runs it in a microtask, off the game's frame loop.
   *
   * @param id - The command id, e.g. "game.step".
   * @param input - The command input; omit it for a command without input.
   * @returns A promise of the command's value and where the game stands after it.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The flow view steps one frame.
   * (await app.channel.run("game.step", { frames: 1 })).state; // { path: "home", frame: 1841, tainted: false }
   * ```
   */
  run(id: string, input?: Json): Promise<RunResult>;
  /**
   * The link state now. The in-process channel answers live or paused only.
   *
   * @returns A fresh LinkStatus.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.channel.status(); // { kind: "live", frame: 1840 }
   * ctx.require(linkPlugin).status(); // { kind: "silent", since: 1790000000000, lastFrame: 1840 }
   * ```
   */
  status(): LinkStatus;
};

/**
 * The logical channel of a wire message.
 */
export type Channel = "game" | "files" | "editor";

/**
 * Why a call failed (R1 adds `link_closed`). The selection relay adds `no_editor_page` (-32003: no
 * tools page with `role=page` is open) and `page_closed` (-32001, retryable: the page closed before
 * it answered). The `node` request adds `no_graph` (-32003, retryable: the Flow view has no graph
 * yet). A build that refuses a command answers `read_only` (a `--debug` page) or `dev_only` (a page
 * without the dev or debug flag), both -32009 and not retryable. connect's editor methods add
 * `port_in_use` and `no_lan` (-32000: device mode could not listen), `not_owner` (-32007: device mode
 * belongs to `moku-editor perf`) and `no_ticket` (-32602: no pairing waits with that ticket), none
 * retryable.
 */
export type ErrorReason =
  | "game_reloaded"
  | "no_session"
  | "choose_session"
  | "timeout"
  | "invalid_input"
  | "unknown_id"
  | "command_failed"
  | "not_json"
  | "forbidden_path"
  | "version_conflict"
  | "unauthorized"
  | "not_installed"
  | "link_closed"
  | "no_editor_page"
  | "page_closed"
  | "no_graph"
  | "read_only"
  | "dev_only"
  | "port_in_use"
  | "no_lan"
  | "not_owner"
  | "no_ticket";

/**
 * A JSON-RPC error object with the editor's data fields.
 */
export type WireError = {
  code: number;
  message: string;
  data?: { retryable?: boolean; reason?: ErrorReason; id?: string; field?: string };
};

/**
 * The `data` member of a WireError.
 */
export type WireErrorData = NonNullable<WireError["data"]>;

/**
 * A request: carries an id and gets exactly one response.
 */
export type Request = {
  jsonrpc: "2.0";
  id: number;
  channel: Channel;
  method: string;
  params?: Json;
  session?: string;
};

/**
 * The response to a request: a result or an error.
 */
export type Response =
  | { jsonrpc: "2.0"; id: number; result: Json }
  | { jsonrpc: "2.0"; id: number; error: WireError };

/**
 * A notification: no id, no response.
 */
export type Notification = {
  jsonrpc: "2.0";
  channel: Channel;
  method: string;
  params?: Json;
  session?: string;
};

/**
 * Any wire message.
 */
export type Message = Request | Response | Notification;

/**
 * A subscription id on the wire: a safe integer ≥ 0 on both hops (R6).
 */
export type SubId = number;

/**
 * Params of the game-channel `read` request.
 */
export type ReadParams = { id: string; input?: Json };

/**
 * Params of the game-channel `watch` request.
 */
export type WatchParams = { sub: SubId; id: string; input?: Json };

/**
 * Params of the game-channel `unwatch` request.
 */
export type UnwatchParams = { sub: SubId };

/**
 * Params of the game-channel `run` request.
 */
export type RunParams = { id: string; input?: Json };

/**
 * Params of the agent's first notification.
 */
export type HelloParams = { manifest: Manifest };

/**
 * Params of a `value` notification.
 */
export type ValueParams = { sub: SubId; value: Json };

/**
 * Params of the editor-channel `session` notification (= the hub's HubSession; also sent to the
 * agent right after its hello, R6).
 */
export type SessionParams = {
  id: string;
  game: string;
  open: boolean;
  reason?: "bye" | "game_reloaded";
  /** The computer's engine fingerprint id; on the agent's copy of the answer to its hello only. */
  engine?: string;
};

/**
 * Params of the editor-channel `sessions` notification.
 */
export type SessionsParams = { list: SessionInfo[] };

/**
 * Params of the files-channel `list` request.
 */
export type ListParams = { dir: string };

/**
 * Params of the files-channel `read` and `readBinary` requests.
 */
export type PathParams = { path: string };

/**
 * Params of the files-channel `write` request.
 */
export type WriteParams = { path: string; text: string; version?: string };

/**
 * Params of the files-channel `writeBinary` request (`data` is a data URL, R1).
 */
export type WriteBinaryParams = { path: string; data: string };

/**
 * Params of the files-channel `find` request: one project-index key.
 */
export type FindParams = { key: string };

/**
 * A graph node by flow and node name: the `node:<flow>/<node>` key of the project index.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // filesView's Used by card lists the nodes a file defines.
 * const ref: NodeRef = { flow: "board", node: "merge" }; // node:board/merge
 * ```
 */
export type NodeRef = { readonly flow: string; readonly node: string };

/**
 * One game session the way a tools client sees it: the five R1 fields, the hub's liveness readout
 * once the game has sent a heartbeat (M4), and the hash of the session's command doors (D-37).
 * Old clients ignore `heartbeat` and `manifestHash`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // A paused game in the editor pane, as moku_sessions lists it.
 * const info: SessionInfo = {
 *   id: "s-7f3a",
 *   game: "merge-game 0.0.0",
 *   page: "http://127.0.0.1:3000/",
 *   embedded: true,
 *   connectedAt: 1790000000000,
 *   heartbeat: { frame: 1840, paused: true, silent: false },
 *   manifestHash: "4f528e73"
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type SessionInfo = {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly game: string;
  readonly page: string;
  readonly embedded: boolean;
  /** Epoch ms. */
  readonly connectedAt: number;
  /**
   * Frame and paused of the last heartbeat, and the hub's silent flag. Absent before the first
   * heartbeat. The hub re-sends the list when paused or silent flips, not on every frame.
   */
  readonly heartbeat?: {
    readonly frame: number;
    readonly paused: boolean;
    readonly silent: boolean;
  };
  /**
   * `commandsHash` of the session's manifest, set by the hub on hello. The MCP bridge compares it
   * to rebuild its door tools only when the commands change. Absent from an old hub.
   */
  readonly manifestHash?: string;
  /** The phone of a device session (a `role=device` agent); absent for a browser session. */
  readonly device?: SessionDevice;
};

/**
 * One child of a folder in the files channel.
 */
export type FileEntry = {
  readonly path: string;
  readonly kind: "file" | "dir";
  readonly size: number;
  readonly version?: string;
};

/**
 * A text file and its version (sha1 of the bytes).
 */
export type FileText = { readonly text: string; readonly version: string };

/**
 * An image read back in a data URL, with its version.
 */
export type FileBinary = { readonly dataUrl: string; readonly version: string };

/**
 * The result of a write.
 */
export type WriteResult = {
  readonly path: string;
  readonly bytes: number;
  readonly version: string;
};

/**
 * Where a project-index key is defined or used, without a line: the file and what in it holds the
 * key. Mirrors the game's `Anchor` (`@moku-labs/game/project`) field by field.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // node:board/merge, defined by the const `merge` of nodes/merge.ts.
 * const anchor: ProjectAnchor = { path: "nodes/merge.ts", binding: "merge" };
 * ```
 */
export type ProjectAnchor = {
  /** The file, root-relative POSIX. */
  readonly path: string;
  /** The const, function or export the definition is bound to. */
  readonly binding?: string;
  /** The property or attribute key: a text style key, the `name` of a projection, a JSX key. */
  readonly key?: string;
  /**
   * JSX: the component a key-carrying prop sits on, or the component a `{id}` or `{amountKey}`
   * pattern is written in.
   */
  readonly component?: string;
  /** JSX only: how the key is written. */
  readonly kind?: "literal" | "template" | "idProp" | "ident";
  /** JSX templates and identifiers: the literal head of the pattern, `card` for `card*Picture`. */
  readonly stem?: string;
  /** JSX idProp: the prop the value sits on, `id` or `amountKey`. */
  readonly prop?: string;
};

/**
 * One answer of the files-channel `find`: the anchor with its line read from disk at the call.
 * Mirrors the game's `Found`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // The JSX key settingsBoard: the line of its attribute, the whole element as the range.
 * const found: ProjectFound = {
 *   path: "features/settings/settings.tsx",
 *   key: "settingsBoard",
 *   component: "Signboard",
 *   kind: "idProp",
 *   prop: "id",
 *   line: 290,
 *   range: [289, 7, 310, 19],
 *   hash: "0f3c9a…"
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type ProjectFound = ProjectAnchor & {
  /** The line, 1-based. */
  readonly line: number;
  /** Start line, start column, end line, end column; 1-based, the end column exclusive. */
  readonly range: readonly [
    startLine: number,
    startColumn: number,
    endLine: number,
    endColumn: number
  ];
  /** sha1 hex of the bytes the line was read from; equals the files `version` of those bytes. */
  readonly hash: string;
  /** The file does not parse now; the line comes from its last good parse. Write no style edit. */
  readonly broken?: true;
};

/**
 * A project-index key that left one file for another in one watch batch.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const move: ProjectMove = {
 *   key: "node:board/catchUp",
 *   from: "nodes/catch-up.ts",
 *   to: "nodes/board/catch-up.ts"
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type ProjectMove = { readonly key: string; readonly from: string; readonly to: string };

/**
 * What one watch batch of the project index changed. The game's `ProjectChange` without its
 * `revision`, which `ProjectState` carries.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // An agent moved nodes/catch-up.ts into nodes/board/ and fixed the import of the board flow.
 * const change: ProjectChange = {
 *   files: ["flows/board.ts", "nodes/board/catch-up.ts", "nodes/catch-up.ts"],
 *   moved: [{ key: "node:board/catchUp", from: "nodes/catch-up.ts", to: "nodes/board/catch-up.ts" }],
 *   removed: []
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type ProjectChange = {
  /** The root-relative paths whose bytes changed, appeared or vanished, sorted. */
  readonly files: readonly string[];
  readonly moved: readonly ProjectMove[];
  /** Keys gone from every file. */
  readonly removed: readonly string[];
};

/**
 * The project index as the server publishes it (`editor.project`): `off` with the reason, or
 * `on` with the key → path maps. JSX keys never ride the state; only `find` reaches them.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const off: ProjectState = { state: "off", reason: "disabled" };
 * const on: ProjectState = {
 *   state: "on",
 *   revision: "9c1e…",
 *   manifest: "manifest.json",
 *   defs: { "flow:board": ["flows/board.ts"], "node:board/merge": ["nodes/merge.ts"] },
 *   uses: { "node:board/merge": ["flows/board.ts"] },
 *   broken: {}
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type ProjectState =
  | { readonly state: "off"; readonly reason: string }
  | {
      readonly state: "on";
      readonly revision: string;
      /** Revision before this batch; absent on the first state after open. */
      readonly previous?: string;
      /** The asset manifest, root-relative, when that file exists. */
      readonly manifest?: string;
      /** Every key except `jsx:` → its def paths, in def order (a conflict lists both). */
      readonly defs: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>;
      /** `node:` and `style:` keys that have uses → the paths of the uses. */
      readonly uses: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>;
      /** Broken files → the first parse error (`<path>:<line>:<col> <message>`). */
      readonly broken: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
      /** What the batch behind this state changed; absent on the first state after open. */
      readonly change?: ProjectChange;
    };

/**
 * What a view drops when a new project state arrives: `all` after a revision gap (reconnect, the
 * first state, off), otherwise the files, moves and removed keys of the batch.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const delta: ProjectDelta = { all: false, files: ["nodes/merge.ts"], moved: [], removed: [] };
 * ```
 */
export type ProjectDelta = {
  readonly all: boolean;
  readonly files: readonly string[];
  readonly moved: readonly ProjectMove[];
  readonly removed: readonly string[];
};

/**
 * Body of `GET {path}/hello`. The socket URL is `{path}/ws?token=<t>&kind=agent|tools` (R1); `ws`
 * carries it without the query.
 */
export type HelloBody = { readonly ws: string; readonly token: string };

/**
 * The JSON of `#moku-editor-boot` in the tools page (R1, R3).
 */
export type ToolsBoot = {
  readonly v: 1;
  /** Socket URL without the query. */
  readonly ws: string;
  readonly token: string;
  /** The hub path, e.g. "/__editor". */
  readonly path: string;
  readonly title: string;
  /** "Open in editor" template, unexpanded. */
  readonly editorUrl: string;
  /** Absolute real project root. */
  readonly root: string;
  /** Same-origin URL of the game page. */
  readonly gameUrl: string;
};

/**
 * The hot reload state of the game server (R6): Bun HMR on or off, and who owns the server. The
 * hub sends it to every tools page as the editor-channel notification `hotReload`, and again
 * after each tools connection opens.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const state: HotReload = { hmr: true, owner: "bin" };
 * ```
 */
export type HotReload = {
  /** True when Bun reloads the game page on a source change. */
  readonly hmr: boolean;
  /** "bin" when the moku-editor bin serves the game, "server" for a game's own Bun.serve. */
  readonly owner: "bin" | "server";
};

/**
 * A selected element: a ui element by its path, or a world entity by id. The same shape as the
 * scene's `ElementRef` (panels/shared/scene), declared here so the wire module imports nothing.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const ref: SelectionRef = { kind: "ui", path: "column#0/hudRow/coins" };
 * ```
 */
export type SelectionRef =
  | { readonly kind: "ui"; readonly path: string }
  | { readonly kind: "entity"; readonly id: number };

/**
 * A rect in CSS px of the game page (the iframe viewport). The same shape as the scene's `PageRect`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const rect: SelectionRect = { x: 12, y: 40, w: 96, h: 24 };
 * ```
 */
export type SelectionRect = {
  readonly x: number;
  readonly y: number;
  readonly w: number;
  readonly h: number;
};

/**
 * One element of an area selection (U9): the group roots that lie in the area, in page order.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const item: SelectionItem = {
 *   ref: { kind: "ui", path: "column#0/hudRow/coins" },
 *   key: "coins",
 *   name: "coins",
 *   type: "text",
 *   rect: { x: 12, y: 40, w: 96, h: 24 },
 *   source: { path: "src/ui/hud.ts", line: 42 }
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type SelectionItem = {
  readonly ref: SelectionRef;
  /** The ui node's `key`, when it has one. */
  readonly key?: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly type: string;
  /** Where it is drawn, in page CSS px. Absent: not placed. */
  readonly rect?: SelectionRect;
  /** The style source line of the element, once found. */
  readonly source?: { readonly path: string; readonly line: number };
};

/**
 * The value of one style property a pending edit carries (U8): a number, a string or a boolean.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const width: StyleValue = 600;
 * const justify: StyleValue = "center";
 * ```
 */
export type StyleValue = number | string | boolean;

/**
 * One pending style edit of an element (U8): a value the person changed in the Element tab and
 * the file does not have yet. `path` is the style property, dotted for a nested one
 * (`padding.top`); `from` is the value the scene had, `to` the wanted one.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // homePlay (features/stage/views/home-screen.tsx:199) is to become 600 wide, with more room on top.
 * const width: StyleEdit = { path: "minWidth", from: 556, to: 600 };
 * const top: StyleEdit = { path: "padding.top", from: 25, to: 30 };
 * ```
 */
export type StyleEdit = {
  readonly path: string;
  readonly from: StyleValue;
  readonly to: StyleValue;
};

/**
 * The element selected in the editor page, as the page publishes it (editor-channel notification
 * `selection`) and as the hub answers `editor.selection` and `editor.select`. Check a received
 * value with `parseSelectionInfo`. Its readonly `items` make it not assignable to the mutable
 * Json: senders pass it through `toWireValue`, like a Manifest.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // The picker landed on the coins label; the card and the crop are written.
 * const info: SelectionInfo = {
 *   ref: { kind: "ui", path: "column#0/hudRow/coins" },
 *   key: "coins",
 *   projection: "hud",
 *   name: "coins",
 *   type: "text",
 *   rect: { x: 12, y: 40, w: 96, h: 24 },
 *   source: { path: "src/ui/hud.ts", line: 42 },
 *   card: ".moku/captures/2026-10-05/coins-f1840.md",
 *   crop: ".moku/captures/2026-10-05/coins-f1840-crop.jpg",
 *   line: "@moku coins text · src/ui/hud.ts:42 · .moku/captures/2026-10-05/coins-f1840.md",
 *   session: "s-7f3a",
 *   frame: 1840,
 *   at: 1790000000000
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type SelectionInfo = {
  readonly ref: SelectionRef;
  /** The ui node's `key`, when it has one. */
  readonly key?: string;
  /** The projection the element belongs to, e.g. "hud". */
  readonly projection?: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly type: string;
  /** Where it is drawn, in page CSS px (as `SceneNode.rect`). Absent: not placed. */
  readonly rect?: SelectionRect;
  /** The style source line of the element, once found. */
  readonly source?: { readonly path: string; readonly line: number };
  /** The capture card, project-relative under `capturesDir`. Set after a pick. */
  readonly card?: string;
  /** The element crop picture, project-relative under `capturesDir`. Set after a pick. */
  readonly crop?: string;
  /** The one-line `@moku …` reference of the element. */
  readonly line?: string;
  /** The game session the element belongs to. */
  readonly session?: string;
  /** The scene frame; after a pick the frame of the pick. */
  readonly frame?: number;
  /**
   * The area of an area selection (U9), in page CSS px. An area selection has `type: "area"`,
   * `name: "area"`, `rect` = the area and `ref` = the first item's ref (`{ kind: "ui", path: "" }`
   * when no element is inside).
   */
  readonly area?: SelectionRect;
  /** The elements of an area selection, top to bottom then left to right; at most 40. */
  readonly items?: readonly SelectionItem[];
  /**
   * The pending style edits of the element (U8). Absent when it has none: `parseSelectionInfo`
   * drops an empty list.
   *
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The agent read the selection of homePlay: two edits to write in home-screen.tsx:199.
   * const lines = (info.edits ?? []).map(edit => `${edit.path}: ${edit.from} -> ${edit.to}`);
   * // ["minWidth: 556 -> 600", "padding.top: 25 -> 30"]
   * ```
   */
  readonly edits?: readonly StyleEdit[];
  /** Epoch ms of the publish (`Date.now()`). */
  readonly at: number;
};

/**
 * The value of each method `publish` sends to the tools pages (A5): the hub keeps the last one
 * per method and replays it to every tools connection that opens. `devices` and `deviceTelemetry`
 * are connect's (spec 11 § 5.4): the device directory and the wired telemetry of a watched phone.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const kept: PublishParams = {
 *   hotReload: { hmr: true, owner: "bin" },
 *   selection: null,
 *   project: { state: "off", reason: "not opened" },
 *   engine: { id: "0.14.12+9c41e0", version: "0.14.12", dist: "9c41e0…" }
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type PublishParams = {
  readonly hotReload: HotReload;
  /** `null`: nothing is selected. */
  readonly selection: SelectionInfo | null;
  /** The project index of the files root (`files:project`). */
  readonly project: ProjectState;
  /** The engine of the computer's project (`files.engine()`), as `editor.engine`. */
  readonly engine: EngineInfo;
  /** connect's device directory, as `editor.devices`. */
  readonly devices: DeviceDirectory;
  /** The newest wired telemetry record of a watched phone, as `editor.deviceTelemetry`. */
  readonly deviceTelemetry: DeviceTelemetry;
};

/**
 * A method `publish` sends to the tools pages (R6): `"hotReload"`, `"selection"`, `"project"`,
 * `"engine"`, `"devices"` or `"deviceTelemetry"`.
 */
export type PublishMethod = keyof PublishParams;

/**
 * The format a picture travels in on the wire (editor.capture, editor.sheet, a crop): `"jpeg"`
 * (the default, D-34) or `"png"` (lossless).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const format: PictureFormat = "jpeg";
 * ```
 */
export type PictureFormat = "jpeg" | "png";

/**
 * Params of the editor-channel request `select`: an area by `rect`, the element by `key` (a ui
 * node key, projection-qualified like `"hud/infoBar"` allowed) or by `ref`. `rect` wins over `key`
 * and `ref`. `card` (the page treats absent
 * as true) asks for the capture card and the crop as after a picker click.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const params: SelectParams = { key: "hud/infoBar", card: true };
 * const areaParams: SelectParams = { rect: { x: 0, y: 30, w: 200, h: 60 } }; // every element inside
 * ```
 */
export type SelectParams = {
  readonly key?: string;
  readonly ref?: SelectionRef;
  /** An area in page CSS px, picked like an area drag of the picker (U9). It wins over key and ref. */
  readonly rect?: SelectionRect;
  readonly card?: boolean;
};

/**
 * The editor-channel notifications by method, with their params. `session` goes to agents and
 * tools, the rest to tools connections. `selection` is also sent by the editor page (a tools
 * connection with `role=page`) to the hub.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const note: EditorNotifications["selection"] = null; // nothing is selected
 * ```
 */
export type EditorNotifications = {
  readonly session: SessionParams;
  readonly sessions: SessionsParams;
} & PublishParams;

/**
 * The name of an editor-channel notification.
 */
export type EditorNotificationMethod = keyof EditorNotifications;

/**
 * A workspace of the tools page rail. The same members as workspace's `WorkspaceId`, declared here
 * so the wire module imports nothing; `WORKSPACE_NAMES` is the list at runtime.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const name: WorkspaceName = "state";
 * ```
 */
export type WorkspaceName = "flow" | "game" | "render" | "state" | "files" | "console";

/**
 * Params of the editor-channel request `device`: the preset by id, the orientation and, for a
 * foldable, whether it is folded. Every field is optional; empty params read the device and change
 * nothing. Check received params with `parseDeviceParams`. The page answers -32602 for a preset id
 * it does not know.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const read: DeviceParams = {};
 * const turn: DeviceParams = { preset: "pixel-8", orientation: "landscape" };
 * const open: DeviceParams = { preset: "galaxy-z-fold-6", folded: false }; // the inner screen
 * ```
 */
export type DeviceParams = {
  /** A preset id, e.g. `"pixel-8"`. */
  readonly preset?: string;
  readonly orientation?: Orientation;
  /** `false` shows the inner screen of a foldable. */
  readonly folded?: boolean;
};

/**
 * One device preset in a `DeviceInfo`: a row of `DeviceSpec` with the same `id`, `name`, `group`
 * and `kind`, and the cover-screen `w` and `h` in portrait.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const row: DevicePresetInfo = {
 *   id: "galaxy-z-fold-6", name: "Galaxy Z Fold 6", group: "foldable", kind: "phone",
 *   w: 369, h: 968, foldable: true
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type DevicePresetInfo = {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly group: DeviceSpec["group"];
  readonly kind: DeviceSpec["kind"];
  readonly w: number;
  readonly h: number;
  /** True when the spec has two screens (`DeviceSpec.fold`). */
  readonly foldable: boolean;
};

/**
 * The answer of the editor-channel request `device`: the device of the game viewer after the
 * change, and every preset a next request can name. Check a received answer with `parseDeviceInfo`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // After `device { preset: "pixel-8", orientation: "landscape" }`.
 * const info: DeviceInfo = {
 *   preset: "pixel-8",
 *   orientation: "landscape",
 *   folded: true,
 *   w: 915,
 *   h: 412,
 *   presets: [
 *     { id: "pixel-8", name: "Pixel 8", group: "android", kind: "phone", w: 412, h: 915, foldable: false }
 *   ]
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type DeviceInfo = {
  readonly preset: string;
  readonly orientation: Orientation;
  /** Always `true` for a preset that is not foldable. */
  readonly folded: boolean;
  /** The width of the game viewport after the change, CSS px, orientation applied. */
  readonly w: number;
  /** The height of the game viewport after the change, CSS px, orientation applied. */
  readonly h: number;
  readonly presets: readonly DevicePresetInfo[];
};

/**
 * Params of the editor-channel request `show`: the workspace to activate. Empty params read the
 * active workspace and change nothing. Check received params with `parseShowParams`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const read: ShowParams = {};
 * const open: ShowParams = { workspace: "state" };
 * ```
 */
export type ShowParams = {
  readonly workspace?: WorkspaceName;
};

/**
 * The answer of the editor-channel request `show`: the active workspace after the change, and the
 * workspaces a next request can name. Check a received answer with `parseShowInfo`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const info: ShowInfo = { workspace: "state", workspaces: WORKSPACE_NAMES };
 * ```
 */
export type ShowInfo = {
  readonly workspace: WorkspaceName;
  readonly workspaces: readonly WorkspaceName[];
};

/**
 * Params of the editor-channel request `node`: the graph node the Flow view focuses, by its id of
 * 1 to 256 chars. Check received params with `parseNodeParams`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const params: NodeParams = { id: "main/home" };
 * ```
 */
export type NodeParams = {
  readonly id: string;
};

/**
 * The answer of the editor-channel request `node`: the asked node id and the item key the Flow
 * view focused. Check a received answer with `parseNodeInfo`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const info: NodeInfo = { id: "main/home", selected: "main/home" };
 * ```
 */
export type NodeInfo = {
  readonly id: string;
  /** The item key the Flow view focused, e.g. `"main/board>board/merge"` inside a sub-flow. */
  readonly selected: string;
};

/**
 * The editor-channel requests by method: `selection` (answered by the hub with the last published
 * selection), and the four the hub relays to the editor page (`RelayedEditorMethod`): `select`
 * answers the selection, `device` the device of the game viewer, `show` the active workspace and
 * `node` the focused graph node.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const answer: EditorRequests["select"]["result"] = info; // the element after the select
 * const turn: EditorRequests["device"]["params"] = { orientation: "landscape" };
 * ```
 */
export type EditorRequests = {
  readonly selection: {
    readonly params: Readonly<Record<string, never>>;
    readonly result: SelectionInfo | null;
  };
  readonly select: { readonly params: SelectParams; readonly result: SelectionInfo };
  readonly device: { readonly params: DeviceParams; readonly result: DeviceInfo };
  readonly show: { readonly params: ShowParams; readonly result: ShowInfo };
  readonly node: { readonly params: NodeParams; readonly result: NodeInfo };
};

/**
 * The name of an editor-channel request.
 */
export type EditorRequestMethod = keyof EditorRequests;

/**
 * An editor-channel request the hub relays to the editor page and answers with the page's answer.
 * `selection` is not one: the hub answers it itself.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const relayed: RelayedEditorMethod[] = ["select", "device", "show", "node"];
 * ```
 */
export type RelayedEditorMethod = Extract<
  EditorRequestMethod,
  "select" | "device" | "show" | "node"
>;

/**
 * The size and corner radius of one screen of a foldable device, in CSS px.
 */
export type FoldScreen = { readonly w: number; readonly h: number; readonly radius: number };

/**
 * A device preset of the tools page (R1, R4): the screen in CSS px, its pixel ratio, safe insets,
 * corner radius, the `<optgroup>` it is listed under and the frame drawn around it (R9). A foldable
 * adds its two screens; its top-level size is the cover screen.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const iphone15: DeviceSpec = {
 *   id: "iphone-15", name: "iPhone 15", w: 393, h: 852, safeTop: 59, safeBottom: 34, kind: "phone",
 *   dpr: 3, radius: 55, group: "iphone", frame: "modern"
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type DeviceSpec = {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly w: number;
  readonly h: number;
  readonly safeTop: number;
  readonly safeBottom: number;
  readonly kind: "phone" | "tablet" | "desktop";
  /** Device pixel ratio of the screen. */
  readonly dpr: number;
  /** Corner radius of the screen in CSS px (0 for a desktop). */
  readonly radius: number;
  /** The `<optgroup>` the preset is listed under. */
  readonly group: "iphone" | "android" | "foldable" | "tablet" | "desktop";
  /**
   * The frame drawn around the screen (R9): "modern" is the thin bezel every current device has;
   * "home-button" is the iPhone SE look, with 64 px bands above and below the screen and a round
   * home button in the bottom one.
   */
  readonly frame: "modern" | "home-button";
  /** Set when a value of the preset is an estimate, not a published figure. */
  readonly approx?: true;
  /** The two screens of a foldable: folded (cover) and unfolded (inner). */
  readonly fold?: { readonly cover: FoldScreen; readonly inner: FoldScreen };
};

/**
 * The twenty-one device presets (round 2 R4, round 2b R10), in display order.
 */
export type DevicePresetId =
  | "iphone-se"
  | "iphone-15"
  | "iphone-17e"
  | "iphone-air"
  | "iphone-18-pro"
  | "iphone-18-pro-max"
  | "iphone-15-pro-max"
  | "iphone-16-pro"
  | "iphone-16-pro-max"
  | "galaxy-s24"
  | "galaxy-a55"
  | "redmi-note-13"
  | "pixel-8"
  | "xperia-1-v"
  | "galaxy-z-fold-6"
  | "galaxy-z-flip-6"
  | "pixel-9-pro-fold"
  | "iphone-duo"
  | "ipad-mini"
  | "ipad-air-11"
  | "desktop";

/**
 * Device orientation.
 */
export type Orientation = "portrait" | "landscape";

/**
 * Size and safe insets of a preset in an orientation (resolveDevice, R8).
 */
export type DeviceSize = {
  w: number;
  h: number;
  safe: { top: number; right: number; bottom: number; left: number };
};
~~~

### The device link (`src/plugins/hub/protocol/device-link.ts`, verbatim)

The runtime-free device-link module of the hub, owned by the hub and imported by the bridge, the overlay, connect and the collector as `../hub/protocol` (never the hub index). `baseAppId` strips one trailing `.debug`, so connect and the collector compare a native debug install's app id with the store app's. It imports nothing: no plugin, no kernel, no `node:` module, no Bun global, not `registry/protocol` (it declares its own `LinkJson`). The functions are shown with their signatures.

~~~ts
/**
 * A JSON value on the device link: the same set of values as registry/protocol's `Json`, declared
 * here so hub/protocol imports nothing (no registry/protocol ↔ hub/protocol cycle). The two are
 * assignable both ways.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const line: LinkJson = { v: 1, kind: "mark", t: 5917.4, label: "boss", auto: false };
 * ```
 */
export type LinkJson = null | boolean | number | string | LinkJson[] | { [key: string]: LinkJson };

/**
 * How a device reached the hub: through adb reverse on 127.0.0.1, or over the LAN.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const link: DeviceLinkKind = "adb";
 * ```
 */
export type DeviceLinkKind = "adb" | "lan";

/**
 * The WebSocket close code of a device upgrade whose device id or token the hub does not know: the
 * socket is upgraded and closed at once, and the phone pairs again.
 */
export const DEVICE_UNPAIRED_CODE = 4401;

/**
 * The WebSocket close reason that goes with `DEVICE_UNPAIRED_CODE`.
 */
export const DEVICE_UNPAIRED_REASON = "unpaired";

/**
 * Params of the device→hub editor-channel notification `pair`: the code the phone shows, and what
 * it is.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const pair: PairParams = { code: "4821", device: { model: "SM-A266B", os: "Android 15", engine: "0.15.1+2b7c11", appId: "com.mokulabs.timber.debug" } };
 * ```
 */
export type PairParams = {
  /** Exactly 4 digits, e.g. "4821", "0421". */
  readonly code: string;
  readonly device: {
    /** The phone's model, e.g. "SM-A266B" (normalized by the hub). */
    readonly model?: string;
    /** The phone's system, e.g. "Android 15". */
    readonly os?: string;
    /** The phone's `__MOKU_GAME_ENGINE__`, e.g. "0.14.12+9c41e0". */
    readonly engine?: string;
    /** The phone's `__MOKU_GAME_BUILD__`, e.g. "debug-20261014T160000Z". */
    readonly build?: string;
    /**
     * The app id of the build (`__MOKU_GAME_APP__`, the PerfLog header's `app.id`), e.g.
     * "com.mokulabs.timber.debug": the bundle identifier, with the `.debug` suffix of a native debug
     * install. Absent on an engine that writes none (0.15.0).
     */
    readonly appId?: string;
  };
};

/**
 * Params of the hub→device editor-channel notification `paired`: the device id and token to
 * reconnect with, and the computer's engine fingerprint.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const paired: PairedParams = { device: "d-7f3a", token: "9f2c…", engine: "0.14.12+9c41e0" };
 * ```
 */
export type PairedParams = {
  readonly device: string;
  readonly token: string;
  readonly engine: string;
};

/**
 * Params of the device→hub editor-channel notification `perf.lines`: a batch of the device's log.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const batch: PerfLinesParams = {
 *   log: "perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl",
 *   from: 0,
 *   lines: [{ v: 1, kind: "mark", t: 5917.4, build: null, label: "boss", auto: false }]
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfLinesParams = {
  /** The device log's name, e.g. "perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl". */
  readonly log: string;
  /** Index of `lines[0]` in that log, 0-based. */
  readonly from: number;
  /** PerfLogLine v1 objects, JSON objects on the wire. */
  readonly lines: readonly LinkJson[];
};

/**
 * Params of the hub→device editor-channel notification `perf.ack`: the next index the hub expects
 * of a log, and how many lines of the batch it took.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const ack: PerfAckParams = { log: "perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl", next: 200, n: 200 };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfAckParams = { readonly log: string; readonly next: number; readonly n: number };

/**
 * The engine of the computer (engine spec 10 E1 without `folder`), published to tools as
 * `editor.engine`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const engine: EngineInfo = { id: "0.14.12+9c41e0", version: "0.14.12", dist: "9c41e0…" };
 * ```
 */
export type EngineInfo = {
  /** "0.14.12+9c41e0", "0.0.0+src" or "unknown". */
  readonly id: string;
  readonly version: string;
  readonly dist: string;
  readonly patch?: { readonly file: string; readonly hash: string };
};

/**
 * A device session's device, on `SessionInfo.device`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const device: SessionDevice = {
 *   id: "d-7f3a", model: "SM-A266B", link: "adb", address: "127.0.0.1", port: 47600,
 *   engine: "0.14.12+9c41e0", build: "debug-20261014T160000Z"
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type SessionDevice = {
  /** The device id the hub issued, e.g. "d-7f3a". */
  readonly id: string;
  /** The normalized model, e.g. "SM-A266B". */
  readonly model: string | null;
  readonly link: DeviceLinkKind;
  /** The phone's address as the hub saw it: "127.0.0.1" (adb), "192.168.1.23" (LAN). */
  readonly address: string;
  /** The port of the device listener it reached, e.g. 47600. */
  readonly port: number;
  readonly engine: string | null;
  readonly build: string | null;
  /**
   * The app id the phone named in its pair, e.g. "com.mokulabs.timber.debug" (compare with
   * `baseAppId`); absent when it named none (an engine before the app id).
   */
  readonly appId?: string;
};

/**
 * The device link of the bridge: what the overlay's Link tab and the pill's link light show.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const live: DeviceLink = { mode: "adb", address: "127.0.0.1:47600", editorEngine: "0.14.12+9c41e0", seenAt: 1760454000000 };
 * ```
 */
export type DeviceLink = {
  /**
   * "none": no computer reached (lost, retrying quietly, or refused); "connecting": a socket opening
   * or pairing; "adb": open at a loopback address (adb reverse); "lan": open at any other address.
   */
  readonly mode: "none" | "connecting" | "adb" | "lan";
  /** The `host:port` dialled. */
  readonly address: string;
  /** Present while the computer has not confirmed this phone: the code the person types on the computer. */
  readonly pairing?: { readonly code: string };
  /** The computer's engine fingerprint; absent before the first session or paired notification. */
  readonly editorEngine?: string;
  /** Epoch ms of the last sign of the computer; absent before the first one. */
  readonly seenAt?: number;
};

/**
 * Normalizes a device model the engine's way: control and bidi characters dropped (whitespace
 * controls such as adb's trailing newline count as whitespace), trimmed, whitespace runs to "-",
 * upper case, at most 64 characters; an empty or non-string value gives null. The hub, the
 * collector's adb reading and the phone's log header agree through it.
 *
 * @param raw - The model as a phone, the shell or adb reported it.
 * @returns The model, or null.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * normalizeModel(" sm a266b "); // "SM-A266B"
 * ```
 */
export function normalizeModel(raw: unknown): string | null;

/**
 * The app id without a trailing `.debug`: a native debug install's id
 * ("com.mokulabs.timber.debug") names the same app as the project's ("com.mokulabs.timber"). The
 * collector compares a log's app with `collector.appId` through it, connect a phone's processes
 * with a linked device's app.
 *
 * @param appId - An app id (bundle identifier or Android package).
 * @returns The id without one trailing ".debug".
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * baseAppId("com.mokulabs.timber.debug"); // "com.mokulabs.timber"
 * baseAppId("com.mokulabs.timber"); // "com.mokulabs.timber"
 * ```
 */
export function baseAppId(appId: string): string;

/**
 * Checks the params of a `pair` notification: an object whose code is exactly four digits and
 * whose `device` is an object. Of the device, only the string fields model, os, engine, build and
 * appId are kept; one of them over 128 characters or with a control or bidi character (C0, DEL, C1,
 * U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069) makes the pair malformed, so every reader (the terminal's
 * question, the logs, `SessionInfo.device`) gets clean text.
 *
 * @param params - The notification's params as they arrived.
 * @returns The params, or undefined when they are malformed.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * parsePairParams({ code: "0421", device: { model: "SM-A266B" } }); // { code: "0421", device: { model: "SM-A266B" } }
 * parsePairParams({ code: "48", device: {} }); // undefined
 * ```
 */
export function parsePairParams(params: LinkJson | undefined): PairParams | undefined;

/**
 * Checks the params of a `perf.lines` notification: `log` of 1–128 word characters, dots or
 * hyphens, `from` a safe integer ≥ 0, `lines` a list of 1–5000 items. The items themselves are
 * checked by the hub one by one.
 *
 * @param params - The notification's params as they arrived.
 * @returns The params, or undefined when they are malformed.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * parsePerfLinesParams({ log: "perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl", from: -1, lines: [] }); // undefined
 * ```
 */
export function parsePerfLinesParams(params: LinkJson | undefined): PerfLinesParams | undefined;

/**
 * Checks a `host:port` (a DNS name or an IPv4 literal) or `[ipv6]:port` address, trimmed, port
 * 1–65535, and normalizes it: the host lower-cased, the port without leading zeros.
 *
 * @param text - The address as typed or configured.
 * @returns The host (IPv6 without brackets), the port and the normalized text, or undefined.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * parseAddress(" 192.168.1.5:47600 ")?.text; // "192.168.1.5:47600"
 * parseAddress("[::1]:47600")?.host; // "::1"
 * parseAddress("192.168.1.5"); // undefined
 * ```
 */
export function parseAddress(
  text: string
): { readonly host: string; readonly port: number; readonly text: string } | undefined;

/**
 * Whether a host is the loopback: any address of 127.0.0.0/8, `localhost` or `::1`. A phone that
 * reaches the computer at such an address came through adb reverse.
 *
 * @param host - A host of `parseAddress`.
 * @returns Whether it is the loopback.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * isLoopback("127.0.0.2"); // true
 * isLoopback("192.168.1.5"); // false
 * ```
 */
export function isLoopback(host: string): boolean;
~~~

### The tools link (`src/plugins/hub/protocol/tools-link.ts`, verbatim)

Who sent a run through the hub. An agent whose `hello` names the capability `run-from` (`hello { manifest, caps: ["run-from"] }`, `capsOf` keeps the known names) gets every forwarded `run` as `StampedRunParams`: `from: "page"` for the editor page, `from: "mcp"` for the MCP bridge, with `client`, the MCP client's name the bridge sent once as the tools→hub notification `client { name }` (`clientNameOf`: control and bidi characters dropped, trimmed, at most 64 characters). A `from` or `client` the tools client wrote into its own params is never forwarded. The bridge turns `from` into the registry's `via` (`page` → `tools`, `mcp` → `mcp`, absent → `bridge`). Runtime-free, imported by the hub, the bridge and the MCP bridge.

~~~ts
/**
 * Who sent a run through the hub: the editor page (`"page"`) or a plain tools client, the MCP bridge
 * of an agent (`"mcp"`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const from: RunFrom = "mcp"; // the bridge turns it into the registry's via "mcp"
 * ```
 */
export type RunFrom = "page" | "mcp";

/**
 * The method of the tools→hub editor-channel notification that names the MCP client.
 */
export const CLIENT_METHOD = "client";

/**
 * Params of the tools→hub editor-channel notification `client`: the MCP client's name, as its
 * `initialize` gave it (`clientInfo.name`). The hub takes it from a plain tools connection only.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const params: ClientParams = { name: "Claude Code" };
 * ```
 */
export type ClientParams = { readonly name: string };

/**
 * The params of a `run` the hub forwards to an agent: the tools client's `id` and `input`, and the
 * hub's own `from` and, with `from: "mcp"` and a known name, `client`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const params: StampedRunParams = { id: "editor.record", input: { on: true }, from: "mcp", client: "Claude Code" };
 * ```
 */
export type StampedRunParams = {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly input?: LinkJson;
  readonly from: RunFrom;
  /** The MCP client's name, cleaned by `clientNameOf`; only with `from: "mcp"`. */
  readonly client?: string;
};

/**
 * The capability an agent names in its `hello` when its bridge reads a stamped run (`from`,
 * `client`, spec 07 B1). Without it the hub forwards a run as `{ id, input }`.
 */
export const RUN_FROM_CAP = "run-from";

/**
 * A capability an agent can name in its `hello`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const cap: AgentCap = "run-from";
 * ```
 */
export type AgentCap = typeof RUN_FROM_CAP;

/**
 * What an agent adds to its `hello { manifest }` params to say what it understands. Older agents
 * send none; the hub ignores a name it does not know.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const extra: HelloCaps = { caps: ["run-from"] }; // the bridge's hello: { manifest, caps: ["run-from"] }
 * ```
 */
export type HelloCaps = { readonly caps?: readonly AgentCap[] };

/**
 * The known capabilities of a hello's `caps`, each once, in order; names the hub does not know, an
 * entry that is no string and a value that is no list are ignored.
 *
 * @param raw - The `caps` of a hello, as it arrived.
 * @returns The capabilities.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * capsOf(["sections", "run-from"]); // ["run-from"]
 * capsOf(undefined); // []
 * ```
 */
export function capsOf(raw: unknown): readonly AgentCap[];
