/**
 * The longest client name, in characters (code points).
 */
export const MAX_CLIENT_NAME = 64;

/**
 * Cleans an MCP client's name: control and bidi characters dropped, trimmed, cut to 64 characters
 * (code points, so a character is never split); an empty result or a value that is no string gives
 * undefined.
 *
 * @param raw - The `name` of a `client` notification, as it arrived.
 * @returns The clean name, or undefined.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * clientNameOf(" Claude\nCode "); // "ClaudeCode"
 * clientNameOf("\n"); // undefined
 * ```
 */
export function clientNameOf(raw: unknown): string | undefined;
~~~

### The connect module (`src/plugins/connect/protocol/`, verbatim)

The runtime-free wire module of the server's `connect` plugin: the published `editor.devices` (`DeviceDirectory`) and `editor.deviceTelemetry` (`DeviceTelemetry`), the listen addresses connect's editor methods answer (`ListenInfo`), and their guards. link checks every published value with `readDirectory` / `readTelemetry` (a malformed value is the warn `link:bad-published` and keeps the held one); activeSource and renderView import the types only. It imports nothing outside its folder. Every reading is a `Reading<T>`: `{ available: true, source, value }` or `{ available: false, source, reason }`, never a 0 for a value that was not read.

`types.ts`:

~~~ts
/**
 * Why a reading is not available: not by wire, an iPhone, a node SELinux hides, a file adb could not
 * read, a format the parser does not know, a process or node not found, two candidates, no WebView
 * devtools socket, no CDP target for the session's page, the first tick of a CPU delta, adb missing,
 * or another failure.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const reason: ReadingOffReason = "no-devtools-socket"; // a release build: WebView debugging is off
 * ```
 */
export type ReadingOffReason =
  | "not-wired"
  | "ios"
  | "no-permission"
  | "unreadable"
  | "unknown-format"
  | "not-found"
  | "ambiguous"
  | "no-devtools-socket"
  | "no-target"
  | "warming-up"
  | "adb-missing"
  | "error";

/**
 * A reading that may be unavailable; every reading names where it came from (`"/sys/kernel/gpu"`,
 * `"/proc/<pid>/stat"`, `"dumpsys meminfo"`, `"cdp Runtime.getHeapUsage"`, `"none"` …). A reading that
 * is not available has no value.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const gpu: Reading<number> = { available: true, source: "/sys/kernel/gpu", value: 221 };
 * const off: Reading<number> = { available: false, source: "none", reason: "not-wired" };
 * ```
 */
export type Reading<T> =
  | { readonly available: true; readonly source: string; readonly value: T }
  | { readonly available: false; readonly source: string; readonly reason: ReadingOffReason };

/**
 * Device mode's listen addresses as published: the device port, the adb listener and the LAN
 * listener (null while it is off). The hub's own `DeviceListen` is its API type; this is the wire
 * copy with the same fields.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const listen: ListenInfo = { port: 47600, adb: "127.0.0.1:47600", lan: "192.168.1.5:47600" };
 * ```
 */
export type ListenInfo = {
  readonly port: number;
  readonly adb: string;
  readonly lan: string | null;
};

/**
 * A phone `adb devices -l` lists, with its getprop facts and how far it got: unauthorized, offline,
 * ready (device mode off), waiting for its debug game, no agent answered, or linked to a device.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const phone: WireDevice = { serial: "R5CX30ABCDE", state: "device", transport: "usb", model: "SM-A266B",
 *   name: "Galaxy A26", os: "Android 15", phase: "linked", device: "d-7f3a" };
 * ```
 */
export type WireDevice = {
  /** "R5CX30ABCDE", "192.168.1.23:37011" or "adb-R5CX…._adb-tls-connect._tcp". */
  readonly serial: string;
  readonly state: "device" | "unauthorized" | "offline" | "other";
  /** "wifi" for an `ip:port` or `_adb-tls-connect` serial (Android 11+ wireless debugging). */
  readonly transport: "usb" | "wifi";
  /** The normalized model, "SM-A266B"; null before getprop answered. */
  readonly model: string | null;
  /** The marketing name when getprop has one, "Galaxy A26". */
  readonly name: string | null;
  /** "Android 15". */
  readonly os: string | null;
  readonly phase: "unauthorized" | "offline" | "ready" | "waiting" | "no-agent" | "linked";
  /** The matched linked device id, "d-7f3a"; null while none matched. */
  readonly device: string | null;
  /** Two linked phones of one model: no telemetry, the panel says which is ambiguous. */
  readonly match?: "ambiguous";
};

/**
 * A pairing waiting for the person at the computer. It carries no code: the person types the code the
 * phone shows, and connect compares it.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const ask: PairAsk = { ticket: "p-3a1f", model: "SM-A266B", address: "192.168.1.23", link: "lan",
 *   engine: "0.15.0+9c41e0", build: "debug-20261016T090000Z", since: 1791986083963 };
 * ```
 */
export type PairAsk = {
  /** "p-" and 4 hex characters. */
  readonly ticket: string;
  readonly model: string | null;
  /** The phone's address as the hub saw it, "192.168.1.23". */
  readonly address: string;
  readonly link: DeviceLinkKind;
  readonly engine: string | null;
  readonly build: string | null;
  /** Epoch ms of the request. */
  readonly since: number;
};

/**
 * A device linked in this device-mode run, as published (the hub's `devices()` without pairing
 * detail), with its open session.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const linked: LinkedEntry = { id: "d-7f3a", model: "SM-A266B", link: "adb", address: "127.0.0.1", online: true,
 *   engine: "0.15.0+9c41e0", build: "debug-20261016T090000Z", latencyMs: 9, session: "s-9" };
 * ```
 */
export type LinkedEntry = {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly model: string | null;
  readonly link: DeviceLinkKind;
  readonly address: string;
  readonly online: boolean;
  readonly engine: string | null;
  readonly build: string | null;
  /** The hub's WebSocket ping round trip, ms; null before the first pong. */
  readonly latencyMs: number | null;
  /** The device's open session id ("s-9"), the session whose `device.id` is this id; null while away. */
  readonly session: string | null;
};

/**
 * The device directory, published as `editor.devices`: device mode, where a LAN pairing is
 * confirmed, adb's availability, the phones adb lists, the pairings asking and the devices linked.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const directory: DeviceDirectory = { v: 1, mode: { on: true, owner: "connect", listen: { port: 47600, adb: "127.0.0.1:47600", lan: null } },
 *   confirmIn: "page", adb: { available: true }, wire: [], asking: [], linked: [], at: 1791986083963 };
 * ```
 */
export type DeviceDirectory = {
  readonly v: 1;
  readonly mode: {
    readonly on: boolean;
    /** "connect": the tools page turned device mode on; "other": `moku-editor perf` did. */
    readonly owner: "connect" | "other" | null;
    readonly listen: ListenInfo | null;
  };
  /** Where a LAN pairing is confirmed: the tools page, perf's terminal, or nowhere (device mode off). */
  readonly confirmIn: "page" | "terminal" | null;
  readonly adb: { readonly available: boolean; readonly reason?: "missing" | "error" };
  readonly wire: readonly WireDevice[];
  readonly asking: readonly PairAsk[];
  readonly linked: readonly LinkedEntry[];
  /** Epoch ms of the build of this directory. */
  readonly at: number;
};

/**
 * CPU of one process over the last tick: % of all cores and % of one core (top's style).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const app: ProcessCpu = { pid: 23811, name: "com.moku.garden", pct: 14.2, oneCorePct: 113.6 };
 * ```
 */
export type ProcessCpu = {
  readonly pid: number;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly pct: number;
  readonly oneCorePct: number;
};

/**
 * Memory of one process from `dumpsys meminfo` (every 5 s), MB: the whole process, never the JS heap.
 * A row the table did not have is null, never 0.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const app: ProcessMemory = { pid: 23811, totalPssMb: 541, javaMb: 18.2, nativeMb: 96.4, graphicsMb: 210.5, glMb: 180.1,
 *   codeMb: 61.3, stackMb: 1.2, otherMb: 22.4, systemMb: 31.9, at: 1791986080000 };
 * ```
 */
export type ProcessMemory = {
  readonly pid: number;
  readonly totalPssMb: number;
  readonly javaMb: number | null;
  readonly nativeMb: number | null;
  readonly graphicsMb: number | null;
  readonly glMb: number | null;
  readonly codeMb: number | null;
  readonly stackMb: number | null;
  readonly otherMb: number | null;
  readonly systemMb: number | null;
  /** Epoch ms of the reading. */
  readonly at: number;
};

/**
 * The GPU reading of a wired phone: clock and busy now, and the clock range (null when the node does
 * not say).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const gpu: GpuLoad = { mhz: 221, busyPct: 63, minMhz: 221, maxMhz: 949 };
 * ```
 */
export type GpuLoad = {
  readonly mhz: number | null;
  readonly busyPct: number | null;
  readonly minMhz: number | null;
  readonly maxMhz: number | null;
};

/**
 * One JS heap sample of the WebView over CDP (`Runtime.getHeapUsage`), `t` in computer epoch ms.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const sample: HeapSample = { t: 1791986083713, usedMb: 41.9, totalMb: 64 };
 * ```
 */
export type HeapSample = { readonly t: number; readonly usedMb: number; readonly totalMb: number };

/**
 * A GC: inferred from a heap drop of at least `gcDropMb` between two samples (`inferred: true`), or
 * exact from CDP Tracing (`gcTrace`), `t` in computer epoch ms.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const gc: HeapGc = { t: 1791986083713, freedMb: 26, inferred: true };
 * ```
 */
export type HeapGc = { readonly t: number; readonly freedMb: number; readonly inferred: boolean };

/**
 * One wired telemetry record of a watched device (1 Hz), published as `editor.deviceTelemetry` and
 * emitted as connect's `connect:telemetry`. Times are computer epoch ms. Every reading names its
 * source and degrades alone.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const record: DeviceTelemetry = { v: 1, device: "d-7f3a", serial: "R5CX30ABCDE", at: 1791986083963, wired: true,
 *   gpu: { available: true, source: "/sys/kernel/gpu", value: { mhz: 221, busyPct: 63, minMhz: 221, maxMhz: 949 } },
 *   cpu: { cores: 8,
 *     app: { available: true, source: "/proc/23811/stat", value: { pid: 23811, name: "com.moku.garden", pct: 14.2, oneCorePct: 113.6 } },
 *     renderer: { available: false, source: "none", reason: "ambiguous" },
 *     surfaceflinger: { available: true, source: "/proc/612/stat", value: { pid: 612, name: "surfaceflinger", pct: 2.1, oneCorePct: 16.8 } } },
 *   memory: { app: { available: false, source: "dumpsys meminfo", reason: "warming-up" }, renderer: { available: false, source: "dumpsys meminfo", reason: "warming-up" } },
 *   heap: { available: false, source: "none", reason: "no-devtools-socket" } };
 * ```
 */
export type DeviceTelemetry = {
  readonly v: 1;
  /** The linked device id, "d-7f3a". */
  readonly device: string;
  readonly serial: string | null;
  readonly at: number;
  readonly wired: boolean;
  readonly gpu: Reading<GpuLoad>;
  readonly cpu: {
    /** Cores of the phone (`cpuN` lines of /proc/stat); null before the probe. */
    readonly cores: number | null;
    readonly app: Reading<ProcessCpu>;
    readonly renderer: Reading<ProcessCpu>;
    readonly surfaceflinger: Reading<ProcessCpu>;
  };
  readonly memory: {
    readonly app: Reading<ProcessMemory>;
    readonly renderer: Reading<ProcessMemory>;
  };
  readonly heap: Reading<{
    readonly samples: readonly HeapSample[];
    readonly gcs: readonly HeapGc[];
  }>;
};

/**
 * Why a watch has no telemetry: a LAN device, an iPhone, a device not linked, adb missing, or two
 * phones of one model.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const reason: TelemetryOffReason = "not-wired"; // connect.watch of a phone on the network
 * ```
 */
export type TelemetryOffReason = "not-wired" | "ios" | "not-linked" | "adb-missing" | "ambiguous";
~~~

`guards.ts` (the two exported guards; the functions are shown with their signatures):

~~~ts
/**
 * Reads a published `editor.devices` value: the directory when every part of it has its shape,
 * else undefined (the tools page then keeps the directory it had and warns).
 *
 * @param value - The published value.
 * @returns The directory, or undefined for another shape.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * readDirectory({ v: 1, mode: { on: false, owner: null, listen: null }, confirmIn: null, adb: { available: true },
 *   wire: [], asking: [], linked: [], at: 1791986083963 })?.mode.on; // false
 * readDirectory({ v: 2 }); // undefined
 * ```
 */
export function readDirectory(value: unknown): DeviceDirectory | undefined;

/**
 * Reads a published `editor.deviceTelemetry` value: the record when every reading has its shape
 * (available with its value, or not available with a known reason), else undefined.
 *
 * @param value - The published value.
 * @returns The record, or undefined for another shape.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * readTelemetry(record)?.gpu; // { available: true, source: "/sys/kernel/gpu", value: { mhz: 221, busyPct: 63, minMhz: 221, maxMhz: 949 } }
 * readTelemetry({ v: 1, device: "d-7f3a" }); // undefined
 * ```
 */
export function readTelemetry(value: unknown): DeviceTelemetry | undefined;
~~~

---

## 3b. perf protocol types (`src/plugins/perf/protocol/`, verbatim)

The runtime-free module perf, recorder, the overlay, renderView's Mission control and the collector's report share. Mission control's parts (spec 03 Delta 2026-10-16) are `frames.ts` (the frames feed and the range detail), `timeline.ts` (the timeline's lines and marks), `passes.ts` (the passes of a second and their filter chains), `sections.ts` (monitoring), `memory.ts` (memory trust), `gpu.ts` (the GPU noise rule) and `history.ts`, the tools page's 2-minute history of one source (about 3 MB, allocated once, written without allocating; renderView owns one). It imports its own files, `registry/protocol` by type and the engine by type only (`import type` of `@moku-labs/game`), never `hub/protocol`; no engine code enters a bundle. The barrel `perf/protocol/index.ts` re-exports every file below. Where a later engine spec adds fields, the type is the engine's with the addition; where the engine has no type yet, a structural copy. The functions are shown with their signatures.

#### `engine.ts`

~~~ts
export type {
  FrameColumns,
  FrameReadout,
  FrameReadResult,
  FrameRecord,
  FrameRing,
  LongFrameEntry,
  OverlayEventDetail,
  OverlayWhat,
  PassKind,
  PassRecord,
  PerfCause,
  PerfChange,
  PerfChangeEntry,
  PerfCollectorLine,
  PerfDisplay,
  PerfEventLine,
  PerfEventName,
  PerfHeaderLine,
  PerfLogLine,
  PerfLongFrameLine,
  PerfMarkLine,
  PerfMeasured,
  PerfSampleLine,
  PerfSpikeLine,
  PerfStartupLine,
  PerfThermalLine,
  PoolTrimDetail,
  WarmDetail
} from "@moku-labs/game";

/**
 * The version every log line carries as `v` (11:930, 11:1135). The editor keeps its own constant: a
 * value import from the engine root would pull the engine into the tools bundle. The contract test
 * compares it with the engine's `PERF_LOG_VERSION`.
 */
export const PERF_LOG_VERSION = 1;

/**
 * Buckets of a sample's `frameHist` (11:1006-1007): [0,1) … [49,50) ms, then [50,55) … [195,200) ms,
 * then 200 ms and over. The contract test compares it with the engine's `PERF_GAP_BUCKETS`.
 */
export const PERF_GAP_BUCKETS = 81;

/**
 * The frame phases in the engine's order (11:731, 11:1016): `phaseMs` holds 6 values a frame, at
 * `slot * 6 + phase index`. The engine's `PHASES` is internal to `time`; the contract test reads
 * the order back through the engine's `frameAt`.
 */
export const PHASES = ["input", "animate", "layout", "sync", "signals", "render"] as const;

/**
 * The render-pass ring of `FrameRing.passes` (11:762-767), named here: the engine inlines it.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const passes: PassColumns = app.renderer.monitor.frames().passes;
 * passes.capacity; // 4096: four passes for each of the 1024 frames
 * ```
 */
export type PassColumns = FrameRing["passes"];

/**
 * The native shell's thermal reading (`Time.ThermalReading`, 11:271-293): a field the shell left out
 * is `null`. The engine's own type.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const reading: ThermalReading = { status: 2, headroom: 0.71, at: 1791986090000, android: null };
 * ```
 */
export type ThermalReading = Time.ThermalReading;

/**
 * The engine's frame-rate mode (spec 21 G1.3, `Time.RateMode`): `"fixed"` (`maxFps`), `"auto"` (the
 * adaptive rule), `"forced"` (`setRate` with a number).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const mode: RateMode = "auto";
 * ```
 */
export type RateMode = Time.RateMode;

/**
 * Why the rate is what it is: the reason of the last change (spec 21 G1.3, `Time.RateReason`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const reason: RateReason = "missed"; // the loop fell back to 60 after missed frames
 * ```
 */
export type RateReason = Time.RateReason;

/**
 * The native shell's thermal status, normalized (spec 21 G1.3, `Time.ThermalStatus`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const status: ThermalStatus = "moderate";
 * ```
 */
export type ThermalStatus = Time.ThermalStatus;

/**
 * The loop's frame rate as `app.time.rate()` answers it (spec 21 G1.3, `Time.FrameRate`); the
 * header's `rate`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const rate: FrameRate = { fps: 60, mode: "auto", reason: "missed", displayHz: 120, ladder: [120, 60], thermal: "none" };
 * ```
 */
export type FrameRate = Time.FrameRate;

/**
 * A change of the loop's rate or of its mode (spec 21 G1.3, `Time.RateChange`): the payload of
 * `time:rate` and the `detail` of a `rate` event line.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const change: RateChange = { from: 120, to: 60, reason: "missed", mode: "auto", displayHz: 120, thermal: "none", window: { drawn: 41, missed: 9, heavy: 0 }, dwellMs: 5000 };
 * ```
 */
export type RateChange = Time.RateChange;

/**
 * The detail of the editor's own `devtools` event line (addendum 3B/4 item 1): the overlay window's
 * mode and tab. The recorder writes it; perf ignores it. The engine lists the name but leaves the
 * detail to the editor, so this is the editor's own type.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const devtools: DevtoolsDetail = { mode: "card", tab: "frames" };
 * ```
 */
export type DevtoolsDetail = { mode: "hidden" | "pill" | "card"; tab: string };

/**
 * Kept pictures of the last drawn frame (spec 23 P12.1, `Renderer.KeptStats`): pictures drawn as one
 * texture, the MiB their textures hold, and the pictures taken in the last full second.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const kept: KeptStats = { pictures: 1, mb: 1.4, retakes: 0 };
 * ```
 */
export type KeptStats = Renderer.KeptStats;

/**
 * The members of the engine's `RenderStats` perf reads (11 R12.2, addendum 3B/4 item 3; 23 P12.1;
 * 26 R2.3.3): `renderPasses`, `renderPassesMax` and `kept` in every build, `redraws` and `rebuilds`
 * in dev or agent builds only.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const stats: RenderStatsLike = { renderPasses: 1, renderPassesMax: 3, kept: { pictures: 1, mb: 1.4, retakes: 0 }, redraws: 0, rebuilds: 0 };
 * ```
 */
export type RenderStatsLike = Pick<
  Renderer.RenderStats,
  "renderPasses" | "renderPassesMax" | "kept" | "redraws" | "rebuilds"
>;

/**
 * The engine's performance monitor as the editor uses it: `app.renderer.monitor` of an agent build
 * (11-monitor R13.1, 11:1153-1158), the engine's `Renderer.PerfMonitorApi`. In a build without the
 * agent flag every member exists and does nothing: `frames()` answers a ring of capacity 0, `stream`
 * never calls.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // perf finds it on the game it wraps.
 * const monitor: MonitorLike | undefined = monitorOf(registry.game());
 * monitor?.frames().capacity; // 1024 on a debug build of the phone
 * ```
 */
export type MonitorLike = Renderer.PerfMonitorApi;

/**
 * The pass ring columns of the 0.15.x patch (E2, TC §2.1): the owner entity (0 = none), the filter
 * kind (`kind2`, 1-based, 0 = none: the name is `kindNames[kind2 - 1]` of the frame ring, not of
 * the pass ring), the draw-call counter at the pass's start (0 where draws are not counted: WebGL),
 * the target format and the resolution. Every column is absent on an older engine.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const extra: PassColumnsNext = { owner: new Uint32Array(4096), kind2: new Uint8Array(4096) };
 * ```
 */
export type PassColumnsNext = {
  readonly owner?: Uint32Array;
  readonly kind2?: Uint8Array;
  readonly drawsAt?: Uint16Array;
  readonly format?: readonly (string | null)[];
  readonly resolution?: Float32Array;
};

/**
 * The frame ring's names of the 0.15.x patch (E2, E8): the interned filter kinds `kind2` indexes
 * 1-based (`"other"` first, at most 32, only growing) and the world's system names `sysIdx` indexes
 * (a new array when a system registers). Absent from the type of an older engine.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const names: RingNamesNext = { kindNames: ["other", "fog.blur"], systemNames: ["ward.update"] };
 * ```
 */
export type RingNamesNext = {
  readonly kindNames?: readonly string[];
  readonly systemNames?: readonly string[];
};

/**
 * The event names the 0.15.x patch and the next change add to the engine's `PerfEventName`: `shader`
 * (E4), `problem` (N3, three rules in 0.15.1), `debug` (U6, overdraw), `gc` (N6) and `sections` (N1).
 * The dev engine (0.15.1) lists the patch's three; the peer floor (0.15.0) none.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const name: PerfEventNameNext = "shader";
 * ```
 */
export type PerfEventNameNext = PerfEventName | "shader" | "problem" | "debug" | "gc" | "sections";

/**
 * The detail of a `shader` event line (E4): what was compiled (`"compile"` or `"module"` in 0.15.x;
 * `"variant"` / `"relink"` with the next change, kept as their string), its label, its ms, the
 * frame, whether it ran at boot, and the pass it ran during.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const detail: ShaderEventDetail = { what: "compile", label: "fog.blur", ms: 38.2, frame: 4851, boot: false,
 *   during: { pass: 2, filter: "fog.blur", owner: 412, view: "fogLayer" } };
 * ```
 */
export type ShaderEventDetail = {
  readonly what: ShaderWhat;
  readonly label: string | null;
  readonly ms: number;
  readonly frame: number;
  readonly boot: boolean;
  readonly during: {
    readonly pass: number | null;
    readonly filter: string | null;
    readonly owner: number | null;
    readonly view: string | null;
  };
};

/**
 * Why a problem opened (engine U5): `filter-still` says why the still view is not kept (`budget`,
 * `not-eligible`), `target-churn` which clause fired (`rate`, `idle`, `after-trim`); a newer
 * engine's word is kept as its string.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const why: ProblemReason = "after-trim"; // targets made right after a pool trim
 * ```
 */
export type ProblemReason =
  | "budget"
  | "not-eligible"
  | "rate"
  | "idle"
  | "after-trim"
  | (string & {});

/**
 * The detail of a `problem` event line (N3): a rule that flagged an owner and view, or the same
 * rule cleared for them (`cleared` carries owner and view, engine U5). `filter-still` and
 * `target-churn` also say why (`reason`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const flagged: ProblemEventDetail = { rule: "filter-still", severity: "warn", owner: 412, view: "fogLayer", filter: "fog.blur",
 *   value: 6.2, threshold: 2, since: 4802, frames: 53, reason: "budget" };
 * const cleared: ProblemEventDetail = { rule: "filter-still", cleared: true, owner: 412, view: "fogLayer" };
 * ```
 */
export type ProblemEventDetail =
  | {
      readonly rule: ProblemRule;
      readonly severity: "info" | "warn";
      readonly owner: number | null;
      readonly view: string | null;
      readonly filter: string | null;
      readonly value: number | null;
      readonly threshold: number | null;
      readonly since: number | null;
      readonly frames: number | null;
      readonly reason?: ProblemReason;
    }
  | {
      readonly rule: ProblemRule;
      readonly cleared: true;
      readonly owner: number | null;
      readonly view: string | null;
    };

/**
 * The detail of a `gc` event line (N6, next change): MB freed, the heap after, and whether it is a
 * hint (inferred from a drop).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const gc: GcEventDetail = { freedMb: 4.2, heapMb: 41.9, hint: true };
 * ```
 */
export type GcEventDetail = {
  readonly freedMb: number;
  readonly heapMb: number | null;
  readonly hint: boolean;
};

/**
 * The detail of a `sections` event line (N1, next change): the sections switched on and off.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const switched: SectionsEventDetail = { on: ["passes", "shaders"], off: [] };
 * ```
 */
export type SectionsEventDetail = {
  readonly on: readonly MonitorSectionName[];
  readonly off: readonly MonitorSectionName[];
};

/**
 * The detail of a `debug` event line (engine U6): the overdraw heat map turned on or off; frames
 * drawn with it on are not real cost.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const debug: DebugEventDetail = { overdraw: true };
 * ```
 */
export type DebugEventDetail = { readonly overdraw: boolean };

/**
 * The fields a `sample` line gains with the 0.15.x patch and the next change: render-target
 * churn (E5), the object counters (engine U3: entities, views, timers, frame and clock listeners
 * and the registered counts), the shader counters (N7), the cost per section (N2) and the memory
 * source (N6, beside the kept `heapMb`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const extra: PerfSampleNext = { targets: { created: 6, destroyed: 6 },
 *   counts: { entities: 104, views: 180, timers: 3, frameListeners: 2, clockListeners: 1 } };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfSampleNext = {
  readonly targets?: { readonly created: number; readonly destroyed: number } | null;
  readonly counts?: {
    readonly entities: number;
    readonly views: number;
    readonly timers: number;
    readonly frameListeners: number;
    readonly clockListeners: number;
    readonly [registered: string]: number;
  } | null;
  readonly shaders?: {
    readonly pipelines: number;
    readonly hits: number;
    readonly compiles: number;
    readonly variants: number;
    readonly relinks: number;
  } | null;
  readonly sectionsMs?: Readonly<Partial<Record<MonitorSectionName, number>>>;
  readonly memory?: {
    readonly source: "performance.memory" | "uasm" | "shell" | null;
    readonly heapMb: number | null;
    readonly processMb: number | null;
  };
};

/**
 * The fields the header gains with the 0.15.x patch and the next change: the app id (with the
 * `.debug` suffix on native debug installs, S-E3; null on a page the build gave none), the overdraw
 * flag (U6) and the sections (N1).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const extra: PerfHeaderNext = { app: { id: "com.moku.garden.debug" }, debug: { overdraw: false } };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfHeaderNext = {
  readonly app?: { readonly id: string | null };
  readonly debug?: { readonly overdraw: boolean };
  readonly sections?: MonitorSections;
};

/**
 * The fields the engine's `FrameRate` (the `game.frameRate` answer) gains with the 0.15.x patch (E6):
 * the rate the loop is told to hold (null only in mode `"auto"`) and who holds it back (`"panel"`:
 * the asked rate is above the display's).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const held: FrameRateNext = { asked: 120, heldBy: "panel" }; // "This display runs at 60 Hz"
 * ```
 */
export type FrameRateNext = {
  readonly asked?: number | null;
  readonly heldBy?: "panel" | null;
};

/**
 * One filter chain of a `passes` summary (N4, next change): an owner and view's consecutive filter
 * passes over the second.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const chain: PassesLineChain = { owner: 412, view: "fogLayer", kinds: ["fog.blur", "fog.blur"], applies: 120, mpx: 221.2, draws: 4,
 *   gpuMs: { p50: 6.2, max: 6.9 } };
 * ```
 */
export type PassesLineChain = {
  readonly owner: number | null;
  readonly view: string | null;
  readonly kinds: readonly string[];
  readonly applies: number;
  readonly mpx: number;
  readonly draws: number | null;
  readonly gpuMs: { readonly p50: number; readonly max: number } | null;
};

/**
 * The engine's per-second `passes` summary line (N4, next change): the chains of the second and the
 * heaviest drawn frame's passes. perf answers it as is (`source: "engine"`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const line: PerfPassesLine = { v: 1, kind: "passes", t: 81000, chains: [], heaviest: null };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfPassesLine = {
  readonly v: 1;
  readonly kind: "passes";
  readonly t: number;
  readonly chains: readonly PassesLineChain[];
  readonly heaviest: { readonly frame: number; readonly passes: readonly PassRecord[] } | null;
};
~~~

#### `causes.ts`

~~~ts
/**
 * The cause bits of the window and the wire, in bit order: index = bit. The engine's `PERF_CAUSES`,
 * kept here engine-free because the tools page and the server's report read the wire and the logs
 * with it; the contract test asserts the two are equal. The agent decodes the ring with
 * `PERF_CAUSES` itself (`perf/ring.ts`), by name into this order.
 */
export const CAUSE_BITS: readonly PerfCause[] = [
  "gap",
  "js",
  "gpu",
  "compile",
  "upload",
  "longFrame",
  "gc?"
];

/**
 * Primary cause codes, by the editor's rank (R11 answer 11): 1 gpu, 2 upload, 3 compile, 4 longFrame,
 * 5 js, 6 gc?, 7 gap; 0 = not a spike. A lower code wins. A long frame names its scripts, so it
 * outranks plain JS; gc? is a hint, so only gap ranks below it.
 */
export const CAUSE_RANK: readonly PerfCause[] = [
  "gpu",
  "upload",
  "compile",
  "longFrame",
  "js",
  "gc?",
  "gap"
];

/**
 * The primary cause code of a frame's cause bits. Allocation-free: a loop over the bit masks in
 * rank order.
 *
 * @param bits - The `causes` column value.
 * @returns 1..7 by CAUSE_RANK, 0 when no bit is set.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * primaryCause(0b0010010); // 2: upload beats js
 * ```
 */
export function primaryCause(bits: number): number;

/**
 * The cause names of a frame, primary first, then by rank. Allocates: for records, not the read loop.
 *
 * @param bits - The `causes` column value.
 * @returns The names; [] for a frame that is not a spike.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * causesOf(0b0100010); // ["longFrame", "js"]
 * ```
 */
export function causesOf(bits: number): PerfCause[];

/**
 * The name of a primary cause code.
 *
 * @param code - 1..7.
 * @returns The PerfCause; undefined for 0 or out of range.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * causeName(6); // "gc?"
 * ```
 */
export function causeName(code: number): PerfCause | undefined;

/**
 * The change names of a frame's `changed` bits, in PerfChange order.
 *
 * @param bits - The `changed` column value.
 * @returns The names; [] when nothing changed.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * changesOf(0b01000); // ["bundle"]
 * ```
 */
export function changesOf(bits: number): PerfChange[];

/**
 * The `causes` bit of a pause: the gap before the frame was long (the engine's judgement; perf clears
 * it for a gap vsync explains).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * (window.causes[row] & GAP_BIT) !== 0; // the row's gap counts
 * ```
 */
export const GAP_BIT = bitOf("gap");

/**
 * Whether a frame's cause bits hold its own work: JS or GPU over budget, or a long animation frame.
 *
 * @param bits - The `causes` column value.
 * @returns Whether the frame worked over budget.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * hasWork(0b1_0001); // false: a gap and an upload, no work over budget
 * ```
 */
export function hasWork(bits: number): boolean;

/**
 * Whether a frame's gap is longer than vsync can explain: more than 1.5 frames of its budget or of
 * the display's frame, whichever is longer. A budget from a 120 fps target on a 60 Hz display is not
 * a reason to flag the display's own 16.7 ms between frames.
 *
 * @param gapMs - The gap before the frame, ms; NaN for none.
 * @param budgetMs - The frame's budget, ms.
 * @param displayHz - The display's refresh rate the engine learned; null when unknown.
 * @returns Whether the gap is notable.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * isNotableGap(16.7, 8.33, 60); // false: one vsync of a 60 Hz display
 * ```
 */
export function isNotableGap(gapMs: number, budgetMs: number, displayHz: number | null): boolean;

/**
 * The editor's spike decision for a frame (spec 03 delta 2026-10-15): a frame is a spike only for its
 * own work — JS or GPU over budget, or a long animation frame — never for a gap or the GC hint read
 * from it alone. A resting frame (the engine's idle cap, or render on demand that drew nothing) and a
 * break (a gap the browser made, no frame) are never spikes; the wake after a rest keeps its work but
 * not its gap. The primary cause then ranks every bit kept (an upload or a compile names the work).
 * Allocation-free.
 *
 * @param causes - The `causes` column value.
 * @param rest - The frame's rest: 0 awake, 1 resting, 2 the wake after a rest, 3 a break.
 * @returns 1..7 by CAUSE_RANK, 0 when the frame is not a spike.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * spikeCause(0b1_0001, 0); // 0: a gap and an upload, no work over budget
 * ```
 */
export function spikeCause(causes: number, rest: number): number;
~~~

#### `rate.ts`

~~~ts
/**
 * The budget a window with no frame shows, ms: one 60 fps frame as the tape and the pill print it
 * (spec 03: `second().budgetMs` is 16.7 while the window is empty).
 */
export const EMPTY_BUDGET_MS = 16.7;

/**
 * The rate of a row whose ring value is missing and that has no row before it, ms: one 60 fps frame
 * (spec 03 read cycle step 4).
 */
export const DEFAULT_RATE_MS = 16.67;

/**
 * Frames per second of one frame of a rate: `Math.round(1000 / rateMs)`.
 *
 * @param rateMs - One frame of the rate, ms (the ring's `rateMs` column).
 * @returns The fps; 0 for a value that is not a finite number above 0 (a ring before `rateMs`, NaN).
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * rateFps(8.33); // 120
 * ```
 */
export function rateFps(rateMs: number): number;
~~~

#### `text.ts`

~~~ts
/** The longest text `cleanText` keeps by default, in characters. */
export const CLEAN_TEXT_MAX = 128;

/**
 * A phone's text, safe to print: control characters (C0, DEL, C1) and bidi embeddings, overrides
 * and isolates dropped, then at most `max` characters (code points, so a character is never cut in
 * half).
 *
 * @param text - The text as the phone sent it.
 * @param max - The most characters kept (128 by default).
 * @returns The clean text.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * cleanText("garden\u001b[2J‮/boss"); // "garden[2J/boss"
 * ```
 */
export function cleanText(text: string, max: number = CLEAN_TEXT_MAX): string;
~~~

#### `values.ts`

~~~ts
/**
 * Why perf has no monitor: a headless game (no renderer), or an engine before block 2b.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const reason: PerfOffReason = "no-renderer"; // a headless test game
 * ```
 */
export type PerfOffReason = "no-renderer" | "no-monitor";

/**
 * What perf can measure now. "waiting": the monitor exists but its ring is empty (capacity 0: the
 * agent flag is off, or the renderer has not attached yet).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * app.perf.status(); // { state: "on", lost: 0, gpuTimer: true } on the phone
 * ```
 */
export type PerfStatus =
  | { readonly state: "on"; readonly lost: number; readonly gpuTimer: boolean }
  | { readonly state: "waiting" }
  | { readonly state: "off"; readonly reason: PerfOffReason };

/**
 * The loop's frame rate as perf knows it: `fps` from the newest row's `rateMs`; `mode`, `reason`,
 * `displayHz` from the newest `rate` event (`RateChange`), else from the header's `rate`
 * (`FrameRate`, spec 21), else null (an engine before spec 21).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const rate: PerfRate = { fps: 120, mode: "auto", reason: "start", displayHz: 120, switches: 0 };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfRate = {
  /** Frames per second of the newest row (`rateFps(rateMs)`); null while the window is empty. */
  readonly fps: number | null;
  readonly mode: RateMode | null;
  readonly reason: RateReason | null;
  readonly displayHz: number | null;
  /** Rate switches inside the window (rows whose `rateMs` differs from the row before). */
  readonly switches: number;
};

/**
 * What perf reads from `renderer.stats()` (11 R12.2, addendum 3B/4 item 3; 23 P12.1; 26 R2.3.3). A
 * key the engine does not answer is null (an engine before spec 23 has no `kept`; a production
 * build has no `redraws`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // The memory screen at rest on a debug build, its lamps kept.
 * const render: PerfRenderStats = { passesMax: 1, kept: { pictures: 4, mb: 1.6, retakes: 0 }, redraws: 0, rebuilds: 0 };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfRenderStats = {
  /** `stats().renderPassesMax`. */
  readonly passesMax: number | null;
  /** `stats().kept`: pictures drawn as one texture, the MB they hold, retakes in the last second. */
  readonly kept: KeptStats | null;
  /** `stats().redraws`: the engine's Graphics redraws in the last second (dev and agent builds). */
  readonly redraws: number | null;
  /** `stats().rebuilds`: Pixi's instruction rebuilds in the last second (dev and agent builds). */
  readonly rebuilds: number | null;
};

/**
 * How the window paced (spec 03 delta 2026-10-15): whether the screen rests now and since when, its
 * resting frames and their time, the breaks the browser made, and the p90 frame time of the awake
 * frames. While `idle` the headline says idle instead of fps.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const activity: PerfActivity = { idle: true, idleSince: 1760454003120, idleFrames: 92, idleMs: 3066, breaks: 0, p90Ms: 17.6 };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfActivity = {
  /** The newest frame rests: the engine's idle cap, or render on demand that drew nothing. */
  readonly idle: boolean;
  /**
   * Epoch ms of the first frame of the current rest (header.timeOrigin + t), steady for the whole rest
   * however long it lasts; null while awake or before a header.
   */
  readonly idleSince: number | null;
  /** Resting frames in the window. */
  readonly idleFrames: number;
  /** Their time, ms. */
  readonly idleMs: number;
  /** Breaks in the window: gaps of 900 ms or more without work, the browser made no frame. */
  readonly breaks: number;
  /**
   * p90 frame time of the awake frames of the window, ms; while the window holds none (a long rest),
   * the last awake window's; null before the first awake frame.
   */
  readonly p90Ms: number | null;
};

/**
 * The headline GPU (spec 03 delta item 8): the p50 and p90 GPU time of the window's drawn frames
 * with a measured GPU. One frame's GPU time is noisy on Apple and Mali (17–25 ms readings at a
 * 0.49 ms p50), so the headline never shows a single frame's.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const gpuTime: PerfGpuTime = { p50Ms: 0.49, p90Ms: 0.61 };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfGpuTime = {
  /** p50 GPU time, ms to hundredths. */
  readonly p50Ms: number;
  /** p90 GPU time, ms to hundredths. */
  readonly p90Ms: number;
};

/**
 * What this page's engine and build measure (spec 03 Delta 2026-10-16 D2): computed when the header
 * arrives and at the first read of a ring, cached until the next header. The tools page shows "not
 * measured on this engine" for a false capability and "X is off" for a section switched off (D7).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const caps: PerfCaps = { passOwners: true, passDraws: true, passFormat: true, systemNames: true, shaderEvents: true,
 *   problems: false, gc: false, sections: false, detail: false, passesLine: false, gpuTimer: true, heap: "untrusted" };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfCaps = {
  /** ring.passes.owner and kind2 present. */
  readonly passOwners: boolean;
  /** ring.passes.drawsAt present. */
  readonly passDraws: boolean;
  /** ring.passes.format and resolution present. */
  readonly passFormat: boolean;
  /** ring.systemNames present. */
  readonly systemNames: boolean;
  /** A `shader` event line seen, or the engine lists the name. */
  readonly shaderEvents: boolean;
  /** header.measured includes "problems", or a `problem` line seen. */
  readonly problems: boolean;
  /** header.measured includes "gc", or a `gc` line seen. */
  readonly gc: boolean;
  /** The monitor has `sections` (next change). */
  readonly sections: boolean;
  /** The monitor has `detail` (next change). */
  readonly detail: boolean;
  /** A `passes` summary line seen (next change). */
  readonly passesLine: boolean;
  /** header.gpu.timer is not null (false on iOS: every gpuMs null). */
  readonly gpuTimer: boolean;
  /** "trusted": a heap number that moves; "untrusted": a WebView or a frozen counter (D6); "none": null (iOS). */
  readonly heap: "trusted" | "untrusted" | "none";
};

/**
 * The pill, the header and the counters: the window's fps and spike count, and the newest sample
 * and screen facts as the engine sent them.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const second: PerfSecond = { state: "on", fps: { loop: 60, drawn: 54 }, spikes: 6, budgetMs: 16.67,
 *   rate: { fps: 60, mode: "auto", reason: "missed", displayHz: 120, switches: 1 },
 *   gpuTime: { p50Ms: 0.49, p90Ms: 0.61 },
 *   render: { passesMax: 3, kept: { pictures: 1, mb: 1.4, retakes: 0 }, redraws: 0, rebuilds: 0 },
 *   sample: null, display: null, device: null, gpu: null, build: "debug-20261014T160000Z", engine: "0.14.12+9c41e0" };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfSecond = {
  readonly state: PerfStatus["state"];
  /** Awake frames of the last 1000 ms of the window: run by the loop, drawn by the renderer. */
  readonly fps: { readonly loop: number; readonly drawn: number };
  /** Spikes in the window (the one-window rule, design §4). */
  readonly spikes: number;
  /** The newest frame's own budget (its `budgetMs` column); 16.7 while the window is empty. */
  readonly budgetMs: number;
  /** The loop's rate now and who decides it (counters, device row). */
  readonly rate: PerfRate;
  /**
   * How the window paced: rest, breaks, p90 of the awake frames (spec 03 delta 2026-10-15). Absent from
   * an agent before the delta.
   */
  readonly activity?: PerfActivity;
  /**
   * The headline GPU over the window (spec 03 delta item 8); null without a measured GPU time (no GPU
   * timer). Absent from an agent before item 8.
   */
  readonly gpuTime?: PerfGpuTime | null;
  /** `renderer.stats()` read when this value was built; null when the renderer has no `stats` or it threw. */
  readonly render: PerfRenderStats | null;
  /** The newest `sample` line, as the engine sent it; null before the first. */
  readonly sample: PerfSampleLine | null;
  /** header.display, replaced by every `display` event. */
  readonly display: PerfDisplay | null;
  /** header.device. */
  readonly device: PerfHeaderLine["device"] | null;
  /** header.gpu. */
  readonly gpu: PerfHeaderLine["gpu"] | null;
  /** header.build: spec 10's build id. */
  readonly build: string | null;
  /** header.engine: spec 10's engine fingerprint. */
  readonly engine: string | null;
  /**
   * Monitoring: the sections, perf's feeds and their cost (spec 03 Delta 2026-10-16 D7). Absent from
   * an agent before that delta.
   */
  readonly monitor?: PerfMonitorState;
  /** The page's memory and whether to trust it (D6). Absent from an agent before that delta. */
  readonly memory?: PerfMemory;
  /** What the engine and build measure (D2). Absent from an agent before that delta. */
  readonly caps?: PerfCaps;
  /** header.timeOrigin as text: a new value means a new page (reload). Absent from an older agent. */
  readonly epoch?: string | null;
  /** The newest sample's object counters (engine U3, D1); null on an engine without them. */
  readonly counts?: PerfSampleNext["counts"];
  /** header.app.id, with the `.debug` suffix on native debug installs (S-E3, D1); null without it. */
  readonly appId?: string | null;
};

/**
 * A frame event of the game that a spike record lists under "what changed": a game overlay changing
 * (`label` + `what`), a pool trim (MB freed) or a warm-up run (draws).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const opened: PerfFrameEvent = { kind: "overlay", frame: 4812, label: "shopDimLayer", what: "open", mode: "freeze" };
 * const trim: PerfFrameEvent = { kind: "pool-trim", frame: 4811, reason: "rest", freedMb: 41.5 };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfFrameEvent =
  | {
      readonly kind: "overlay";
      readonly frame: number;
      readonly label: string;
      readonly what: OverlayWhat;
      readonly mode: string;
    }
  | {
      readonly kind: "pool-trim";
      readonly frame: number;
      readonly reason: PoolTrimDetail["reason"];
      readonly freedMb: number;
    }
  | { readonly kind: "warm"; readonly frame: number; readonly draws: number };

/**
 * One spike of the window, for lists and MCP.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const spike: PerfSpikeSummary = { frame: 4812, agoMs: 980, ms: 41.3, budgetMs: 16.7, overMs: 24.6, cause: "upload",
 *   causes: ["upload", "gap"], jsMs: 8, gpuMs: 6.6, path: "garden/boss", why: "41.0 MB of textures uploaded this frame (bundle garden-boss)" };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfSpikeSummary = {
  readonly frame: number;
  /** ms before the newest frame of the window. */
  readonly agoMs: number;
  readonly ms: number;
  /** The frame's own budget: its `budgetMs` column, the budget the engine's spike rule used for it. */
  readonly budgetMs: number;
  /** ms − budgetMs. */
  readonly overMs: number;
  /** The primary cause by CAUSE_RANK. */
  readonly cause: PerfCause;
  /** Every cause, primary first. */
  readonly causes: readonly PerfCause[];
  readonly jsMs: number;
  readonly gpuMs: number | null;
  /** The flow path of the frame (ring.paths). */
  readonly path: string;
  /** One sentence: why this frame was late. */
  readonly why: string;
};

/**
 * The spike record (design §7): the summary plus the frame's numbers and, once the engine's spike
 * line arrived (about one flush later), its full detail.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * app.perf.spike(4812)?.rateSwitch; // { from: 120, to: 60, reason: "missed", mode: "auto" }
 * ```
 */
export type PerfSpikeRecord = PerfSpikeSummary & {
  /** Epoch ms of the frame's start (header.timeOrigin + t); null before a header. */
  readonly at: number | null;
  /** The frame's rate in fps (`rateFps(rateMs)`). */
  readonly fps: number;
  /** The rate switch at this frame; `reason` and `mode` from its `rate` event (null when only the rows show it). */
  readonly rateSwitch: {
    readonly from: number;
    readonly to: number;
    readonly reason: RateReason | null;
    readonly mode: RateMode | null;
  } | null;
  readonly gapMs: number | null;
  readonly drawn: boolean;
  /** The GPU time may still change. */
  readonly gpuPartial: boolean;
  /** Phase ms in PHASES order plus agent; null when the ring slot was overwritten and no spike line came. */
  readonly phases: {
    readonly input: number;
    readonly animate: number;
    readonly layout: number;
    readonly sync: number;
    readonly signals: number;
    readonly render: number;
    readonly agent: number;
  } | null;
  readonly passes: number | null;
  readonly draws: number | null;
  readonly filters: { readonly applies: number; readonly mpx: number } | null;
  readonly uploads: { readonly count: number; readonly mb: number } | null;
  readonly compiles: number | null;
  readonly changed: readonly PerfChange[];
  /** The game's frame events of this frame (and the `pool-trim` lines of the frame before), in arrival order. */
  readonly events: readonly PerfFrameEvent[];
  /** The engine's spike line; null until it arrives. */
  readonly detail: PerfSpikeLine | null;
};
~~~

#### `window.ts`

~~~ts
/**
 * The last `windowMs` of frames as struct-of-arrays, oldest row first: what the frame graph draws.
 * perf owns one, rewrites it at every read and hands it out only for the length of a `readWindow`
 * call, as the read-only `PerfWindowView` (never keep the reference; copy what you keep); a tools
 * page fills its own from the wire with `readWireWindow`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * app.perf.readWindow(window => {
 *   window.count; // 358 at 60 fps
 *   window.budgetMs[window.count - 1]; // 16.67
 * });
 * ```
 */
export type PerfWindow = {
  /** Rows the arrays hold. */
  readonly capacity: number;
  /** Rows in use, oldest first. */
  count: number;
  /** Page-clock ms of the left edge of the time axis: endMs − windowMs. */
  startMs: number;
  /** Page-clock ms of the right edge: start of the newest frame plus its frame time. */
  endMs: number;
  /** False when the page has no GPU timer (header.gpu.timer null, WebKit): the graph stacks JS and idle only. */
  gpuTimer: boolean;
  /** Increments whenever any row or scalar changed, so a painter skips an unchanged window. */
  version: number;
  /**
   * The headline GPU (spec 03 delta item 8): p50 of the GPU times of the drawn frames with a measured
   * GPU, ms; NaN without one (no GPU timer). One frame's GPU time is noisy, the window's p50 is not.
   */
  gpuP50Ms: number;
  /** p90 of the same GPU times, ms; NaN without one. */
  gpuP90Ms: number;
  /** The frame number of each row. */
  readonly frame: Uint32Array;
  /** Page-clock ms of each frame's start. */
  readonly t: Float64Array;
  /** Frame time: max(gap, js + gpu). */
  readonly ms: Float32Array;
  /** The game's work: workMs − agentMs, at least 0. */
  readonly jsMs: Float32Array;
  /** GPU ms; NaN = not measured (yet). */
  readonly gpuMs: Float32Array;
  /** One frame of the frame's rate, ms (ring column `rateMs`); a change from one row to the next is a rate switch. */
  readonly rateMs: Float32Array;
  /** The frame's own spike budget, ms (ring column `budgetMs`): the budget the engine's spike rule used for it. */
  readonly budgetMs: Float32Array;
  /** 1 when the renderer drew the frame. */
  readonly drawn: Uint8Array;
  /**
   * How the frame paced (spec 03 delta 2026-10-15, `REST`): 0 awake, 1 resting (the engine's idle cap,
   * or render on demand that drew nothing), 2 the wake right after a rest (awake, its gap is the
   * rest's), 3 a break (a gap of 900 ms or more without work: the browser made no frame).
   */
  readonly rest: Uint8Array;
  /**
   * The cause bits perf counts (CAUSE_BITS): the engine's, without the gap bit of a gap vsync explains
   * and without a GPU that is noise (see `noise`).
   */
  readonly causes: Uint8Array;
  /**
   * The cause bits perf heard but did not count (spec 03 delta item 8): `GPU_BIT` for a GPU over the
   * frame's budget that is not sustained (no other over-budget GPU within 2 drawn frames), the faint
   * GPU tick of the graph. Moves to `causes` when a second over-budget GPU lands near it.
   */
  readonly noise: Uint8Array;
  /** The primary cause code (CAUSE_RANK), 0 = not a spike. */
  readonly cause: Uint8Array;
  /** Rows of the spikes, oldest first. */
  readonly spikes: Uint16Array;
  /** Spikes in `spikes`. */
  spikeCount: number;
  /**
   * A sort scratch of `capacity` values for the window's percentiles (`spreadGpu`, the awake p90):
   * made once with the window, so no read allocates. Not part of the view.
   */
  readonly sorted: Float64Array;
};

/**
 * The window as a reader sees it: every scalar `readonly` and every column a read-only
 * `ArrayLike<number>` (a typed array is assignable to it), so a visitor cannot write a row or a
 * scalar without a cast. No copy is made; typed arrays cannot be frozen, so the guard is the type.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * app.perf.readWindow(window => {
 *   window.ms[window.count - 1]; // 41.3
 *   // window.ms[0] = 0; — a type error: the index signature only permits reading
 * });
 * ```
 */
export type PerfWindowView = {
  readonly capacity: number;
  readonly count: number;
  readonly startMs: number;
  readonly endMs: number;
  readonly gpuTimer: boolean;
  readonly version: number;
  /** The headline GPU p50, ms (NaN: none); absent in a window an agent before item 8 filled. */
  readonly gpuP50Ms?: number;
  /** The headline GPU p90, ms (NaN: none); absent in a window an agent before item 8 filled. */
  readonly gpuP90Ms?: number;
  readonly frame: ArrayLike<number>;
  readonly t: ArrayLike<number>;
  readonly ms: ArrayLike<number>;
  readonly jsMs: ArrayLike<number>;
  readonly gpuMs: ArrayLike<number>;
  readonly rateMs: ArrayLike<number>;
  readonly budgetMs: ArrayLike<number>;
  readonly drawn: ArrayLike<number>;
  /** `REST` per row; absent in a window an agent before the 2026-10-15 delta filled (all awake). */
  readonly rest?: ArrayLike<number>;
  readonly causes: ArrayLike<number>;
  /** Cause bits heard but not counted (`GPU_BIT`: a faint GPU tick); absent before item 8 (no noise). */
  readonly noise?: ArrayLike<number>;
  readonly cause: ArrayLike<number>;
  readonly spikes: ArrayLike<number>;
  readonly spikeCount: number;
};

/**
 * The wire form of a window (source `editor.perf.window`). Columns are plain arrays, so the value
 * is Json.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const wire: PerfWindowWire = { v: 1, startMs: 40123.5, endMs: 46123.5, gpuTimer: true, frame: [4811, 4812],
 *   t: [5917.4, 5958.7], ms: [16.7, 41.3], jsMs: [3.4, 8], gpuMs: [5.2, 6.6], rateMs: [16.67, 16.67],
 *   budgetMs: [16.67, 16.67], drawn: [1, 1], causes: [0, 17] }; // 17 = gap + upload: primary upload
 * ```
 */
export type PerfWindowWire = {
  v: 1;
  startMs: number;
  endMs: number;
  gpuTimer: boolean;
  frame: number[];
  /** ms after startMs. */
  t: number[];
  ms: number[];
  jsMs: number[];
  gpuMs: (number | null)[];
  rateMs: number[];
  /** The frame's own spike budget (ring column `budgetMs`). */
  budgetMs: number[];
  drawn: (0 | 1)[];
  /** `REST` per row; absent from an agent before the 2026-10-15 delta (all awake). */
  rest?: RestState[];
  causes: number[];
  /** Cause bits heard but not counted per row (`GPU_BIT`); absent from an agent before item 8 (none). */
  noise?: number[];
};

/**
 * How a frame paced, the window's `rest` column (spec 03 delta 2026-10-15): awake; resting (the
 * engine's idle cap, or render on demand that drew nothing); the wake right after a rest (its gap is
 * the rest's); a break (a gap of 900 ms or more without work: the browser made no frame). Only awake
 * frames and wakes count in the fps, only awake frames in the p90; resting frames and breaks are
 * never spikes.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * app.perf.readWindow(window => window.rest?.[window.count - 1] === REST.idle); // true on a still screen
 * ```
 */
export const REST = { awake: 0, idle: 1, woke: 2, break: 3 } as const;

/**
 * One state of `REST`.
 */
export type RestState = (typeof REST)[keyof typeof REST];

/**
 * Allocates a window of `capacity` rows: every array once, `count` 0, `gpuTimer` true, `version` 0.
 *
 * @param capacity - Rows, a whole number from 1 to 65535.
 * @returns The empty window.
 * @throws {TypeError} For a capacity that is not a whole number from 1 to 65535.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createPerfWindow(1024).capacity; // 1024
 * ```
 */
export function createPerfWindow(capacity: number): PerfWindow;

/**
 * The row of a frame number (binary search: frames grow along the rows).
 *
 * @param window - The window.
 * @param frame - A frame number.
 * @returns The row; −1 when the frame is not in the window.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * rowOfFrame(window, 4812); // 357 when 4812 is the newest of 358 rows
 * ```
 */
export function rowOfFrame(window: PerfWindowView, frame: number): number;

/**
 * The next (1) or previous (−1) spike row after (before) `row`, wrapping around; from a row that is
 * not a spike, the first spike after / the last before it.
 *
 * @param window - The window.
 * @param row - The row to step from.
 * @param dir - 1 for next, −1 for previous.
 * @returns The spike row; −1 when the window has no spike.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * stepSpike(window, 300, 1); // 12: past the newest spike (row 290), wrapped to the oldest
 * ```
 */
export function stepSpike(window: PerfWindowView, row: number, dir: 1 | -1): number;

/**
 * The 1-based position of a row among the spikes: the "5/6" counter is `spikeOrdinal` / `spikeCount`.
 *
 * @param window - The window.
 * @param row - A row.
 * @returns The position; 0 when the row is not a spike.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * spikeOrdinal(window, 290); // 5 when row 290 is the fifth spike
 * ```
 */
export function spikeOrdinal(window: PerfWindowView, row: number): number;

/**
 * The mean of the measured `gpuMs` of the drawn rows: the "GPU avg" counter of the overlay and the
 * tools strip. An indexed loop, no allocation.
 *
 * @param window - The window.
 * @returns The mean; null when no drawn row has a measured GPU time (WebKit has no GPU timer).
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // Two drawn rows whose GPU took 5 and 7 ms: the "GPU avg" counter reads 6.
 * const window = createPerfWindow(2);
 * window.count = 2;
 * window.drawn.set([1, 1]);
 * window.gpuMs.set([5, 7]);
 * meanGpu(window); // 6
 * ```
 */
export function meanGpu(window: PerfWindowView): number | null;

/**
 * The wire value of a window (source `editor.perf.window`). Allocates: `t` as ms after `startMs`
 * rounded to 0.1, ms values (`rateMs` and `budgetMs` included) to 0.01, a `NaN` GPU time as `null`.
 *
 * @param window - The window.
 * @returns The wire value.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * writeWireWindow(window).budgetMs; // [16.67, 16.67]
 * ```
 */
export function writeWireWindow(window: PerfWindowView): PerfWindowWire;

/**
 * Fills `into` from a wire value: false and `into` untouched for a value of another shape (see
 * `checkedWire`); keeps the newest `into.capacity` rows; drops the cause bits the editor does not
 * know; recomputes `cause` and `spikes` with the editor's spike rule and the headline GPU p50/p90
 * from the rows; `version += 1`.
 *
 * @param value - The value of `editor.perf.window`.
 * @param into - The window to fill.
 * @returns Whether the value was a window.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * readWireWindow({ v: 2 }, window); // false: window unchanged
 * ```
 */
export function readWireWindow(value: Json, into: PerfWindow): boolean;
~~~

#### `guards.ts`

~~~ts
/**
 * The engine's performance monitor of a game: `game.renderer.monitor` when it has `stream`,
 * `frames`, `mark`, `event`, `beginAgent` and `endAgent` as functions. Never throws.
 *
 * @param game - The game app (any value).
 * @returns The monitor, or undefined.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * monitorOf({ time: {}, flow: {} }); // undefined: a headless game has no renderer
 * ```
 */
export function monitorOf(game: unknown): MonitorLike | undefined;

/**
 * Why a game has no monitor perf can use.
 *
 * @param game - The game app (any value).
 * @returns "no-renderer" without a renderer object, "no-monitor" with one but no usable monitor,
 *   undefined when a monitor exists.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * offReasonOf({ renderer: {} }); // "no-monitor": an engine before block 2b
 * ```
 */
export function offReasonOf(game: unknown): PerfOffReason | undefined;

/**
 * Whether a value has the shape of a `PerfDisplay` (11:960-964).
 *
 * @param value - The detail of a `display` event.
 * @returns Whether it is a display.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * isPerfDisplay({ dpr: 2 }); // false: canvas, css, safeArea, backend and orientation are missing
 * ```
 */
export function isPerfDisplay(value: unknown): value is PerfDisplay;

/**
 * What perf reads from `game.renderer.stats()`: calls it once and copies `renderPassesMax`, `kept`,
 * `redraws`, `rebuilds`, each null where the engine does not answer it. Never throws.
 *
 * @param game - The game app (any value).
 * @returns The copy; undefined when there is no `stats` function or the call throws.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * statsOf({ renderer: { stats: () => ({ renderPasses: 1 }) } });
 * // { passesMax: null, kept: null, redraws: null, rebuilds: null }: an engine before spec 23
 * ```
 */
export function statsOf(game: unknown): PerfRenderStats | undefined;

/**
 * The display's refresh rate the engine learned: `game.time.rate().displayHz` (spec 21), read
 * structurally. The engine's stream does not announce it until the rate itself changes, so perf asks
 * the game. Never throws.
 *
 * @param game - The game app (any value).
 * @returns The Hz; null when unknown, without `time.rate`, or when the call throws.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * displayHzOf({ time: { rate: () => ({ fps: 60, displayHz: 60 }) } }); // 60
 * ```
 */
export function displayHzOf(game: unknown): number | null;

/**
 * The display's refresh rate as a newer engine announces it in its display (engine diagnosis
 * 2026-10-15: `PerfDisplay` gains `hz`, and a `display` event follows each change), read
 * structurally: the engine before it has no `hz`. Preferred over `time.rate().displayHz`. Never
 * throws.
 *
 * @param display - The header's display or a `display` event's detail (any value).
 * @returns The Hz; null when absent or not a positive finite number.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * announcedHzOf({ ...header.display, hz: 120 }); // 120
 * announcedHzOf(header.display); // null on an engine before the display's hz
 * ```
 */
export function announcedHzOf(display: unknown): number | null;

/**
 * A game frame event of an event line (engine fact 11): `overlay` with a numeric `entity`, a string
 * `label`, `what` among `OverlayWhat` and a string `mode`; `pool-trim` with its reason and a finite
 * `freedMb`; `warm` with finite `draws`. The editor's own `devtools`, `command`, `recorder` lines
 * and malformed details are not frame events.
 *
 * @param line - An event line.
 * @returns The frame event, or undefined.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * frameEventOf({ v: 1, kind: "event", t: 0, build: null, frame: 4812, name: "warm", detail: { draws: 18 } });
 * // { kind: "warm", frame: 4812, draws: 18 }
 * ```
 */
export function frameEventOf(line: PerfEventLine): PerfFrameEvent | undefined;

/**
 * Whether a value has the shape of a `RateChange` (21:117-129): numbers `from`, `to`, `dwellMs`;
 * `reason` and `mode` among their unions; `displayHz` a number or null; `window` with three numbers;
 * `thermal` a status or null.
 *
 * @param value - The detail of a `rate` event line.
 * @returns Whether it is a rate change.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * isRateChange({ from: 120, to: 60 }); // false: reason, mode, window and dwellMs are missing
 * ```
 */
export function isRateChange(value: unknown): value is RateChange;

/**
 * Whether a value is the detail of a `pool-trim` event line (spec 25 M1.8): a known reason and a
 * finite `freedMb`.
 *
 * @param value - The detail.
 * @returns Whether it is a pool trim.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * isPoolTrimDetail({ reason: "rest", freedMb: 41.5 }); // true
 * ```
 */
export function isPoolTrimDetail(value: unknown): value is PoolTrimDetail;

/**
 * Whether a value is the detail of a `shader` event line (E4): a string `what` (a newer engine's
 * word included), a label or null, finite `ms` and `frame`, a boolean `boot`, and the pass it ran
 * during (`pass`, `owner` numbers or null; `filter`, `view` strings or null).
 *
 * @param value - The detail.
 * @returns Whether it is a shader compile.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * isShaderDetail({ what: "compile", label: null, ms: 3, frame: 4851, boot: false }); // false: no `during`
 * ```
 */
export function isShaderDetail(value: unknown): value is ShaderEventDetail;

/**
 * Whether a value is the detail of a `problem` event line (N3): a string `rule` (a newer engine's
 * rule included) with an owner and a view, then either `cleared: true`, or a severity, a filter,
 * the numbers `value`, `threshold`, `since`, `frames` (each a number or null) and an optional
 * string `reason` (`filter-still`'s `budget` / `not-eligible`, `target-churn`'s `rate` / `idle` /
 * `after-trim`, a newer engine's word).
 *
 * @param value - The detail.
 * @returns Whether it is a problem.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * isProblemDetail({ rule: "filter-still", cleared: true, owner: 412, view: "fogLayer" }); // true
 * ```
 */
export function isProblemDetail(value: unknown): value is ProblemEventDetail;

/**
 * Whether a value is the detail of a `gc` event line (N6): a finite `freedMb`, the heap after it
 * (a number or null) and a boolean `hint`.
 *
 * @param value - The detail.
 * @returns Whether it is a GC.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * isGcDetail({ freedMb: 4.2, heapMb: 41.9, hint: true }); // true
 * ```
 */
export function isGcDetail(value: unknown): value is GcEventDetail;

/**
 * Whether a value is the detail of a `sections` event line (N1): `on` and `off` lists of section
 * names. A name the editor does not know (a newer engine's section) is a string here; the reader
 * keeps the names it knows.
 *
 * @param value - The detail.
 * @returns Whether it has the shape.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * isSectionsDetail({ on: ["passes"], off: [] }); // true
 * ```
 */
export function isSectionsDetail(
  value: unknown
): value is { readonly on: readonly string[]; readonly off: readonly string[] };

/**
 * Whether a value is the detail of the recorder's own `recorder` event line: a known action and,
 * for a start, who started it (`by`, absent from an older recorder).
 *
 * @param value - The detail.
 * @returns Whether it is a recorder action.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * isRecorderDetail({ action: "start", label: "boss", by: "agent", name: "Claude" }); // true
 * ```
 */
export function isRecorderDetail(value: unknown): value is {
  readonly action: "start" | "stop" | "export";
  readonly by?: string | null;
};

/**
 * What this page's engine and build measure (spec 03 Delta 2026-10-16 D2), from the ring, the header
 * and the monitor, read structurally once per header (each column tested once with
 * `ArrayBuffer.isView` / `Array.isArray` and its length, so the read loop branches on cached
 * booleans only). `passDraws` also needs `draws` in the header's `measured`: the engine writes the
 * `drawsAt` column on every backend but counts draws only where it measures them (WebGPU), so a
 * WebGL page's column is all 0. `shaderEvents` is true on an engine with the pass ring's 0.15.x
 * columns or `systemNames` (the release that sends `shader` lines); a seen `shader`, `problem`,
 * `gc` or `passes` line turns its capability on later (perf's reader). Never throws; allocates its
 * answer.
 *
 * @param ring - `monitor.frames()` (any value).
 * @param header - The newest header line, or undefined before one.
 * @param monitor - `renderer.monitor` (any value).
 * @returns The capabilities.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * capsOf({ passes: { capacity: 4096 } }, undefined, undefined).passDraws; // false: an engine before 0.15.x
 * ```
 */
export function capsOf(
  ring: unknown,
  header: PerfHeaderLine | undefined,
  monitor: unknown
): PerfCaps;
~~~

#### `frames.ts`

~~~ts
/**
 * The systems kept per frame: the engine's top 5 (`sysIdx` / `sysMs` are rows × 5, −1 = none).
 */
export const SYSTEMS_PER_FRAME = 5;

/**
 * The top 5 systems of each frame row: `names` indexes, `idx` and `ms` are rows × 5, −1 = none.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const systems: PerfSystemsWire = { names: ["ward.update", "fog.render"], idx: [0, 1, -1, -1, -1], ms: [6.2, 1.4, 0, 0, 0] };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfSystemsWire = { names: string[]; idx: number[]; ms: number[] };

/**
 * Pass rows, flat columns; `row` is the index into the frame columns. Owner / filter / draws / format
 * are null when not measured (an engine before the 0.15.x patch).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const passes: PerfPassRowsWire = { row: [0], index: [0], kind: ["canvas"], view: ["main"], owner: [null], filter: [null],
 *   w: [1080], h: [2340], format: ["bgra8unorm"], resolution: [2.6], draws: [41], gpuMs: [3.1] };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfPassRowsWire = {
  row: number[];
  index: number[];
  kind: PassKind[];
  view: (string | null)[];
  owner: (number | null)[];
  filter: (string | null)[];
  w: number[];
  h: number[];
  format: (string | null)[];
  resolution: (number | null)[];
  draws: (number | null)[];
  gpuMs: (number | null)[];
};

/**
 * Window rows after a frame, with the per-frame blocks the feeds switched on (the wire value of
 * `editor.perf.frames { after? }`). Each frame crosses the wire once.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const wire: PerfFramesWire = { v: 1, epoch: "1792000000000.5", t0: 80000, hole: false, gpuTimer: true,
 *   frame: [4855], t: [310.2], ms: [18.4], jsMs: [8.1], gpuMs: [9.6], rateMs: [16.67], budgetMs: [16.67], drawn: [1],
 *   rest: [0], causes: [4], noise: [0], draws: [61],
 *   systems: { names: ["ward.update", "fog.render"], idx: [0, 1, -1, -1, -1], ms: [6.2, 1.4, 0, 0, 0] }, nodes: [20] };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfFramesWire = {
  v: 1;
  /** The page's clock origin (header.timeOrigin) as text; a new value means a new page (reload). */
  epoch: string | null;
  /** Page-clock ms every `t` is relative to (the first row's start, rounded to 0.1). */
  t0: number;
  /** True when `after` was older than the oldest row perf still had: frames are missing before `frame[0]`. */
  hole: boolean;
  gpuTimer: boolean;
  frame: number[];
  t: number[];
  ms: number[];
  jsMs: number[];
  gpuMs: (number | null)[];
  rateMs: number[];
  budgetMs: number[];
  drawn: (0 | 1)[];
  rest: RestState[];
  causes: number[];
  noise: number[];
  /** Draw calls per frame (ring `draws`); absent on WebGL (not counted). */
  draws?: (number | null)[];
  /** feeds.systems and caps.systemNames: the top 5 systems per frame. */
  systems?: PerfSystemsWire;
  /** feeds.nodes: demand marks per frame (ring `marks`). */
  nodes?: number[];
  /** feeds.passes: the pass rows of these frames. */
  passes?: PerfPassRowsWire;
};

/**
 * The wire value of `editor.perf.detail { from, to }`: the rows of a range from the engine's
 * `monitor.detail` (next change), else from perf's own window, else none (`reason: "gone"`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const detail: PerfDetailWire = { v: 1, from: 4810, to: 4860, source: "agent", reason: "no-detail", frames: null, nodes: null };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfDetailWire = {
  v: 1;
  from: number;
  to: number;
  /** Where the rows came from; null when none. */
  source: "engine" | "agent" | null;
  /** Why not the engine's detail: no `monitor.detail` (older engine), refused (build without control), failed, or the frames are gone. */
  reason: "no-detail" | "control" | "failed" | "gone" | null;
  frames: PerfFramesWire | null;
  /** Nodes updated or redrawn, from the engine's mark ring (next change); null otherwise. */
  nodes:
    | {
        entity: number;
        label: string | null;
        how: "mark" | "moved" | "loose" | "invalidate" | "redraw";
        count: number;
      }[]
    | null;
};

/**
 * Checks a frames wire: `v: 1`, an epoch (text or null), a finite `t0`, boolean `hole` and
 * `gpuTimer`; frame columns of one length (at most 65 535 rows) with whole frame numbers, finite
 * numbers, `drawn` 0 or 1 and `rest` a REST value; and each optional block aligned with the rows:
 * `draws` and `nodes` per row, `systems.idx` / `ms` of rows × 5 with indexes inside `names`, pass rows
 * inside the rows and in order with a known kind. The tools page drops a value it refuses and warns
 * once. Pure; answers the value itself, never a copy.
 *
 * @param value - The value read from `editor.perf.frames` (or the frames of a detail answer).
 * @returns The value typed, or undefined.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * readFramesWire({ ...wire, ms: wire.ms.slice(1) }); // undefined: a column one row short
 * ```
 */
export function readFramesWire(value: Json): PerfFramesWire | undefined;
~~~

#### `gpu.ts`

~~~ts
/**
 * The `causes` bit of a GPU over the frame's budget (the engine sets it when the late GPU result
 * lands over `budgetMs`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * app.perf.readWindow(window => (window.noise?.[row] ?? 0) & GPU_BIT); // 4: a faint GPU tick
 * ```
 */
export const GPU_BIT = 1 << CAUSE_BITS.indexOf("gpu");

/**
 * Whether a row's GPU was a lone outlier: over its budget, not sustained, so not counted (the faint
 * GPU tick of the graph). False for a window without the `noise` column (an agent before item 8).
 *
 * @param window - The window.
 * @param row - A row.
 * @returns Whether the row's GPU is noise.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * isGpuNoise(window, 290); // true: 22 ms on one frame, 0.5 ms around it
 * ```
 */
export function isGpuNoise(window: PerfWindowView, row: number): boolean;

/**
 * Counts every sustained GPU of the window: a GPU over budget on 2 of 3 consecutive drawn frames
 * (frames not drawn are skipped), both frames. A row's GPU is never uncounted again, so a spike
 * stays a spike after its partner left the window. Run after the late GPU results landed, so the
 * second over-budget result promotes the first. Allocation-free: one pass, two row indices.
 *
 * @param window - The window; rows with an uncounted GPU hold it in `noise`.
 * @returns Whether a row changed.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * promoteSustainedGpu(window); // true: rows 40 and 42 both 20 ms, both now gpu spikes
 * ```
 */
export function promoteSustainedGpu(window: PerfWindow): boolean;

/**
 * Sorts the first `count` values of a scratch in place, ascending: the unused tail is filled with
 * +Infinity first, so one whole-array sort (no comparator, no copy) leaves them at the start.
 * Allocation-free.
 *
 * @param sorted - The scratch; its first `count` values are the ones to sort.
 * @param count - Values in use.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const scratch = Float64Array.of(3, 1, 9, 9);
 * sortHead(scratch, 2); // scratch: 1, 3, Infinity, Infinity
 * ```
 */
export function sortHead(sorted: Float64Array, count: number): void;

/**
 * The value at a nearest-rank percentile of the first `count` sorted values.
 *
 * @param sorted - Ascending values (`sortHead`).
 * @param count - Values in use.
 * @param fraction - The percentile, 0..1.
 * @returns The value; NaN without values.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * nearestRank(Float64Array.of(1, 2, 3, 4), 4, 0.5); // 2
 * ```
 */
export function nearestRank(sorted: Float64Array, count: number, fraction: number): number;

/**
 * Writes the window's headline GPU: the p50 and p90 (nearest rank) of the GPU times of its drawn
 * frames with a measured GPU, NaN without one (no GPU timer). Allocation-free: sorts in the
 * window's own scratch (`sorted`).
 *
 * @param window - The window.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * spreadGpu(window);
 * window.gpuP50Ms; // 0.49
 * window.gpuP90Ms; // 0.61: one 22 ms outlier moves neither
 * ```
 */
export function spreadGpu(window: PerfWindow): void;
~~~

#### `history.ts`

~~~ts
/** The history's span, ms: owner item 25, "about 2 min". */
export const HISTORY_MS = 120_000;

/** Frame rows held at most: 120 s × 120 fps. */
export const HISTORY_ROWS = 14_400;

/** Pass rows held at most: 4 per frame, like the engine ring. */
export const HISTORY_PASS_ROWS = 57_600;

/** Timeline events held at most: 2 min with room for a shader burst at boot. */
export const HISTORY_EVENTS = 1024;

/** Per-second pass summaries (and samples) held at most: one per second. */
export const HISTORY_SECONDS = 120;

/** Holes (frames or events missing after a frame or a seq) held at most; the oldest drop first. */
export const HISTORY_HOLES = 256;

/**
 * The tools page's history of one source, oldest row at index 0 of every column. Frame columns hold
 * `count` rows, pass columns `passCount`, `events` `eventCount`, `seconds` `secondCount`, `samples`
 * `sampleCount`, `holes` `holeCount`, `eventHoles` `eventHoleCount`. A number that was not measured
 * is NaN in a float column (null on the wire). The pass texts (view, filter, format) are ids into
 * `passNames` (0: none) and the pass kind an index into `PASS_KINDS`, so the pass columns are typed
 * arrays: about 3 MB in all, allocated once. A new `epoch` (a reload) or another source clears it;
 * `version` is bumped on every change, so painters and selections key on it.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const history = createPerfHistory();
 * appendFrames(history, framesWire); // the editor.perf.frames answer, checked by readFramesWire
 * history.passNames[history.passView[0] ?? 0]; // "main": the first pass row's view
 * PASS_KINDS[history.passKind[0] ?? 0]; // "canvas"
 * ```
 */
export type PerfHistory = {
  /** Frame rows held at most (HISTORY_ROWS). */
  readonly capacity: number;
  /** Frame rows held. */
  count: number;
  /** The page's clock origin of the rows (the feeds' `epoch`); null before the first rows. */
  epoch: string | null;
  /** Bumped whenever rows, pass rows, events, seconds, samples or holes change. */
  version: number;
  /** The newest frames wire's `gpuTimer`: false on iOS, every gpuMs is then NaN. */
  gpuTimer: boolean;

  /** Frame number of each row. */
  readonly frame: Uint32Array;
  /** Page-clock ms of each frame's start (the wire's `t0 + t`). */
  readonly t: Float64Array;
  readonly ms: Float32Array;
  readonly jsMs: Float32Array;
  /** NaN: not measured. */
  readonly gpuMs: Float32Array;
  readonly rateMs: Float32Array;
  readonly budgetMs: Float32Array;
  /** 1: the renderer drew the frame. */
  readonly drawn: Uint8Array;
  /** REST values (awake, idle, woke, break). */
  readonly rest: Uint8Array;
  /** Cause bits in CAUSE_BITS order (the agent's counted bits; unknown bits dropped). */
  readonly causes: Uint8Array;
  /** Cause bits heard but not counted (`GPU_BIT`: a faint GPU tick). */
  readonly noise: Uint8Array;
  /** Draw calls; NaN: not counted (WebGL, or the feed sent none). */
  readonly draws: Float32Array;
  /** Top 5 systems per row (rows × SYSTEMS_PER_FRAME): indexes into `systemNames`; −1: none. */
  readonly sysIdx: Int16Array;
  /** Their ms (rows × SYSTEMS_PER_FRAME). */
  readonly sysMs: Float32Array;
  /** The source's system names by the index `sysIdx` holds, merged by name from each wire's names. */
  readonly systemNames: string[];
  /** Demand marks per row; −1: not sent (feeds.nodes off). */
  readonly nodes: Int32Array;

  /** Pass rows held at most (HISTORY_PASS_ROWS). */
  readonly passCapacity: number;
  /** Pass rows held, in frame order. */
  passCount: number;
  /** The frame number each pass row belongs to. */
  readonly passFrame: Uint32Array;
  readonly passIndex: Uint8Array;
  /** The pass kind: an index into PASS_KINDS. */
  readonly passKind: Uint8Array;
  /** The view label: an id into `passNames`; 0: none. */
  readonly passView: Uint16Array;
  /** The owner entity; 0: none or not measured. */
  readonly passOwner: Uint32Array;
  /** The filter kind's name: an id into `passNames`; 0: not a filter or not measured. */
  readonly passFilter: Uint16Array;
  readonly passW: Uint16Array;
  readonly passH: Uint16Array;
  /** The target format: an id into `passNames`; 0: not measured. */
  readonly passFormat: Uint16Array;
  /** NaN: not measured. */
  readonly passResolution: Float32Array;
  /** NaN: not counted. */
  readonly passDraws: Float32Array;
  /** NaN: not measured. */
  readonly passGpuMs: Float32Array;
  /**
   * The pass texts by id: index 0 is null ("none"). Grows with each new name; when its 65 536 ids are
   * used up, the names no held pass row uses are dropped and the ids renumbered (a long session).
   */
  readonly passNames: (string | null)[];

  /** Frame numbers after which frames are missing (a stall longer than the agent's window), oldest first. */
  readonly holes: Uint32Array;
  /** Holes held. */
  holeCount: number;

  /** Timeline events, oldest first. */
  readonly events: (PerfTimelineEvent | undefined)[];
  /** Events held. */
  eventCount: number;
  /** The events feed's `next` of the newest answer: the `after` of the next read; undefined before. */
  eventsNext: number | undefined;
  /** Seqs after which the agent's ring overwrote events before they were read (`lost`), oldest first. */
  readonly eventHoles: Uint32Array;
  /** Event holes held. */
  eventHoleCount: number;

  /** Per-second pass summaries (`editor.perf.passes`), oldest first. */
  readonly seconds: (PerfPassesSummary | undefined)[];
  /** Summaries held. */
  secondCount: number;
  /**
   * The source's per-second samples (`editor.perf.second`'s `sample`), oldest first: the per-second
   * systems a range falls back on when its rows carry no top 5 (an engine without `systemNames`).
   */
  readonly samples: (PerfSampleLine | undefined)[];
  /** Samples held. */
  sampleCount: number;

  /** The index of each name of `systemNames` (the interning table). */
  readonly systemIds: Map<string, number>;
