  /** The id of each name of `passNames` (the interning table). */
  readonly passNameIds: Map<string, number>;
};

/**
 * What one `appendFrames` did: rows added, whether a hole was recorded, whether a new epoch cleared
 * the history first.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const appended: AppendResult = { added: 120, hole: false, reset: false };
 * ```
 */
export type AppendResult = {
  readonly added: number;
  readonly hole: boolean;
  readonly reset: boolean;
};

/**
 * One system over a range: total ms, its share of the range's summed JS, its largest frame.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const system: RangeSystem = { name: "ward.update", totalMs: 312.4, share: 0.41, maxMs: 9.1 };
 * ```
 */
export type RangeSystem = {
  readonly name: string;
  readonly totalMs: number;
  readonly share: number;
  readonly maxMs: number;
};

/**
 * One pass kind and view over a range: how often it ran, its GPU ms in total, its share of the
 * range's pass GPU.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const pass: RangePass = { kind: "filter", view: "fogLayer", count: 102, gpuMs: 316.2, share: 0.58 };
 * ```
 */
export type RangePass = {
  readonly kind: PassKind;
  readonly view: string | null;
  readonly count: number;
  readonly gpuMs: number | null;
  readonly share: number | null;
};

/**
 * One filter chain over a range.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const chain: RangeChain = { owner: 412, view: "fogLayer", kinds: ["fog.blur", "fog.blur"], applies: 102, gpuMs: 316.2 };
 * ```
 */
export type RangeChain = {
  readonly owner: number | null;
  readonly view: string | null;
  readonly kinds: readonly string[];
  readonly applies: number;
  readonly gpuMs: number | null;
};

/**
 * What a range selection holds (D10 `rangeSummary`): its frames and seconds, the worst frame, the
 * systems (from the per-frame top 5, or prorated from the seconds' `sample.systems` with
 * `systemsPerSecond`), spikes, GCs, rate changes, shader compiles, passes and filter chains (from
 * the pass rows, or the seconds' chains with `passesPerSecond`), demand marks and the holes inside.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const summary: PerfRangeSummary = { from: 4810, to: 4860, frames: 51, durationMs: 850.2, seconds: 1, worstMs: 41.3, jsMs: 762.1,
 *   systems: [{ name: "ward.update", totalMs: 312.4, share: 0.41, maxMs: 9.1 }], systemsPerSecond: false,
 *   spikes: [{ frame: 4851, cause: "compile", ms: 41.3 }], gcs: [{ frame: 4818, t: 79102, freedMb: 4.2 }],
 *   rates: [{ frame: 4855, from: 120, to: 60, reason: "missed" }],
 *   compiles: [{ frame: 4851, what: "compile", label: "fog.blur", ms: 38.2, boot: false }],
 *   passes: [], chains: [], passesPerSecond: false, nodes: 420, holes: [] };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfRangeSummary = {
  readonly from: number;
  readonly to: number;
  /** Frames of the range the history holds. */
  readonly frames: number;
  /** Page-clock ms from the first frame's start to the last frame's end. */
  readonly durationMs: number;
  /** Per-second summaries inside the range. */
  readonly seconds: number;
  readonly worstMs: number | null;
  /** The range's summed JS ms, the base of every system's share. */
  readonly jsMs: number;
  readonly systems: readonly RangeSystem[];
  /** The systems are prorated from the seconds (no per-frame top 5 in the rows). */
  readonly systemsPerSecond: boolean;
  readonly spikes: readonly {
    readonly frame: number;
    readonly cause: PerfCause;
    readonly ms: number;
  }[];
  readonly gcs: readonly {
    readonly frame: number | null;
    readonly t: number;
    readonly freedMb: number;
  }[];
  readonly rates: readonly {
    readonly frame: number | null;
    readonly from: number;
    readonly to: number;
    readonly reason: RateReason;
  }[];
  readonly compiles: readonly {
    readonly frame: number;
    readonly what: ShaderWhat;
    readonly label: string | null;
    readonly ms: number | null;
    readonly boot: boolean;
  }[];
  readonly passes: readonly RangePass[];
  readonly chains: readonly RangeChain[];
  /** The passes and chains come from the seconds' summaries (no pass rows in the range). */
  readonly passesPerSecond: boolean;
  /** Demand marks summed over the range; null when no row carried them. */
  readonly nodes: number | null;
  /** Hole frames inside the range. */
  readonly holes: readonly number[];
};

/**
 * Allocates an empty history: every column at its full capacity, once (about 3 MB). The `append*`
 * functions write into it without allocating.
 *
 * @returns The empty history.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const history = createPerfHistory();
 * history.capacity; // 14400
 * history.epoch; // null
 * ```
 */
export function createPerfHistory(): PerfHistory;

/**
 * Empties the history without reallocating (a source switch, a reload): every count to 0, no
 * epoch, the system and pass names forgotten, the kept events, seconds and samples released,
 * `version` bumped.
 *
 * @param history - The history.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * clearPerfHistory(history);
 * history.count; // 0, the same 14 400-row columns kept
 * ```
 */
export function clearPerfHistory(history: PerfHistory): void;

/**
 * Appends a frames wire (D10): a different `epoch` clears first (`reset`); rows with a `frame` at or
 * below the newest kept are skipped (dedup); `hole` or a frame jump records a hole after the newest
 * held frame; past capacity or older than HISTORY_MS the oldest rows drop with their pass rows
 * (`copyWithin`, no allocation); the pass rows of the new frames follow; `version` is bumped when
 * rows changed. Allocates nothing per row: names are interned once.
 *
 * @param history - The history.
 * @param wire - A checked frames wire (`readFramesWire`).
 * @returns What the append did.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * appendFrames(history, framesWire); // { added: 120, hole: false, reset: false } at 120 fps, once a second
 * ```
 */
export function appendFrames(history: PerfHistory, wire: PerfFramesWire): AppendResult;

/**
 * Appends an events wire by `seq` (D10): its lines become marks here (`eventsOf`: the agent sends
 * them raw); a different epoch clears first; events at or below the newest seq seen are skipped
 * (dedup); `lost` records a hole after the newest held event; past HISTORY_EVENTS the oldest drop;
 * `next` is kept as the next read's `after`.
 *
 * @param history - The history.
 * @param wire - The events wire.
 * @returns The events added.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * appendEvents(history, eventsWire); // 2: a GC and a rate change since the last read
 * history.eventsNext; // the `after` of the next editor.perf.events read
 * ```
 */
export function appendEvents(history: PerfHistory, wire: PerfEventsWire): number;

/**
 * Appends a second of `editor.perf.passes` by `t` (dedup), kept as its summary (`passesSummaryOf`:
 * the chains are built here, the agent sends raw rows): a second at or before the newest held is
 * skipped; past HISTORY_SECONDS the oldest drops.
 *
 * @param history - The history.
 * @param passes - The `editor.perf.passes` value.
 * @returns True when it was added, false for a second the history has.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * appendSecond(history, passes); // true once per second, false for the same watched value again
 * ```
 */
export function appendSecond(history: PerfHistory, passes: PerfPassesWire): boolean;

/**
 * Appends a per-second sample (`editor.perf.second`'s `sample`) by its frame (dedup): the source of
 * the per-second systems a range falls back on (an engine without `systemNames`). A sample at or
 * before the newest held frame is skipped; past HISTORY_SECONDS the oldest drops.
 *
 * @param history - The history.
 * @param sample - The sample line.
 * @returns True when it was added, false for a sample the history has.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * if (second.sample !== null) appendSample(history, second.sample); // true once per second
 * ```
 */
export function appendSample(history: PerfHistory, sample: PerfSampleLine): boolean;

/**
 * The row indexes of the held frames in `[from, to]` (either way round).
 *
 * @param history - The history.
 * @param from - The first frame of the range.
 * @param to - The last frame of the range (inclusive).
 * @returns The first and last row; `{ first: -1, last: -1 }` when no frame of the range is held.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * rangeRows(history, 4810, 4860); // { first: 10, last: 58 } with frames 4841 and 4842 missing
 * ```
 */
export function rangeRows(
  history: PerfHistory,
  from: number,
  to: number
): { readonly first: number; readonly last: number };

/**
 * The summary of a range selection (D10; allocates once per selection): its frames, duration,
 * overlapping seconds and worst frame; the systems from the rows' per-frame top 5, else prorated from
 * the samples' per-second systems (`systemsPerSecond`); spikes with their primary cause; the GCs,
 * rate changes and shader compiles of the timeline; passes and filter chains from the pass rows, else
 * the seconds' chains prorated (`passesPerSecond`); demand marks summed; the holes inside.
 *
 * @param history - The history.
 * @param from - The first frame of the range.
 * @param to - The last frame of the range (inclusive; either way round).
 * @returns The summary.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const summary = rangeSummary(history, 4810, 4860);
 * summary.systems[0]; // { name: "ward.update", totalMs: 306.7, share: 0.782, maxMs: 9.1 }
 * summary.systemsPerSecond; // false: the rows carried the top 5
 * ```
 */
export function rangeSummary(history: PerfHistory, from: number, to: number): PerfRangeSummary;
~~~

#### `memory.ts`

~~~ts
/**
 * Equal consecutive heap samples (while the window had awake frames) after which a counter is
 * frozen, not flat.
 */
export const FROZEN_SAMPLES = 20;

/**
 * The page's memory as far as this page can tell, and whether to believe it.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const desktop: PerfMemory = { heapMb: 41.9, source: "performance.memory", trusted: true, why: null, processMb: null };
 * const a26: PerfMemory = { heapMb: 10.68, source: "performance.memory", trusted: false, why: "webview", processMb: null };
 * const iphone: PerfMemory = { heapMb: null, source: null, trusted: false, why: "not-measured", processMb: null };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfMemory = {
  readonly heapMb: number | null;
  /**
   * Where the heap number comes from: the engine's `memory.source` when it says (next change, N6:
   * `"uasm"` is `measureUserAgentSpecificMemory`), else `"performance.memory"` for a heap number.
   */
  readonly source: "performance.memory" | "uasm" | "shell" | null;
  /** True only for a heap number this page can stand behind (the D6 rule). */
  readonly trusted: boolean;
  /** Why not trusted: a WebView (frozen on Android), a counter that has not moved for FROZEN_SAMPLES samples, or none. */
  readonly why: "webview" | "frozen" | "not-measured" | null;
  /** The native shell's whole-process memory (ask to `@moku-labs/native`); never shown as heap. null until it exists. */
  readonly processMb: number | null;
};

/**
 * Why the page's heap is not trusted (D6): no heap number → "not-measured" (iOS, WebKit); a WebView
 * → "webview" (frozen on Android, the A26 finding); the same value in FROZEN_SAMPLES consecutive
 * samples → "frozen" (a quantized desktop counter); otherwise null (trusted). Pure.
 *
 * @param heapMb - The newest sample's heapMb.
 * @param webview - `header.device.webview` (non-null on a native WebView).
 * @param sameSamples - Consecutive samples, this one included, with this same heapMb while the
 *   window had awake frames.
 * @returns The reason, or null when the heap is trusted.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * memoryWhy(41.9, null, 20); // "frozen": twenty samples of one value on a desktop page
 * memoryWhy(10.68, "141", 1); // "webview": never the device's heap
 * ```
 */
export function memoryWhy(
  heapMb: number | null,
  webview: string | null,
  sameSamples: number
): PerfMemory["why"];
~~~

#### `passes.ts`

~~~ts
/**
 * Pass rows the agent's pass window keeps per frame of its window: the engine ring's own bound
 * (4 passes per frame of capacity, TC §2.1).
 */
export const PASS_ROWS_PER_FRAME = 4;

/**
 * The pass kinds the editor knows, in the order the tools page's history stores them as a byte
 * (`PerfHistory.passKind`): the engine's `PassKind` union. A type-level test fails when the engine
 * adds a kind this list does not have (`readFramesWire` refuses a kind it does not know).
 */
export const PASS_KINDS = ["canvas", "texture", "filter"] as const satisfies readonly PassKind[];

/**
 * One pass of a frame as the passes panel lists it: `gpuMs` is the pass's own reading; `share` is its
 * part of the frame's summed pass GPU (the number a tile GPU shows), null without a GPU timer.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const pass: PassRowWire = { index: 0, kind: "canvas", view: "main", owner: null, filter: null, w: 1080, h: 2340,
 *   format: "bgra8unorm", resolution: 2.6, draws: 41, gpuMs: 3.1, share: 0.3 };
 * ```
 */
export type PassRowWire = {
  index: number;
  kind: PassKind;
  view: string | null;
  owner: number | null;
  filter: string | null;
  w: number;
  h: number;
  format: string | null;
  resolution: number | null;
  draws: number | null;
  gpuMs: number | null;
  share: number | null;
};

/**
 * One filter chain over a second: consecutive filter passes of one frame with the same owner (or,
 * without owners, the same label), their interned kind names in order, applies, megapixels, draws,
 * GPU ms over the frames and the chain's mean share of the frame's pass GPU.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const chain: PassChainSummary = { owner: 412, view: "fogLayer", kinds: ["fog.blur", "fog.blur"], applies: 120, mpx: 221.2, draws: 4,
 *   gpuMs: { p50: 6.2, max: 6.9 }, share: 0.6 };
 * ```
 */
export type PassChainSummary = {
  owner: number | null;
  view: string | null;
  kinds: string[];
  applies: number;
  mpx: number;
  draws: number | null;
  gpuMs: { p50: number; max: number } | null;
  share: number | null;
};

/**
 * The GPU passes of a second as the passes panel shows them, and the heaviest drawn frame's pass
 * list: what `passesSummaryOf` builds on the tools page from an `editor.perf.passes` answer. `gpuMs`
 * of a pass on a tile GPU (Mali, Adreno, Apple, PowerVR) is a share of the frame, never a ranking:
 * `tiler: true` tells the reader to show `share` (TC §1e).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const passes: PerfPassesSummary = { v: 1, source: "agent", t: 81000, frames: 60, tiler: true, gpuTimer: true,
 *   chains: [{ owner: 412, view: "fogLayer", kinds: ["fog.blur", "fog.blur"], applies: 120, mpx: 221.2, draws: 4,
 *     gpuMs: { p50: 6.2, max: 6.9 }, share: 0.6 }],
 *   heaviest: { frame: 4852, passes: [{ index: 0, kind: "canvas", view: "main", owner: null, filter: null, w: 1080, h: 2340,
 *     format: "bgra8unorm", resolution: 2.6, draws: 41, gpuMs: 3.1, share: 0.3 }] },
 *   shaders: null, targets: { created: 6, destroyed: 6 }, lost: 0 };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfPassesSummary = {
  v: 1;
  /** "engine": from the engine's `passes` line (next change); "agent": from perf's pass rows (0.15.x). */
  source: "engine" | "agent";
  /** Page-clock ms of the end of the second. */
  t: number;
  /** Drawn frames in the second. */
  frames: number;
  tiler: boolean;
  gpuTimer: boolean;
  chains: PassChainSummary[];
  heaviest: { frame: number; passes: PassRowWire[] } | null;
  /** sample.shaders of the second (next change); null before. */
  shaders: {
    pipelines: number;
    hits: number;
    compiles: number;
    variants: number;
    relinks: number;
  } | null;
  /** sample.targets (0.15.x patch); null before. */
  targets: { created: number; destroyed: number } | null;
  /** Passes the engine's ring overwrote before perf read them, since start. */
  lost: number;
};

/**
 * The engine's per-second `passes` line (N4, next change) as the wire carries it: the line's chains
 * and heaviest frame, arrays plain (Json).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const line: PassesLineWire = { t: 1_792_000_081_000, heaviest: null,
 *   chains: [{ owner: 412, view: "fogLayer", kinds: ["fog.blur"], applies: 60, mpx: 37.9, draws: 1, gpuMs: { p50: 3, max: 3.4 } }] };
 * ```
 */
export type PassesLineWire = {
  t: number;
  chains: {
    owner: number | null;
    view: string | null;
    kinds: string[];
    applies: number;
    mpx: number;
    draws: number | null;
    gpuMs: { p50: number; max: number } | null;
  }[];
  heaviest: {
    frame: number;
    passes: {
      index: number;
      kind: PassKind;
      label: string | null;
      stencil: boolean | null;
      w: number;
      h: number;
      gpuMs: number | null;
    }[];
  } | null;
};

/**
 * The wire value of `editor.perf.passes` (owner 2026-10-16: the agent sends raw rows, the tools
 * page builds the chains): the newest full second, either the pass rows perf read of its drawn
 * frames and its heaviest drawn frame (`source: "agent"`, 0.15.x), or the engine's own `passes` line
 * as it came (`source: "engine"`, next change). `passesSummaryOf` turns it into the panel's summary.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const wire: PerfPassesWire = { v: 1, source: "agent", t: 81000, frames: 60, tiler: true, gpuTimer: true,
 *   rows: { row: [0], index: [0], kind: ["canvas"], view: ["main"], owner: [null], filter: [null], w: [1080], h: [2340],
 *     format: [null], resolution: [null], draws: [41], gpuMs: [3.1] },
 *   heaviest: { frame: 4852, row: 0 }, line: null, shaders: null, targets: { created: 6, destroyed: 6 }, lost: 0 };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfPassesWire = {
  v: 1;
  source: "engine" | "agent";
  /** Page-clock ms of the end of the second. */
  t: number;
  /** Drawn frames in the second. */
  frames: number;
  tiler: boolean;
  gpuTimer: boolean;
  /** source "agent": the pass rows of the second, `row` the index of the frame among its frames; null for "engine". */
  rows: PerfPassRowsWire | null;
  /** source "agent": the heaviest drawn frame and its row among the second's frames; null when none. */
  heaviest: { frame: number; row: number } | null;
  /** source "engine": the engine's `passes` line as sent; null for "agent". */
  line: PassesLineWire | null;
  /** sample.shaders of the second (next change); null before. */
  shaders: PerfPassesSummary["shaders"];
  /** sample.targets (0.15.x patch); null before. */
  targets: PerfPassesSummary["targets"];
  /** Passes the engine's ring overwrote before perf read them, since start. */
  lost: number;
};

/**
 * How a chain walk reads pass rows in order, whatever stores them (a wire's columns, the history's
 * interned columns): the frame each row belongs to, its index, whether it is a filter pass, its
 * owner (0: none) and its view (compared with `===`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const reader: ChainReader = { count: rows.row.length, frame: pass => rows.row[pass] ?? -1, index: pass => rows.index[pass] ?? -1,
 *   isFilter: pass => rows.kind[pass] === "filter", owner: pass => rows.owner[pass] ?? 0, view: pass => rows.view[pass] ?? null };
 * ```
 */
export type ChainReader = {
  readonly count: number;
  frame(pass: number): number;
  index(pass: number): number;
  isFilter(pass: number): boolean;
  owner(pass: number): number;
  view(pass: number): number | string | null;
};

/**
 * Walks pass rows in order and calls `visit` once per filter chain (D5): consecutive filter passes
 * of one frame with the same owner (or, without owners, the same view) at consecutive indexes; a
 * pass of another kind ends a chain. Allocates nothing itself.
 *
 * @param reader - The pass rows.
 * @param visit - Called with the chain's first pass and the pass after its last.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * walkChains(reader, (first, end) => console.info(end - first)); // 3 for fog.blur, fog.blur, colorMatrix of owner 412
 * ```
 */
export function walkChains(reader: ChainReader, visit: (first: number, end: number) => void): void;

/**
 * The filter chains of pass rows (D5): consecutive filter passes of one frame (`row`) with the same
 * owner, or without owners the same view, in index order (`walkChains`), summed over the rows'
 * frames by owner, view and kinds: `kinds` the filter names (an unnamed filter of an engine before
 * the patch is "filter"), `applies` the passes, `mpx` w × h / 1e6 summed, `draws` per frame (null
 * without a draw count), `gpuMs` p50 and max over the frames (null without a GPU timer), `share` the
 * mean of the chain's part of its frame's summed pass GPU, rounded to 0.05. Heaviest first (GPU, then
 * megapixels). Pure; allocates its answer.
 *
 * @param rows - The pass rows of the second.
 * @returns The chains, heaviest first.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * chainsOf(rows)[0]?.kinds; // ["fog.blur", "fog.blur", "colorMatrix"]: owner 412's filters, one chain
 * ```
 */
export function chainsOf(rows: PerfPassRowsWire): PassChainSummary[];

/**
 * Whether the page's GPU is a tile GPU: `header.gpu.vendor`, `architecture` or `renderer` names arm,
 * mali, qualcomm, adreno, apple, imagination or powervr (a case-insensitive word match, so "Mali-G68"
 * is one and "charming" is not). False for null. On a tile GPU a pass's own GPU ms is a share of
 * the frame, never a ranking (TC §1e).
 *
 * @param gpu - The header's gpu, or null.
 * @returns True for a tile GPU.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * isTilerGpu({ backend: "webgpu", vendor: "arm", architecture: "valhall", renderer: null, timer: "timestamp-query" }); // true
 * ```
 */
export function isTilerGpu(gpu: PerfHeaderLine["gpu"] | null): boolean;

/**
 * A pass's share of its frame's summed pass GPU ms, within 0..1 and rounded to 0.05 (one cell of the
 * UI); null without a measured frame GPU.
 *
 * @param passMs - The pass's GPU ms.
 * @param frameMs - The frame's summed pass GPU ms.
 * @returns The share, 0 to 1, or null.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * gpuShare(1, 3); // 0.35
 * ```
 */
export function gpuShare(passMs: number, frameMs: number): number | null;

/**
 * The passes panel's summary of an `editor.perf.passes` answer (the tools page's side of D5): the
 * engine's line as sent when the agent passed one on, else the filter chains of the agent's pass rows
 * (`chainsOf`) and the heaviest drawn frame's passes with their GPU shares; the second's facts as
 * they came. Pure; allocates its answer.
 *
 * @param wire - An `editor.perf.passes` answer.
 * @returns The summary.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * passesSummaryOf(wire).chains[0]?.kinds; // ["fog.blur", "fog.blur"]
 * ```
 */
export function passesSummaryOf(wire: PerfPassesWire): PerfPassesSummary;
~~~

#### `sections.ts`

~~~ts
/**
 * The engine's monitoring sections, in the engine's order (TC §2.7); `engine-contract.test.ts`
 * asserts it equals the engine's `MONITOR_SECTIONS` when the engine exports it (ask E7, next change).
 */
export const MONITOR_SECTIONS = [
  "gpu",
  "passes",
  "shaders",
  "problems",
  "memory",
  "systems",
  "nodes",
  "longFrames"
] as const;

/**
 * One monitoring section of the engine.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const section: MonitorSectionName = "passes";
 * ```
 */
export type MonitorSectionName = (typeof MONITOR_SECTIONS)[number];

/**
 * The engine's sections on or off (TC §2.7, `monitor.sections()`), the mirror of the engine's
 * `MonitorSections` (next change, N1).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const sections: MonitorSections = { ...SECTION_DEFAULTS, passes: true };
 * ```
 */
export type MonitorSections = Readonly<Record<MonitorSectionName, boolean>>;

/**
 * The engine's defaults (owner 2026-10-16: "defaults as the engine proposes"): passes, shaders,
 * nodes and all systems off.
 */
export const SECTION_DEFAULTS: MonitorSections = {
  gpu: true,
  passes: false,
  shaders: false,
  problems: true,
  memory: true,
  systems: true,
  nodes: false,
  longFrames: true
};

/**
 * What perf itself reads and sends (its own cost), independent of the engine's sections: the pass
 * window, the top 5 systems per frame and the demand marks per frame. Initialised from perf's flat
 * config (`feedPasses`, `feedSystems`, `feedNodes`), switched by `editor.perf.sections`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const feeds: PerfFeeds = { passes: false, systems: true, nodes: false };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfFeeds = {
  readonly passes: boolean;
  readonly systems: boolean;
  readonly nodes: boolean;
};

/**
 * The Monitoring popover's data: which sections are on (the engine's, when it can switch), what perf
 * reads, and the measured cost. "systems: true" means the top 5 per frame; all systems is the
 * engine's next change (sysAll).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const state: PerfMonitorState = { engine: true, sections: { ...SECTION_DEFAULTS, passes: true }, feeds: { passes: true, systems: true, nodes: false },
 *   costMs: { gpu: 0.01, passes: 0.01, problems: 0.004, memory: 0.005, systems: 0.04, longFrames: 0 }, monitorMs: 0.21, editorMs: 0.12, overdraw: false };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfMonitorState = {
  /** The engine has `monitor.sections` (next change). False: `sections` mirrors SECTION_DEFAULTS and only `feeds` switch. */
  readonly engine: boolean;
  readonly sections: MonitorSections;
  readonly feeds: PerfFeeds;
  /** sample.sectionsMs: ms per drawn frame per section, page clock (next change); null before. */
  readonly costMs: Readonly<Partial<Record<MonitorSectionName, number>>> | null;
  /** sample.monitorMs (exists): the listeners' cost of the second. */
  readonly monitorMs: number | null;
  /** perf's own read and feed time per second, ms (measured around readTick with the monitor's clock; an EMA). */
  readonly editorMs: number | null;
  /**
   * The overdraw heat map is on (header `debug.overdraw` and the `debug` event, engine U6, RE1);
   * null on an engine that does not report it.
   */
  readonly overdraw: boolean | null;
};
~~~

#### `timeline.ts`

~~~ts
/**
 * What a `shader` event compiled, in 0.15.x (E4): `"compile"` or `"module"`; `"variant"` and
 * `"relink"` arrive with the next change. `engine-contract.test.ts` asserts it equals the engine's
 * `SHADER_WHATS` (exported from 0.15.1).
 */
export const SHADER_WHATS = ["compile", "module"] as const;

/**
 * The problem rules of 0.15.1 (N3, N10, engine U5), in the engine's order: `filter-still`,
 * `target-churn` and `retakes`; `filter-area`, `late-compile`, `variants` and `pass-budget` come
 * next. `engine-contract.test.ts` asserts it equals the engine's `PROBLEM_RULES`.
 */
export const PROBLEM_RULES = ["filter-still", "target-churn", "retakes"] as const;

/**
 * What a shader event compiled: a known value, or a newer engine's word kept as its string.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const what: ShaderWhat = "module";
 * const newer: ShaderWhat = "relink"; // a next-change engine: shown by name
 * ```
 */
export type ShaderWhat = (typeof SHADER_WHATS)[number] | (string & {});

/**
 * A problem rule: a known rule, or a newer engine's rule kept as its string.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const rule: ProblemRule = "filter-still";
 * ```
 */
export type ProblemRule = (typeof PROBLEM_RULES)[number] | (string & {});

/**
 * The timeline events perf keeps by reference on the agent: the newest 256 (seq % TIMELINE_SLOTS).
 * An `after` older than that answers `lost: true`.
 */
export const TIMELINE_SLOTS = 256;

/**
 * One mark of the timeline, as the tools page draws it. Built only when the events feed is read;
 * `t` is page-clock ms.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const drop: PerfTimelineEvent = { seq: 812, kind: "rate", t: 80310.2, frame: 4855, from: 120, to: 60, mode: "auto", reason: "missed", displayHz: 120 };
 * const gc: PerfTimelineEvent = { seq: 790, kind: "gc", t: 79102.0, frame: 4818, freedMb: 4.2, heapMb: 41.9 };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfTimelineEvent =
  | {
      seq: number;
      kind: "rate";
      t: number;
      frame: number | null;
      from: number;
      to: number;
      mode: RateMode;
      reason: RateReason;
      displayHz: number | null;
    }
  | { seq: number; kind: "display"; t: number; frame: number | null; hz: number }
  | {
      seq: number;
      kind: "shader";
      t: number;
      frame: number;
      what: ShaderWhat;
      label: string | null;
      ms: number | null;
      boot: boolean;
      pass: number | null;
      filter: string | null;
      owner: number | null;
      view: string | null;
    }
  | {
      seq: number;
      kind: "gc";
      t: number;
      frame: number | null;
      freedMb: number;
      heapMb: number | null;
    }
  | {
      seq: number;
      kind: "problem";
      t: number;
      frame: number | null;
      rule: ProblemRule;
      severity: "info" | "warn";
      cleared: boolean;
      owner: number | null;
      view: string | null;
      filter: string | null;
      value: number | null;
      threshold: number | null;
      since: number | null;
      frames: number | null;
      /**
       * Why it opened (engine U5): `filter-still`'s `budget` / `not-eligible`, `target-churn`'s
       * `rate` / `idle` / `after-trim`; null without one or for a clear.
       */
      reason: ProblemReason | null;
    }
  | {
      seq: number;
      kind: "sections";
      t: number;
      frame: number | null;
      on: MonitorSectionName[];
      off: MonitorSectionName[];
    }
  | {
      seq: number;
      kind: "pool-trim";
      t: number;
      frame: number | null;
      reason: "rest" | "scene" | "pause";
      freedMb: number;
    }
  | {
      seq: number;
      kind: "recorder";
      t: number;
      frame: number | null;
      action: "start" | "stop" | "export";
      by: string | null;
    }
  | { seq: number; kind: "mark"; t: number; frame: number | null; label: string; auto: boolean };

/**
 * The wire value of `editor.perf.events` (owner 2026-10-16: the tools page builds the marks): the
 * lines the agent kept from seq `after` on, oldest first, each with its seq and as the engine wrote
 * it, and the page's `timeOrigin` once. The tools page turns them into marks with `eventsOf`
 * (`timelineEventOf` on each); `appendEvents` does it for the history.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const wire: PerfEventsWire = { v: 1, epoch: "1792000000000.5", timeOrigin: 1_792_000_000_000.5, next: 813, lost: false,
 *   items: [{ seq: 812, line: { v: 1, kind: "mark", t: 1_792_000_080_310.7, build: null, label: "boss fight", auto: false } }] };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfEventsWire = {
  v: 1;
  /** The page's clock origin (header.timeOrigin) as text: a new value means a new page (reload), the history restarts. */
  epoch: string | null;
  /** header.timeOrigin: a line's `t` is epoch ms, `eventsOf` subtracts this (the frames' page clock); null before a header. */
  timeOrigin: number | null;
  /** seq of the next line perf will keep: pass it as `after` next time. */
  next: number;
  /** True when lines after `after` were overwritten before this read (more than TIMELINE_SLOTS since). */
  lost: boolean;
  /** The kept lines with their seq, oldest first, as the engine wrote them. */
  items: { seq: number; line: PerfTimelineLine }[];
};

/**
 * An event line as the timeline reads it: the engine's `PerfEventLine` with the names of the 0.15.x
 * patch and the next change (`shader`, `problem`, `gc`, `sections`, `debug`), which the peer floor's
 * type (0.15.0) does not list and the dev engine's (0.15.1) lists but `gc` and `sections`. Every
 * `PerfEventLine` is one.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const compiled: TimelineEventLine = { v: 1, kind: "event", t: 1792000080310.7, build: null, frame: 4851, name: "shader",
 *   detail: { what: "compile", label: "fog.blur", ms: 38.2, frame: 4851, boot: false, during: { pass: 2, filter: "fog.blur", owner: 412, view: "fogLayer" } } };
 * ```
 */
export type TimelineEventLine = Omit<PerfEventLine, "name"> & { readonly name: PerfEventNameNext };

/**
 * A line the agent's timeline keeps and `editor.perf.events` sends: an event line of a name the
 * timeline marks, or a mark.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const line: PerfTimelineLine = { v: 1, kind: "mark", t: 1_792_000_080_310.7, build: null, label: "boss fight", auto: false };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfTimelineLine = TimelineEventLine | PerfMarkLine;

/**
 * The timeline event of one kept line (D4), on the page clock of the frames (`t − timeOrigin`,
 * rounded to 0.1 ms). Each detail is read with its guard; a malformed detail answers undefined,
 * never a throw. An unknown problem rule or shader `what` of a newer engine is kept as its string.
 * An old engine's `compile { frame, count }` answers a compile with `ms` null (the agent keeps it
 * only while no `shader` line was seen). Names the timeline does not mark (`devtools`, `command`,
 * `overlay`, `scene`, `warm`…) answer undefined. Allocates the event.
 *
 * @param line - The kept event or mark line.
 * @param seq - Its position in the agent's timeline ring.
 * @param timeOrigin - header.timeOrigin: line `t` is epoch ms, the timeline's page-clock ms.
 * @returns The event, or undefined.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * timelineEventOf(markLine("boss fight"), 8, header.timeOrigin);
 * // { seq: 8, kind: "mark", t: 42000, frame: null, label: "boss fight", auto: false }
 * ```
 */
export function timelineEventOf(
  line: TimelineEventLine | PerfMarkLine,
  seq: number,
  timeOrigin: number
): PerfTimelineEvent | undefined;

/**
 * The marks of an events wire (the tools page's side of D4): each kept line through
 * `timelineEventOf` with its seq and the wire's `timeOrigin` (0 before a header), oldest first; a
 * line the timeline does not mark, a malformed detail or a broken item is skipped. Pure; allocates
 * its answer.
 *
 * @param wire - An `editor.perf.events` answer.
 * @returns The timeline events.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * eventsOf(wire)[0]; // { seq: 812, kind: "mark", t: 80310.2, frame: null, label: "boss fight", auto: false }
 * ```
 */
export function eventsOf(wire: PerfEventsWire): PerfTimelineEvent[];
~~~

---

## 4. Error codes

All errors are JSON-RPC error objects (`WireError`). Messages start with `[moku-editor] ` (`ERROR_PREFIX`). No stack crosses the wire. `bareMessage(message)` strips the prefix for UI text.

| Code | `errorCode` key | `data.reason` | Retryable | Raised by | When |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| -32600 | `invalidRequest` | — | no | hub | duplicate `sub` on one connection; more than 256 pending calls per tools connection |
| -32601 | `unknownMethod` | `unknown_id` (with `data.id`) or none | no | channel, bridge, hub, files, capture | unknown source or command id; unknown channel or method; missing file or folder (`files`) |
| -32602 | `invalidInput` | `invalid_input` (`data.field`) | no | registry, capture, hub, files | input fails `checkInput`; bad `sub`; text over 2 MiB or binary over 16 MiB on write; bad data URL |
| -32000 | `commandFailed` | `command_failed` | no | registry, capture, hub, files | a door threw; `game.capture` gave no picture; a series is already recording; IO error; file too large on read |
| -32000 | `commandFailed` | `port_in_use` | no | connect | `connect.wire` / `connect.network`: the device port is taken (`[moku-editor] port 47600 is in use.` / `  Is moku-editor perf running? Stop it, or connect from its tools page.`) |
| -32000 | `commandFailed` | `no_lan` | no | connect | `connect.network`: the computer has no LAN address |
| -32001 | `gameReloaded` | `game_reloaded` | yes | hub | the agent closed while a call was pending |
| -32001 | `pageClosed` | `page_closed` | yes | hub | the editor page closed before it answered a relayed `editor.select` |
| -32002 | `timeout` | `timeout` | yes | bridge, hub, link | the call passed its deadline (the command is not cancelled) |
| -32002 | `timeout` | `link_closed` | yes | link | socket not open, socket closed, or `app.stop()` |
| -32003 | `noSession` | `no_session` | no | hub, link | no game connected, or the named session is not open |
| -32003 | `noSession` | `choose_session` | no | hub, link | several sessions and not exactly one embedded; `link.choose` with an id that is not open |
| -32003 | `noEditorPage` | `no_editor_page` | no | hub | `editor.select` and no tools connection with `role=page` is open ("Open the editor page: <url>") |
| -32004 | `forbiddenPath` | `forbidden_path` | no | files | a path fails a sandbox rule |
| -32005 | `versionConflict` | `version_conflict` | no | files | stale `version`, or a `version` for a missing file |
| -32006 | `notJson` | `not_json` | no | registry (`toWireValue`) | a value is not JSON (function, symbol, bigint, cycle, depth over 64) |
| -32007 | `unauthorized` | `unauthorized` | no | hub | a request from an agent connection (a registered editor method included) |
| -32007 | `unauthorized` | `not_owner` | no | connect | `connect.off`: device mode belongs to `moku-editor perf` |
| -32602 | `invalidInput` | `no_ticket` | no | connect | `connect.confirm` / `connect.refuse`: no pairing waits with that ticket |
| -32008 | `notInstalled` | `not_installed` (with `data.id`) | no | registry | a read or watch of a source the game does not have: its door threw on the probe (manifest `available: false`). Message `[moku-editor] source <id> is not available in this game: <reason>`. The link does not log or retry it. |
| -32009 | `readOnly` | `read_only` (with `data.id`) | no | registry | the page's build refuses the command: a `--debug=read` page (or `--debug` of engine 0.15.0) runs `read` and `cosmetic` commands only (the engine's `controlReadOnly`). `[moku-editor] <id>: refused by this debug build, which runs read and cosmetic commands only.` / `  Build the game with --debug=full to run it.` |
| -32009 | `devOnly` | `dev_only` (with `data.id`) | no | registry | a page with neither the dev nor the debug flag (the engine's `controlRefused`). `[moku-editor] <id>: refused by this build, which has neither the dev nor the debug flag.` / `  Run the game from the dev server, or build it with --debug.` |

Deadlines: bridge `callTimeoutMs` (5000), hub `callTimeoutMs` (5000), link `CALL_TIMEOUT_MS` (10000). A `run` of `editor.series` gets `min(input.durationMs, 60000)` on top in all three, and a `run` of `editor.sheet` gets `min(input.frames × input.everyMs, 60000)`. The MCP bridge waits at most 70 s for any hub answer.

Config errors (not wire errors) are thrown at `createApp` from `onInit`, in the shape:

```
[moku-editor] <plugin>.<field> <problem>.
  <fix line, e.g. Pass pluginConfigs.channel.heartbeatMs, for example 1000.>
```

Examples: `[moku-editor] registry.game is missing.`, `[moku-editor] registry.game is not a game app.`, `[moku-editor] Duplicate registry id "<id>".`, `[moku-editor] files.root "<root>" is not a directory.`, `[moku-editor] files.allow is empty.`, `[moku-editor] Panel "<id>" is already registered.`, `[moku-editor] Key "<combo>" is already bound in <scope>.`

Websocket close codes: 1000 normal (bridge `bye`, link stop, bridge `switch`), 1001 `editor stopping` (hub stop) / `device mode off` / `lan off` (`hub.stopLan()`: a LAN phone, which stays paired) / `replaced` (a phone reconnected with its token), 1003 binary frame, 1008 `hello first` / `bad manifest` / `hello twice` / ten malformed messages / `pair first` (a pairing socket's first message, or none within 5 s) / `pairing refused` / `pairing timed out` / `pairing busy`, 1009 frame over 32 MiB (Bun), 1012 `editor restarting` (the bin's Hot reload restart), 4401 `unpaired` (a device token the hub does not know, closed right after the open: the bridge pairs again).

Upgrade refusals of `hub.fetch` (in check order): 404 `missing`, 503 `unavailable`, 426 `upgrade`, 403 `forbidden`, 401 `unauthorized`, 400 `invalid`. The device listeners add 429 `busy` (check `cooldown`: an address that cools down after a refusal or already holds 4 open pairing sockets) and refuse `kind=tools` on the LAN listener (403, check `listener`).

---

## 5. Event catalog

Global events are declared in `src/config.ts` (section 2: `AgentEvents`, `ServerEvents`, `ToolsEvents`). An event is global only when its listener cannot depend on its emitter; the per-plugin events (second table) are declared by their emitter with `register<T>()` and reach only the plugins that list the emitter in `depends`. Payload types are in sections 2, 3 and 7.

| Core | Event | Payload type | Emitted by | When | Hooked by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| agent | `bridge:status` | `{ status: LinkStatus; session?: string; link?: DeviceLink }` | bridge | at start (`connecting`), on every change of status kind, on every session change; in device mode on every change of the link's mode, address, pairing code or computer engine, and at most once a second for `seenAt`; `link` in device mode only; never from `onStop` | overlay (link light, Link tab) |
| agent | `overlay:changed` | `OverlayChanged` (`{ mode: OverlayMode; tab: OverlayTab }`) | overlay | every mode or tab change, once at a visible start; never on a place change | recorder (the `devtools` monitor event) |
| agent | `overlay:connect` | `{ address: string }` | overlay | Connect / Pair on the Link tab with a valid `host:port` | bridge (`connect(address)`) |
| server | `hub:session` | `HubSession` | hub | a valid `hello` (`open: true`); an agent close (`open: false`, `reason` `"bye"` or `"game_reloaded"`) | none in the package; for consumer plugins |
| server | `files:written` | `FilesWritten` | files | after each successful `write` or `writeBinary`, after the rename; `kind` from `classifyWrite(path)` | none in the package; for consumer plugins |
| server | `files:project` | `ProjectState` | files | the project index opened (on), a watch batch changed it (on, with `previous` and `change`), or it went off (once) | hub (`publish("project", state)`: the `editor.project` notification, kept and replayed) |
| tools | `link:status` | `{ status: LinkStatus; session?: string }` | link | status changed kind or any field, or the session changed | workspace, panels, flowView, gameView, renderView, stateView, filesView, consoleView |
| tools | `link:project` | `{ state: ProjectState; delta: ProjectDelta }` | link | a new `editor.project` state: not the held one again (on at the same revision and manifest, off with the same reason). `delta` is `projectDelta(held, next)`; at the same revision with another `manifest` it is `{ all: false, files: [old, new manifest] }` | flowView, gameView, renderView, filesView |
| tools | `workspace:changed` | `{ ws: WorkspaceId }` | workspace | `show()` changed the workspace | panels, flowView, gameView, renderView, filesView |
| tools | `workspace:ran` | `RanEvent` | workspace (origins `topbar`, `key`, `palette`), panels (origin `panel`, or the api `run` origin) | a command run from the tools page settled | stateView (taint), consoleView (error lines) |
| tools | `workspace:density` | `{ density: Density }` (`"compact" \| "comfortable"`) | workspace | the applied density changed: a choice in the palette, or `auto` crossing 820 px of window width | flowView (ELK spacing) |
| tools | `workspace:open-file` | `{ path: string; line?: number }` | flowView, gameView | "Open in Files" | filesView |
| tools | `workspace:select-node` | `{ id: string }` | filesView | a Used-by chip | flowView |
| tools | `workspace:focus-frame` | `{ frame: number }` | consoleView | a frame link, `focusFrame()` | flowView |
| tools | `workspace:reveal` | `{ ref: ElementRef }` | gameView | "Show in render tree" | renderView |
| tools | `workspace:inspect` | `{ ref: ElementRef }` | renderView | "Inspect in Game" | gameView |
| tools | `workspace:open-sheet` | `{ index: string }` | filesView | "Open contact sheet" on a series `index.json` | gameView |

`files:written` kind rules (`classifyWrite`, first match wins): starts with `.moku/captures/` → `capture`; equals `.moku/editor/layout.json` → `layout`; ends with `.css`, basename `styles.ts`/`styles.tsx`, ends with `.styles.ts`/`.styles.tsx`, or a `.ts`/`.tsx` module directly in a `styles/` folder (`shared/styles/text.ts`) → `style`; other `.ts`/`.tsx` → `code`; else `other`.

`LinkStatus` semantics: `connecting` (socket open or session attached, no heartbeat yet); `live`/`paused` (the chosen session beats; `paused` from the heartbeat flag); `silent` (no heartbeat for 6 s, or 65 s after a `paused: true` beat); `lost` (socket closed, chosen session closed, or no boot tag `no_boot`); `empty` (connected, no game session, also 10 s after a lost session; inside an expected reload window, at the end of the window). The bridge reports only `connecting`, `live`, `paused`, `lost`.

Per-plugin events:

| Core | Event | Payload type | Emitter | When | Hooked by (through `depends`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| agent | `registry:command` | `RegistryCommandEvent` `{ id, input, via, ok }` | registry | a command run settled (door, module or editor command; `via` `"overlay"`, `"tools"`, `"mcp"`, `"bridge"` or `"local"`; not for an input refused with -32602) | recorder (the `command` monitor event; `editor.record` turns `via` into `startedBy`) |
| agent | `recorder:status` | `RecorderStatusEvent` `{ state, lines, bytes, sent, pending }` | recorder | start, stop, share (exporting and back), remove, and a flush tick that changed a number | overlay (REC, Record tab), bridge (ships the pending lines) |
| server | `hub:device` | `HubDeviceEvent` | hub | `listening` (`listenDevices`, `listenLan`, `stopLan`), `connected` (a pairing or a token reconnect), `lines` (a `perf.lines` batch with new items or a gap), `closed` (`bye`, `lost`, `replaced`, `stopped`), `stopped` (`stopDevices`); never from `onStop` | collector, connect |
| server | `connect:telemetry` | `DeviceTelemetry` (`connect/protocol`) | connect | each telemetry tick (`telemetryEveryMs`, 1 s) of a wired phone a tools page watches; also published as `editor.deviceTelemetry` | collector (one `telemetry` line into that phone's live log while it records) |
| server | `collector:session` | `CollectorSessionEvent` `{ device, file, state, lines, lost, last }` | collector | a log's first written batch, then at most once a second per log; after a close on `away` and `done` | pages (the perf CLI's live lines) |
| tools | `activeSource:changed` | `SourceChange` `{ from, to, reason, at }` (`reason` `connected`, `user`, `lost`, `rejoined`, `stopped`, `adopted`) | activeSource | every source switch | workspace (source pill, notice, veil), renderView (the switch burst: every watch and the poll of the old source stop, the history resets) |
| tools | `activeSource:connect-requested` | `ConnectRequest` `{ tab: "wire" \| "network" \| undefined }` | activeSource | `openConnect(tab?)` (the source menu's Connect device…) | renderView (shows Render with the Connect panel open on that tab) |

Not events: heartbeats are a callback api (`channel.onHeartbeat`, `link.onHeartbeat`), and so are taps (`link.onTap`), session lists (`link.onSessions`), published values (`link.onPublished`) and source changes for code outside the tools core (`activeSource.onChange`); `ctx.log` lines such as `hub:refused`, `bridge:lost`, `registry:watch-failed`, `registry:source-unavailable`, `link:watch-failed`, `panels:view-failed` are log events, listed in each plugin README.

---

## 6. Configuration reference

All options are set per plugin through `createApp({ pluginConfigs: { <plugin>: { … } } })`, shallow-merged over the defaults (arrays replace). Global configs are empty. Bad values throw at `createApp`.

### Agent

| Plugin | Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| registry | `game` | `GameLike \| undefined` | `undefined` | Required. The app the game made with `createApp`. `onInit` throws without it. |
| registry | `modules` | `readonly DevModule[]` | `[]` | The game's `.dev` modules: extra sources and commands, added after the doors. |
| registry | `name` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | `Manifest.game`. Falls back to trimmed `document.title`, then `"game"`. |
| channel | `heartbeatMs` | `number` | `1000` | Ms between two beats. Whole number ≥ 100. |
| perf | `readEveryMs` | `number` | `250` | How often perf reads the monitor's frame ring (4 Hz). 50–1000. |
| perf | `windowMs` | `number` | `6000` | The window the graph, the spike index and every spike count cover. 1000–30000. |
| perf | `frames` | `number` | `1024` | Rows perf keeps: at least `windowMs` at 120 Hz (720). Whole number, 64–16384. |
| perf | `feedPasses` | `boolean` | `false` | Read the engine's pass ring and send the pass rows (the engine's default sections). Flat on purpose: per-plugin config merges shallowly. |
| perf | `feedSystems` | `boolean` | `true` | Read and send the top 5 systems of each frame. |
| perf | `feedNodes` | `boolean` | `false` | Read and send the demand marks of each frame. |
| recorder | `autoStart` | `boolean \| "device"` | `false` | `false`: nothing records until the phone (Record tab), the tools page (Record) or an agent (`editor.record`) starts it. `"device"`: a log starts on a debug build only (agent flag on, dev flag off). `true`: always. An opted-in start waits for the engine's header (the first flush tick with it, at most 10 ticks). |
| recorder | `keepMb` | `number` | `64` | Most MB in memory: unconfirmed outbox lines, memory-store logs, pending text. 1–512. |
| recorder | `flushEveryMs` | `number` | `1000` | How often the queue is serialized. 100–10000. |
| recorder | `persistEveryMs` | `number` | `5000` | How often text is written to the store (also at 64 KB pending, and at stop). 1000–60000. |
| recorder | `storage` | `"auto" \| "memory"` | `"auto"` | OPFS when the page has it, or never on disk. |
| recorder | `keepFiles` | `number` | `10` | Finished logs kept; the oldest beyond go when a log starts. Whole number, 1–100. |
| recorder | `maxLogMb` | `number` | `32` | The size of one log: at it the recorder rotates to the next log with the same label and `startedBy` (32 is the native share's cap). Whole number, 1–512. |
| overlay | `mode` | `"hidden" \| "pill" \| "card"` | `"hidden"` | Mode at start when the device remembers none (or `remember` is false). The engine's `config.debug.overlay` opens it later through the global channel. The old `open` throws a `TypeError` naming `mode`. |
| overlay | `dock` | `"left" \| "right"` | `"right"` | Edge the window docks to until the person drags it. The old `corner` throws a `TypeError` naming `dock`. |
| overlay | `remember` | `boolean` | `true` | Remember place, mode and tab in `localStorage["moku-editor:overlay"]`. |
| overlay | `mount` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | CSS selector of the element the host is appended to; `undefined` = `document.body`. |
| bridge | `hello` | `string` | `"/__editor/hello"` | Hello route: same-origin path or absolute URL. Non-empty. |
| bridge | `retryMs` | `number` | `1000` | First reconnect delay; doubles per failure up to `MAX_RETRY_MS` (30000), ±20 % jitter. Whole number ≥ 100. |
| bridge | `callTimeoutMs` | `number` | `5000` | Deadline of one `read` or `run`, and of one `perf.ack`. Whole number ≥ 100. |
| bridge | `device` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | Device mode at this computer address (`host:port`, `[v6]:port`). `undefined`: page mode on a served page; device mode with `__MOKU_GAME_EDITOR__` or on a native page, at the remembered address, else the build's, else `"127.0.0.1:47600"`. |
| bridge | `linesPerBatch` | `number` | `200` | Most log lines in one `perf.lines` message. Whole number 1–1000. |
| capture | `maxDurationMs` | `number` | `20000` | Longest series accepted. More → -32602 field `durationMs`. |
| capture | `minIntervalMs` | `number` | `16` | Shortest interval accepted. Less → -32602 field `intervalMs`. |

### Server

| Plugin | Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| files | `root` | `string` | `"."` | Project root, absolute or relative to the working folder. Resolved once with `realpathSync`; must be an existing folder. |
| files | `allow` | `readonly string[]` | `["**/*.ts", "**/*.tsx", "**/*.json", "**/*.md", "**/*.css", ".moku/**"]` | Globs a file must match to be read or written. Case-sensitive. Not empty. |
| files | `deny` | `readonly string[]` | `["**/node_modules/**", "**/.git/**", "**/dist/**", "**/.env*"]` | Globs never listed, read or written. Case-insensitive. |
| files | `project` | `boolean` | `true` | Open the project index of `root` on start. `false` leaves it off with reason `"disabled"`; the index is never loaded. |
| hub | `path` | `string` | `"/__editor"` | URL prefix of every editor route. Starts with `/`; letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `/`; no trailing or double slash. |
| hub | `allowOrigins` | `readonly string[]` | `[]` | Extra exact http(s) origins allowed to upgrade and call same-origin routes. No path, no trailing slash. |
| hub | `callTimeoutMs` | `number` | `5000` | Deadline of a forwarded call before -32002. Integer ≥ 100. |
| hub | `silentAfterMs` | `number` | `6000` | No heartbeat this long → silent. 65 s after a `paused: true` beat. Integer ≥ 100. |
| hub | `devicePort` | `number` | `47600` | Port of the device listeners (127.0.0.1 and, with `deviceLan`, the LAN address). Integer 0–65535; 0 picks a free port (tests). |
| hub | `deviceLan` | `boolean` | `false` | Also listen on the computer's LAN address: device upgrades only, pairing confirmed by the person. |
| hub | `lanAddress` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | The LAN address to bind: an IPv4 literal, or an IPv6 literal in canonical lower case without a zone id. Unset picks the first non-internal IPv4 of an `en*`, `wl*` or `eth*` interface, else of any interface. |
| hub | `deviceOrigins` | `readonly string[]` | `["tauri://localhost", "https://tauri.localhost", "http://tauri.localhost"]` | Exact Origins a device's WebView sends: scheme `tauri:`, `http:` or `https:`, a host, no path, lower case. Never added to the normal listener's origins. |
| hub | `pairing` | `"lan" \| "always"` | `"lan"` | `"lan"`: only LAN phones are asked; an adb phone is confirmed at once. `"always"`: every phone is asked. |
| hub | `pairTimeoutMs` | `number` | `60000` | How long a pairing waits for the person before it is refused. Integer ≥ 1000. |
| connect | `adb` | `string` | `"adb"` | The adb command (a name on PATH or a path). |
| connect | `adbTimeoutMs` | `number` | `5000` | One adb call is killed after this. 500–60000. |
| connect | `scanEveryMs` | `number` | `2000` | `adb devices -l` period while a scan lease (the Connect panel) or device mode is on. 500–60000. |
| connect | `answerTimeoutMs` | `number` | `20000` | A ready phone with no session after this reads "no debug game answered". 1000–300000. |
| connect | `leaseMs` | `number` | `10000` | A scan or watch lease not renewed for this long ends. 2000–120000. |
| connect | `telemetryEveryMs` | `number` | `1000` | The telemetry tick. 250–10000. |
| connect | `meminfoEveryMs` | `number` | `5000` | `dumpsys meminfo` period. 1000–60000. |
| connect | `heapEveryMs` | `number` | `250` | CDP `Runtime.getHeapUsage` period. 100–5000. |
| connect | `gcDropMb` | `number` | `0.5` | A heap drop of at least this is an inferred GC. 0.05–64. |
| connect | `gcTrace` | `boolean` | `false` | Lets the CDP client send `Tracing.start` / `Tracing.end`; GCs stay inferred until the trace reading is measured on a phone. |
| connect | `wire` | `"manual" \| "auto"` | `"manual"` | `"auto"`: the adb listener on at start when `adb version` answers and the port is free (never the LAN). The bin keeps `"manual"`: device mode starts from the tools page. |
| collector | `out` | `string` | `".moku/perf"` | Folder of the device logs: relative to the files root, or absolute. Created on the first log. Non-empty. |
| collector | `everyS` | `number` | `10` | Seconds between two adb readings (heat, system frames) of a phone. Whole number, 1–3600. |
| collector | `reverseEveryMs` | `number` | `2000` | Ms between two `adb devices` + `adb reverse` rounds. Whole number ≥ 500. |
| collector | `adb` | `string` | `"adb"` | The adb command (a name on PATH or a path). Non-empty. |
| collector | `adbTimeoutMs` | `number` | `5000` | The longest one adb command may run before it is killed. Whole number ≥ 500. |
| collector | `appId` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | The game's Android package; `<appId>.debug` is preferred when installed. Undefined: no gfx lines. |
| pages | `title` | `string` | `"moku editor"` | Tools page `<title>` and `ToolsBoot.title`. 1–120 characters. |
| pages | `editorUrl` | `string` | `"vscode://file/{path}:{line}"` | "Open in editor" template. Must contain `{path}`; scheme cannot be `javascript`, `data`, `vbscript`. |
| pages | `pageDir` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | Built page folder. `undefined` tries `dist/tools` next to the bundled module, then the repo `dist/tools`. |
| pages | `gameUrl` | `string` | `"/"` | Same-origin URL of the game page. Starts with `/`, not `//`, no `\`. |
| pages | `toolsPage` | `boolean` | `true` | Serve the tools page and its assets. `false` (`moku-editor perf --no-ui`) answers 404 on `P`, `P/` and `P/assets/*`; `P/hello` and `P/hmr` are unchanged. |

### Tools

| Plugin | Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| link | `retryMs` | `number` | `1000` | Base of the reconnect backoff `min(retryMs × 2^n, 8000)`. |
| link | `boot` | `string` | `"#moku-editor-boot"` | CSS selector of the boot JSON tag `pages` injects. |
| link | `role` | `"page" \| "tools"` | `"page"` | `"page"`: the editor page (`&role=page`: the hub takes its `selection` and relays `select`, `device`, `show`, `node` to it). `"tools"`: a plain tools client (a headless test). |
| link | `reloadGraceMs` | `number` | `8000` | How long an expected reload (U7: close 1012, a reload the editor started, a game that said bye) reads `lost` with `reloading: true`. Without a heartbeat of the game by then the status is a plain `lost`, or `empty` when the window is still open 10 s after a session loss and no session came back (no upper bound). Positive; `onInit` throws `[moku-editor] link.reloadGraceMs is invalid.` otherwise. |
| activeSource | `autoUse` | `boolean` | `true` | A device that links while the local preview is the source becomes the source (once per device id). |
| activeSource | `pauseLocal` | `boolean` | `true` | Pause the local preview while a device is the source. |
| activeSource | `rejoinMs` | `number` | `15000` | A lost device that returns within this becomes the source again (0: never). Integer 0–600000. |
| activeSource | `noticeMs` | `number` | `12000` | How long the disconnect notice shows. Integer 1000–120000. |
| activeSource | `renewMs` | `number` | `4000` | How often the scan and watch leases on connect are renewed (connect's `leaseMs` is 10 s). Integer 500–60000. |
| activeSource | `markers` | `number` | `32` | Source-switch markers kept. Integer 1–512. |
| workspace | `defaultWorkspace` | `WorkspaceId` | `"game"` | Shown at start when the URL hash names none. |
| workspace | `storageKey` | `string` | `"moku-editor"` | localStorage key of the preferences record. |
| workspace | `reloadTimeoutMs` | `number` | `15000` | How long `reload()` waits for the new session. |
| workspace | `hotReloadWaitMs` | `number` | `1500` | After a save with Bun hot reload on: how long `gameFrame().reload()` waits for the page Bun reloads before it reloads the frame itself. Positive. |
| workspace | `toastMs` | `number` | `2600` | How long one toast stays; hover or focus pauses it. |
| panels | — | `Record<string, never>` | `{}` | No options. |
| flowView | `historyLast` | `number` | `20` | Entries of `game.history` the panel watches. |
| flowView | `trailLength` | `number` | `6` | Edges drawn as the trail. |
| flowView | `rejectedOutcomes` | `readonly string[]` | `["rejected"]` | Outcomes drawn as rejections. |
| flowView | `layout.file` | `string` | `".moku/editor/layout.json"` | Saved positions. |
| flowView | `layout.worker` | `boolean` | `true` | Run ELK in a Blob Web Worker; `false` runs it inline. |
| flowView | `layout.saveDelayMs` | `number` | `400` | Debounce of the layout save after a drop. |
| flowView | `zoom.min` | `number` | `0.08` | Lowest zoom. |
| flowView | `zoom.max` | `number` | `3` | Highest zoom. |
| flowView | `zoom.defaultMin` | `number` | `0.8` | Floor of the default camera. |
| flowView | `hub.minOutcomes` | `number` | `6` | Hub rule: a rest node with at least this many outcomes. |
| flowView | `hub.minReturns` | `number` | `4` | Hub rule: at least this many other nodes return to it. |
| gameView | `capturesDir` | `string` | `".moku/captures"` | Screenshots, series and the two pictures of a pick (`<key>-f<frame>-crop.jpg`, `f<frame>-full.jpg`), each in a day folder `<yyyy-mm-dd>/` (local date; a Shot is `<hhmm>-<flow>.jpg`, a series `series-<hhmm>/`). `.moku/captures` or a folder under it (the files sandbox); `onInit` throws `[moku-editor] gameView.capturesDir must be .moku/captures or a folder under it.` otherwise. |
| gameView | `captureCardMs` | `number` | `10000` | Capture card hides after this unless hovered or focused. |
| gameView | `seriesDurationsMs` | `readonly number[]` | `[1000, 2000, 5000, 10000, 20000]` | Duration chips. |
| gameView | `seriesIntervalsMs` | `readonly number[]` | `[16, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000]` | Interval chips. |
| gameView | `seriesWarnShots` | `number` | `200` | Popover warns above this many planned shots. |
| renderView | `releaseLogMax` | `number` | `50` | Release log entries kept. |
| stateView | `expandDepth` | `number` | `2` | Tree levels open by default. |
| stateView | `maxPatches` | `number` | `200` | Most patches kept per commit. |
| stateView | `pageSize` | `number` | `100` | Children shown per array or object before "Show N more". |
| filesView | `maxFiles` | `number` | `5000` | Most files the tree walk indexes. |
| filesView | `maxHighlightChars` | `number` | `512000` | Longer files show without colour. |
| filesView | `reloadExtensions` | `readonly string[]` | `[".ts", ".tsx", ".css", ".json"]` | A save of these outside `.moku/` runs the D-07 reload. |
| filesView | `revalidateMs` | `number` | `2000` | A clean tab is re-read on activation when older than this. |
| consoleView | `maxLines` | `number` | `5000` | Most lines kept; oldest go first. |
| consoleView | `preserveLog` | `boolean` | `false` | Initial state of Preserve log. |
| consoleView | `freshMs` | `number` | `1200` | Highlight time of a fresh error row. |
| consoleView | `summaryChars` | `number` | `160` | Characters of non-string `data` shown inline. |

### Bin

```
moku-editor [--root DIR] [--preload FILE]… [--serve-plugin FILE]… [--port 3000] [--no-hmr]
moku-editor <game-html> [--port 3000] [--root .] [--no-hmr] [--help]
moku-editor mcp [<game-html>] [--port N] [--root DIR] [--no-hmr]
moku-editor mcp-config [<game-html>] [--port N]
moku-editor e2e -c <playwright config> [playwright args…]
moku-editor perf [--lan] [--port 47600] [--out DIR] [--every 10] [--no-ui]
moku-editor perf mark "<label>" | perf summary <log.jsonl> | perf compare <a.jsonl> <b.jsonl>
```

| Flag | Short | Default | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--port` | `-p` | `3000` | Digits, 0–65535. `0` picks a free port. |
| `--root` | `-r` | `.` | Project root the editor reads and writes; the moku-game folder of the engine page. Not empty. |
| `--no-hmr` | | hot reload on | Serves with `development: { hmr: false, console: true }`; `hotReload()` reports `{ hmr: false, owner: "bin" }`. |
| `--preload` | | none | A file Bun preloads in the serving process. Repeatable. Engine page only. |
| `--serve-plugin` | | none | A Bun plugin the engine page bundles with, after the engine's hot plugin. Repeatable. Engine page only. |
| `--help` | `-h` | | Prints usage, exit 0. |

Engine page (B5, D-49 … D-51; keys watch D-54, D-55): without an html file the bin serves a moku-game folder (`index.ts` + `config.ts`). (0) Checked first: without the real process (`deps.reexec`, unit seams): "[moku-editor] the engine page needs the real process: pass the game HTML file", exit 1. (1) Not a moku-game folder: "[moku-editor] <root> has no index.ts and config.ts: pass the game HTML file, or run in a moku-game folder", exit 2. (2) It imports `@moku-labs/game/cli` as the game root resolves it, once, for `preparePage` and `watchKeys` (both required, D-54); when it does not resolve or lacks either: "[moku-editor] @moku-labs/game/cli does not resolve from <root>: install @moku-labs/game >=0.13.1 in the game", exit 1. (3) `preparePage(root, { agents: ["@moku-labs/editor/agent/page"], preload, servePlugins })`, the flag paths resolved against the cwd; a throw prints the engine's `[game] …` text, exit 1. (4) From an editor working tree (its package root, found from `Bun.main`, is not under `realpath(<root>)/node_modules` and has `scripts/tree/bundle.ts`) that plugin is appended to `servePlugins`: `@moku-labs/editor`, `/agent`, `/agent/page` and `/tools` bundle from the tree's `dist/`, whose imports of the engine, Pixi, core, common and preact are rewritten in `onLoad` to the game's copies (never `onResolve`, demos#46). (5) Keys watch (D-54, D-55): the parent bin calls `watchKeys(root, { onError })` of the same cli import. It resolves after the engine's first scan, so `generated/` is fresh before the child serves; later a save of an asset or of a `strings/<locale>.json` scans again. A failed scan, the first one too, is one warning (`ui.warn` with the engine's message) and the bin keeps running. A rejection prints the engine's `[game] …` text, exit 1, and no child is spawned. The html form never watches keys; the child never imports the engine's cli. (6) The bin always re-runs itself (D-51): `[execPath, "--config=<root>/.moku/bunfig.toml", Bun.main, "<root>/.moku/index.html", "--root", root, "--port", port, "--no-hmr"?]`, `cwd: root`, `MOKU_EDITOR_REEXEC=1`, signals forwarded, the parent exits with the child's code. The keys watch is closed in a `finally` around the child, so it stops with the child; a throw of `close()` is one warning. Before the spawn the parent has no signal handlers of its own (`main` installs the early ones only with an html file): a SIGINT or SIGTERM while the page is written or the first scan runs ends it with the default action, exit 130 or 143, no child is spawned, and the keys watch ends with the process. The child serves that html as any re-spawned bin; the discovery file's `html` is `<root>/.moku/index.html`. `--preload` and `--serve-plugin` with an html file: "--preload and --serve-plugin need the engine page: drop the html file"; on `mcp` and `mcp-config`: "--preload and --serve-plugin belong to the serving bin". The MCP launcher restarts a gone engine bin in the engine form (no html), so the page is written again and served under that bunfig. Limit: `--preload` and `--serve-plugin` are not in the discovery file, so the restarted bin has none.

Hot reload (D-23, round 2 R6): by default the bin serves with `development: { hmr: true, console: true }` and calls `pages.attachServer(options)` right after `Bun.serve`. A save of a game source makes Bun reload the game page; before it reloads, the bridge stores a `game.bookmark` checkpoint in `sessionStorage`, and the new page restores it (and pauses again when it was paused) and says so in its hello (`manifest.restored`). Bun 1.3.14 cannot switch HMR on a running server, so the bin gives `attachServer` its restart and the Hot reload switch restarts the server with HMR flipped on the same port (D-32): `POST {P}/hmr` answers 200 with the asked state, then the server restarts (A1); the token, the sessions table and `.moku/editor.json` stay, every socket drops for about a second, and the tools page reloads the game frame with its checkpoint so the page gains or drops `/_bun/client`. While HMR is off a save on disk does not reload the game. A failed restart publishes the old state and serves the old options again. Before the restart serves with HMR on, the bin waits, at most 5 s, until Bun's bundler is idle (D-57): Bun 1.3.14 froze its main thread, or crashed, when the page rebundle of the server without HMR (Bun starts one on every page request) and the dev server's first bundle ran at once, and a page request that reaches the old server during the switch set that up. The floor is now Bun 1.4.2 (D-58): the freeze did not reproduce there in 241 runs, and the wait stays as a guard of about 2 ms. Hot swap (game 0.5.0): with `[serve.static] plugins = ["@moku-labs/game/hot"]` in the game root's `bunfig.toml`, a save of a view module (`.tsx`, `styles.ts`, `view.ts`, `animations.ts`, `effects.ts`, `generated/strings.<locale>.ts`) swaps in place: same session, no reload, toast "Game updated"; a logic module still reloads and restores. Bun reads that bunfig once at process start from the process cwd, so a `run` whose `--root` has a `[serve.static]` bunfig and whose cwd is another folder re-spawns the bin in the root (`reexec.ts`: absolute html and root, `MOKU_EDITOR_REEXEC=1` loop guard, SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP forwarded, the parent exits with the child's code, the discovery file names the child). The MCP launcher spawns the bin with `cwd: root`.

e2e (D-52, D-53, `e2e.ts`): one Playwright process, so one fresh editor bin, per project and spec file, because Bun's dev server degrades after many hot reloads in one process (also within one project: merge-game failed from the ~90th reload-heavy spec). `splitRest(rest)` sorts the user's words into `projects` (`--project X Y…` takes every next word not starting with `-`, as Playwright's variadic option, up to a path-like word (a `/`, or `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.js`/`.mjs` at the end), which is a file filter, so a project named like a path needs `--project=X`; `--project=X` one), `files` (any other word not starting with `-` that is not a flag's value), `reporters` (`--reporter`, `--add-reporter`), `listOnly` (`--shard`, `--last-failed`) and `other`; a flag with a required value (`-g`, `-G`, `-j`, `--repeat-each`, `--timeout`, …) keeps its next word, `-u` / `--update-snapshots` only `all|changed|missing|none`, `--debug` only `inspector|cli`, `--only-changed` a word not starting with `-` and not ending in `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.js`; `--flag=v` is one word. The plan comes from `bun x playwright test -c <config> --list --reporter=json --pass-with-no-tests <files> --project=<p>… <other> <listOnly>` (JSON output env vars removed; a failed or unparsable list: "[moku-editor] could not list the tests of <config>: <reason>", exit 1). `listPlan(json)` answers `{ rootDir: config.rootDir, pairs }`: one (project, file) pair per named project and spec file with at least one listed test, projects in config order, files in list order (`specs[].file`, relative to `rootDir`), unnamed projects skipped. Each pair runs as `bun x playwright test -c <config> --project=<p> <fileFilter(file, rootDir)> --pass-with-no-tests <other> <reporters>` with `PORT` = `PORT` (an integer 1-65535, else 4417) + its index, one after another, all of them; `fileFilter` = `^<rootDir>/<file>$`, regex-escaped with `/` separators (Playwright tests a file argument as a regex on the absolute path). `--project=<p>` is one word because the variadic `--project <p>` would read the file regex as a project. After each run `ui.info("<project> · <file> · passed|failed (code N) · <s> s")`, at the end `ui.info("e2e: <n> runs · <failed> failed · <s> s")` (`E2eDeps.now`, default `performance.now`). A failed run's line and a failing summary print as errors; a warning names the tests of an unnamed project that did not run. Exit = the first non-zero code, else 0. A `--list`, an empty plan (no test matched, or only an unnamed project) runs once as given, without `--pass-with-no-tests`, so Playwright's "No tests found" tells the user. Lock (`E2eDeps.lock`: `take(): Promise<number | undefined>`, `release(): Promise<void>`; `processE2eDeps` sets `fileLock(process.cwd())`): before the CI install `runE2e` creates `.moku/e2e.lock` in the cwd with the bin's pid (`wx`, folder created); while a live pid (`process.kill(pid, 0)`) holds it: "[moku-editor] another e2e run (pid N) holds .moku/e2e.lock: wait for it, or delete the file when no run is left", exit 1, nothing runs; a dead or unreadable pid is taken over; released in a `finally` after the last run, also after a failure, and only while the file holds this pid; a `--list` takes no lock. `CI=true` runs `bun x playwright install chromium` first. Only `-c X` / `--config X` / `--config=X` is read, before `--help` (missing: "[moku-editor] e2e needs the Playwright config: -c <file>", exit 2); no signal handlers, a Ctrl+C reaches Playwright through the process group.

perf (`src/plugins/pages/perf/`, device mode): a first word `perf` picks the perf CLI before the global `--help` scan. `runPerf` starts the server core (files, hub, connect, collector, pages) without a game, with `files.root` the cwd, `files.project: false` and `collector.appId` from `native.identifier` of the game's `config.ts`; the switches map onto plugin fields through the pure `perfConfigOf` (`--lan` → `hub.deviceLan`, `--port`/`-p` → `hub.devicePort` (default 47600, 0 random), `--out`/`-o` → `collector.out` (default `.moku/perf`), `--every` → `collector.everyS` (1–3600, default 10), `--no-ui` → `pages.toolsPage: false`). It calls `hub.listenDevices({ confirm, routes: { "/": the no-game page } })`, prints the ready block (Phones `127.0.0.1:<port> · adb reverse every 2 s`, LAN, Tools `http://127.0.0.1:<port><path>/#render`, Logs, Engine; the token never; device mode is perf's there, so the tools page says "Confirm in the terminal that runs moku-editor perf" and has no local preview), then `pages.attachPerf(output)`: per phone log a header line (`◉ <model> · <backend> · engine <id> · build <id> · adb <address>`, `● REC → <file>`), a STALE warning once when the phone's engine differs from `files.engine().id`, a digest line at most every 5 s (`garden/boss  @60  54 fps  p90 18.2  gpu 6.1  spikes 2 (upload, gc?)  38.0 °C  · 1 840 lines`), `○ <model> left …` on `away`, `■ <model> · <n> lines → <file>` on `done`. The pairing prompt (`perf/prompt.ts`) asks for the four-digit code a LAN phone shows (`node:readline/promises` behind `PerfDeps.ask`, the known MC1 exception); an empty Enter, another code or a cut question refuses; a phone that prints its own code into its model, engine or build is refused without a question. Ctrl+C: `.moku/perf.json` goes first, then `hub.stopDevices()` → `collector.settled()` → `editor.stop()`, then one summary table per log. `.moku/perf.json` `{ version: 1, pid, port, path, token, lan, startedAt }` (0600, temp file and rename, removed on stop): `perf mark` reads it, checks the pid, refuses a host other than 127.0.0.1, and posts the label to `http://127.0.0.1:<port><path>/perf/mark` with `authorization: Bearer <token>` (200 `✓ mark "boss" in N log(s)`; 401 `The running perf has another token.`; no run `No moku-editor perf runs in this folder.`). `perf summary <log>` prints `summaryText(summarize(parsePerfLog(text)))` (a file without a header or sample: `<log> is not a moku perf log (v1).`); `perf compare <a> <b>` prints `compareText` by screen and rate, then one warning counting the screens that got worse by 10 % or more (exit 0). Every argument error is two lines with the usage, exit 2.

Exit codes: 0 help, `mcp-config`, `mcp` after stdin ended or a SIGINT/SIGTERM, or serving; the child's code after a re-spawn or the engine page's re-run; 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) when the engine form gets the signal before its child is spawned, no child; 1 missing or bad HTML file, start failed, port in use, the engine page not written or its keys watch not started; 2 bad arguments, or no html file and a root that is not a moku-game folder. Binds 127.0.0.1 only; the token is never printed.

Discovery file: (`moku-editor perf` never touches it, so the MCP bridge never mistakes a perf run for a served game.) After `Bun.serve` the bin writes `<root>/.moku/editor.json` `{ version: 1, pid, port, url, ws, token, root, html, startedAt }` (type `EditorDiscovery`, mode 0600, temp file then rename) and removes it on SIGINT/SIGTERM and in an `exit` listener, only while it still carries this pid. A bin killed with SIGKILL leaves it; the MCP bridge treats a dead pid as no bin. Add `.moku/` to the game's `.gitignore`.

`mcp-config` prints the `.mcp.json` snippet, a blank line and the `claude mcp add` line, then exits 0:

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "moku-editor": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "bunx",
      "args": ["moku-editor", "mcp", "web/index.html", "--port", "3000"]
    }
  }
}

claude mcp add moku-editor -- bunx moku-editor mcp web/index.html --port 3000
```

MCP bridge (`moku-editor mcp`, `src/plugins/pages/mcp/`, D-31): a separate process, not a plugin; a hub **tools client** (`${ws}?token=…&kind=tools`, `Origin: http://127.0.0.1:<port>`), so the hub's session choice, input checks and files sandbox apply as for the tools page. Newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 on stdio; stdout carries only protocol frames, logs go to stderr.

- `initialize` → `{ protocolVersion, capabilities: { tools: { listChanged: true }, logging: {} }, serverInfo: { name: "moku-editor", version }, instructions }` (`instructions`: which tools are generic, which are command doors, that cheat_* and raw_* change the game outside its rules, that the list changes when the game reloads, and that `moku_device`, `moku_show`, `moku_select` and `moku_hot_reload` drive the editor itself while `moku_files_find` and `moku_project` read the project index); versions `2025-11-25`, `2025-06-18`, `2025-03-26` (the client's when listed, else `2025-11-25`). `ping` and `logging/setLevel` → `{}`. An unknown method → -32601, bad params → -32602, a line that is not JSON → -32700. Notifications are never answered; `notifications/cancelled { requestId }` aborts that call. `notifications/progress` during `moku_wait` and `moku_series` when the request has `_meta.progressToken`; `notifications/tools/list_changed` only when the door tools change (below); a change before `notifications/initialized` is sent once right after it. `tools/list` is the generic tools, then the door tools; the first one waits at most 3 s for the door tools. A door tool that is gone answers `isError` "`<name>` is gone: the game changed. Call moku_manifest, or moku_run { id }."
- Who ran it: an `initialize` hands the MCP client's name (`clientInfo.title` when it has text, Claude Code: `"Claude Code"`, else `clientInfo.name`) to the hub as the editor-channel notification `client { name }`, sent again on every connection the bridge opens later. The hub stamps the bridge's runs `from: "mcp"` with that `client`, so an agent's `editor.record` reads `startedBy: { by: "agent", name: "Claude Code" }`.
- Claude Code 2.1.280 (recorded in `src/plugins/pages/__tests__/fixtures/claude-*.json`): it sends `server/discover` (draft protocol 2026-07-28) first, gets -32601, then `initialize` with `protocolVersion: "2025-11-25"` and id 0, `notifications/initialized` and `tools/list`.
- Which bin: a live `.moku/editor.json` under `--root` (default the working directory) wins. Without one the bridge starts `moku-editor <html> --port <port> --root <root> [--no-hmr]` detached (output in `.moku/editor.log`, 0600), when it knows a game html (argv, else the last discovery file it saw, else, in a moku-game folder, the engine page `<root>/.moku/index.html`: a root with `index.ts` and `config.ts`, `isGameFolder` of `pages/discovery.ts`, D-63; so `moku-editor mcp --root <game>` with no html and no `.moku/` starts the engine page, at startup and on `moku_start {}`); the html `<root>/.moku/index.html` (the engine page) is left out, so the bin starts in the engine form `moku-editor --port <port> --root <root> [--no-hmr]` and re-runs under `--config=<root>/.moku/bunfig.toml` (D-51); port `--port`, else the last port, else 3000; it waits at most 15 s for the discovery file and owns that bin. Without an html, in a root that is no moku-game folder, tools answer `isError` "moku-editor is not running. Start it (`bunx moku-editor web/index.html --port 3000`) or call moku_start."
