   * app.bridge.link(); // { mode: "connecting", address: "192.168.1.5:47600" } until the socket opens
   * ```
   */
  connect(address: string): void;
};
~~~

### 7.7 capture — agent, Standard, opt-in

- depends: `[registryPlugin]`. Lifecycle: `createState`, `onInit` (adds four commands), `onStop` (ends a running series). No app api.
- Commands: `editor.capture` (`{ maxWidth: "number?", key: "string?", rect: "json?", format: "string?", quality: "number?" }`, effect `read`, value `Shot`; JPEG 0.8 by default, `key` (through `game.locate`/`game.rect`) or `rect` crops plus 8 px, unknown key -32602; `png` keeps the lossless path; a picture that fails to decode stays PNG), `editor.series` (`{ durationMs: "number", intervalMs: "number" }`, effect `read`, value `SeriesValue`), `editor.seriesStop` (`{}`, effect `read`, value `{ stopped: boolean }`), `editor.sheet` (`{ frames: "number", everyMs: "number", maxWidth: "number?", format: "string?", quality: "number?" }`, effect `read`, value `Sheet`, JPEG by default).
- Every shot runs the door command `game.capture` (needs `__MOKU_GAME_DEV__`). The picture is the PNG data URL the door answers (game 0.1) or the string `png` of `{ png, legend? }` (game 0.4); anything else is -32000 "gave no picture". A series plans `max(1, floor(durationMs / intervalMs))` shots, never overlapping, one series at a time.
- `maxWidth` (a whole number 64–4096, else -32602 field `maxWidth`): a wider picture is shrunk in the page to `maxWidth` pixels wide, aspect kept (`createImageBitmap`, then an `OffscreenCanvas` or a canvas element, PNG data URL). A page that cannot do it answers the full picture and logs `capture:downscale-failed`.
- `editor.sheet` runs `game.capture { sheet: { frames, everyMs } }` once (game ≥ 0.4: the game lays the frames out in `ceil(sqrt(frames))` columns) and shrinks the sheet to `maxWidth`. `frames` is a whole number 2–12, `everyMs` a number 1–5000, else -32602 naming the field. `frame` is the frame after the last picture. MCP `moku_series` sends `maxWidth: 1080`.
- Events: none. Logs: `capture:series-large`, `capture:shots-skipped`, `capture:downscale-failed` (warn).

~~~ts
/**
 * A plan above this many shots logs `capture:series-large` and still runs.
 */
export const WARN_SHOTS = 200;

/**
 * The door command every shot runs.
 */
export const CAPTURE_ID = "game.capture";

/**
 * The id of the one-shot command, named in its errors.
 */
export const SHOT_ID = "editor.capture";

/**
 * The id of the contact-sheet command, named in its errors.
 */
export const SHEET_ID = "editor.sheet";

/**
 * The fewest pictures a contact sheet takes (the game's own limit).
 */
export const MIN_SHEET_FRAMES = 2;

/**
 * The most pictures a contact sheet takes (the game's own limit).
 */
export const MAX_SHEET_FRAMES = 12;

/**
 * The shortest game time between two pictures of a contact sheet, in ms.
 */
export const MIN_SHEET_EVERY_MS = 1;

/**
 * The longest game time between two pictures of a contact sheet, in ms.
 */
export const MAX_SHEET_EVERY_MS = 5000;

/**
 * The smallest `maxWidth` editor.capture and editor.sheet accept, in pixels.
 */
export const MIN_MAX_WIDTH = 64;

/**
 * The largest `maxWidth` editor.capture and editor.sheet accept, in pixels.
 */
export const MAX_MAX_WIDTH = 4096;

/**
 * Capture configuration.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ plugins: [capturePlugin], pluginConfigs: { capture: { maxDurationMs: 10_000 } } });
 * ```
 */
export type Config = {
  /** Longest series accepted, in ms. Default 20000. */
  maxDurationMs: number;
  /** Shortest interval accepted, in ms. Default 16. */
  minIntervalMs: number;
};

/**
 * The game page viewport of a shot (not the tools-side DeviceSpec).
 */
export type Device = {
  readonly w: number;
  readonly h: number;
  readonly orientation: "portrait" | "landscape";
};

/**
 * Value of `editor.capture`.
 */
export type Shot = { readonly image: string; readonly frame: number; readonly device: Device };

/**
 * Value of `editor.sheet`: the contact sheet (one JPEG or PNG data URL), the frame of the last picture and
 * the device.
 */
export type Sheet = { readonly image: string; readonly frame: number; readonly device: Device };

/**
 * One shot of a series, tagged with its real frame and real time.
 */
export type SeriesShot = { readonly image: string; readonly frame: number; readonly atMs: number };

/**
 * Value of `editor.series` (R2).
 */
export type SeriesValue = { readonly shots: readonly SeriesShot[]; readonly device: Device };
~~~

### 7.8 files — server, Standard

- depends: none (first server plugin). Lifecycle: `onInit` (`validateFilesConfig`), `onStart` (opens the project index of the root, not awaited; `find` waits for it), `onStop` (ends the watch, closes the index, state off `"stopped"`, nothing emitted).
- Node built-ins only; no `Bun.*`. Limits (`io.ts`): `MAX_TEXT_BYTES` 2 MiB, `MAX_BINARY_BYTES` 16 MiB, `MAX_PATH_LENGTH` 1024. Image extensions: `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.webp`, `.gif`.
- Sandbox order: lexical → deny → allow (files only; image and `.moku/captures/` rules for binaries) → real path under the real root → kind.
- `writeDataUrl(path, dataUrl)` decodes the files-channel data URL (`decodeDataUrl` in `binary.ts`, not exported from the plugin) for `hub`.
- Project index (D-38, D-40, D-48): `openProject({ root })` of `@moku-labs/game/project`; its watch emits every batch of file changes. The index is the only source of code locations; off is an error state, not a fallback. On: `defs` (every key but `jsx:` → def paths), `uses` (`node:`/`style:` keys → use paths), `broken` (path → first parse error), `manifest`, `revision`, `previous`, `change`. Off reasons: `"disabled"` (`project: false`), `"@moku-labs/game 0.7.0 or newer is needed for the project index"`, the bare message of a rejected open (no `typescript`, bad root), `"not opened"` before start, `"stopped"` after stop.
- `find(key)` (files channel `find { key }`): the `ProjectFound[]` of a key, `line` and `range` read from disk now, `hash` = the `version` of `read`, `broken: true` when the file does not parse now; answers outside the sandbox are dropped; `[]` for an unknown key; key over 512 chars -32602; index off -32008 `"project index off: <reason>"`. `project()` is the last state. The editor's own writes are not fed to the index; other tabs hear them through the next watch batch.
- Version check (D-45): `write(path, text, version)` compares the version right before the rename, after the temp file is written; a conflict removes the temp file and rejects -32005. An external write between that hash and the rename is still overwritten (window narrowed, not closed).
- Engine fingerprint (engine spec 10 E2): `engine()` answers the computer's `EngineInfo` `{ id, version, dist, patch? }` of the `@moku-labs/game` the root resolves (`id` `"unknown"` when none); `refreshEngine()` reads it again (the hub calls it after a pairing). The hub publishes it as `editor.engine`; a phone's `__MOKU_GAME_ENGINE__` that differs reads STALE.
- Events: emits `files:written`, `files:project`. Logs: `files:emit-failed`, `files:project-on { files, keys, ms }` (info; the bin prints it), `files:project-off { reason }` (error, once).

~~~ts
/**
 * Resolved config of the files plugin. Shallow-merged; arrays replace the default entirely.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ pluginConfigs: { files: { root: `${import.meta.dir}/..` } } });
 * ```
 */
export type FilesConfig = {
  /** Project root. Absolute, or relative to process.cwd() at init. Default ".". */
  root: string;
  /** Globs (relative to root, posix) a file must match to be read or written. */
  allow: readonly string[];
  /** Globs that are never listed, read or written. Matched case-insensitively. */
  deny: readonly string[];
  /** Open the project index of the root on start. `false` leaves it off as `"disabled"`. */
  project: boolean;
};

/**
 * What a write was about, classified from its path.
 */
export type WrittenKind = "code" | "style" | "layout" | "capture" | "other";

/**
 * Payload of the global server event `files:written`.
 */
export type FilesWritten = {
  readonly path: string;
  readonly bytes: number;
  readonly kind: WrittenKind;
};

/**
 * The files api (`app.files`, `ctx.require(filesPlugin)`). Every rejection is an
 * `Error & WireError` built with the protocol's wireError.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const { text, version } = await app.files.read("features/ui/styles.ts");
 * ```
 */
export type FilesApi = {
  /**
   * Lists the direct children of a folder inside the project root.
   *
   * @param dir - Relative folder path; `""` or `"."` for the root.
   * @returns Folders first, then allowed files, each sorted by path. `size` is 0 for folders.
   * @throws {Error} -32004 `forbidden_path` when a sandbox rule refuses the path, -32601
   * `unknown_id` when the folder is missing.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The files panel opens the `src/nodes` folder of the tree.
   * await app.files.list("src/nodes"); // [{ path: "src/nodes/await-intent.ts", kind: "file", size: 812 }, …]
   * ```
   */
  list(dir: string): Promise<FileEntry[]>;

  /**
   * Reads a regular file as UTF-8 (invalid bytes become U+FFFD) with its version: the lowercase
   * hex sha1 of the bytes. Max 2 MiB.
   *
   * @param path - Relative file path.
   * @returns `{ text, version }`.
   * @throws {Error} -32004 `forbidden_path`, -32601 `unknown_id` when missing, -32000 over 2 MiB.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // Load a style file before editing it; keep the version for the save.
   * const { text, version } = await app.files.read("features/ui/styles.ts");
   * ```
   */
  read(path: string): Promise<FileText>;

  /**
   * Atomic text write. Missing parent folders are created inside the root. Emits `files:written`
   * after the rename. Max 2 MiB.
   *
   * @param path - Relative file path.
   * @param text - The new content.
   * @param version - Optional version from the last read; a stale one fails with -32005.
   * @returns `{ path, bytes, version }` of the written file.
   * @throws {Error} -32004 `forbidden_path`, -32005 `version_conflict` when the file changed
   * meanwhile, -32602 `invalid_input` (`field: "text"`) over 2 MiB.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // Save the edited text only if nobody changed the file since it was read.
   * const { version } = await app.files.read("features/ui/styles.ts");
   * await app.files.write("features/ui/styles.ts", edited, version); // { path, bytes, version }
   * ```
   */
  write(path: string, text: string, version?: string): Promise<WriteResult>;

  /**
   * Atomic image write, only under `.moku/captures/` and only for png, jpg, jpeg, webp and gif.
   * Missing parent folders are created. Emits `files:written` with `kind: "capture"`. Max 16 MiB.
   *
   * @param path - Relative capture path.
   * @param bytes - The image bytes.
   * @returns `{ path, bytes, version }` of the written image.
   * @throws {Error} -32004 `forbidden_path` outside `.moku/captures/` or without an image
   * extension, -32602 `invalid_input` (`field: "data"`) over 16 MiB.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // Store a board screenshot the capture panel took.
   * await app.files.writeBinary(".moku/captures/2026-10-05/0846-board.png", bytes);
   * ```
   */
  writeBinary(path: string, bytes: Uint8Array): Promise<WriteResult>;

  /**
   * Decodes a `data:image/(png|jpeg|webp|gif);base64,…` URL and writes the image with
   * `writeBinary`. The mime must match the extension of `path`. Same limits, errors and event as
   * `writeBinary`.
   *
   * @param path - Relative capture path; its extension must match the mime of the data URL.
   * @param dataUrl - The image as a base64 data URL.
   * @returns `{ path, bytes, version }` of the written image.
   * @throws {Error} -32004 `forbidden_path` for a path that is not an image, outside
   * `.moku/captures/`; -32602 `invalid_input` (`field: "data"`) for a data URL that is not a
   * base64 image, a mime that does not match the path, or over 16 MiB.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // hub serves the files-channel `writeBinary { path, data }` of a tools page.
   * const files = ctx.require(filesPlugin);
   * await files.writeDataUrl(".moku/captures/2026-10-05/f12-full.jpg", "data:image/jpeg;base64,/9j/4AAQ…");
   * // { path: ".moku/captures/2026-10-05/f12-full.jpg", bytes: 48213, version: "3f7a…" }
   * ```
   */
  writeDataUrl(path: string, dataUrl: string): Promise<WriteResult>;

  /**
   * Reads an image back as a data URL with its version (R3). Emits nothing. Max 16 MiB.
   *
   * @param path - Relative image path.
   * @returns `{ dataUrl, version }`.
   * @throws {Error} -32004 `forbidden_path` without an image extension, -32601 `unknown_id` when
   * missing, -32000 over 16 MiB.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // Show a stored capture again.
   * const { dataUrl } = await app.files.readBinary(".moku/captures/2026-10-05/0846-board.png");
   * // dataUrl: "data:image/png;base64,…"
   * ```
   */
  readBinary(path: string): Promise<FileBinary>;

  /**
   * Synchronous full sandbox check, as for a write. A missing file gives the path it would have.
   *
   * @param path - Relative file path.
   * @returns The real absolute path.
   * @throws {Error} -32004 `forbidden_path` when a sandbox rule refuses the path.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // Turn a project path into the absolute path an "Open in editor" link needs.
   * app.files.resolve("src/main.ts"); // "/home/dev/game/src/main.ts"
   * ```
   */
  resolve(path: string): string;

  /**
   * The real, symlink-resolved project root (R3), for "Open in editor" links.
   *
   * @returns The absolute root.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // pages puts the root into the tools boot JSON.
   * const files = ctx.require(filesPlugin);
   * const boot = { root: files.root() }; // { root: "/home/dev/game" }
   * ```
   */
  root(): string;

  /**
   * Where a key of the project index lives, with lines read from the files on disk now. Waits
   * for the open that started with the app. Answers the files the sandbox lets it read only.
   *
   * @param key - A project-index key, at most 512 characters: `node:board/merge`,
   *   `jsx:settingsBoard`, `textStyle:ui.title`, `style:features/ui/popup.tsx#popupScreen`.
   * @returns One answer per place, in the index's order; `[]` for a key the index does not know.
   *   `hash` equals the `version` of `read`; `broken` when the file does not parse now.
   * @throws {Error} -32602 `invalid_input` (`field: "key"`) for a key that is not a string or is
   *   too long, -32008 `not_installed` (`project index off: <reason>`) while the index is off.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // hub serves the files-channel `find { key }` of a tools page.
   * const files = ctx.require(filesPlugin);
   * await files.find("node:main/open"); // [{ path: "features/settings/nodes.ts", binding: "open", line: 3, … }]
   * ```
   */
  find(key: string): Promise<ProjectFound[]>;

  /**
   * The project state last announced with `files:project`: on with its revision and key maps, or
   * off with a reason (`"not opened"` before start, `"disabled"`, `"stopped"`, why the open failed).
   *
   * @returns The state.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // A server plugin checks the index before it answers a location.
   * const state = ctx.require(filesPlugin).project();
   * if (state.state === "on") state.defs["node:board/merge"]; // ["nodes/merge.ts"]
   * ```
   */
  project(): ProjectState;

  /**
   * The engine of this computer's project: the installed `@moku-labs/game`, by the recipe of the
   * engine's `__MOKU_GAME_ENGINE__` (version + hash of its dist and patch). Computed on start;
   * `refreshEngine()` renews it. The hub publishes it as `editor.engine`.
   *
   * @returns The fingerprint; `{ id: "unknown", … }` when the game is not installed under the root.
   * @throws {Error} `[moku-editor] files.engine() needs a started app.` before the first start (a
   * lifecycle error).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The perf command prints the computer's engine next to each phone's.
   * editor.files.engine().id; // "0.14.12+9c41e0"
   * ```
   */
  engine(): EngineInfo;

  /**
   * Computes the fingerprint again when the last run is older than 2 s (ENGINE_REFRESH_MS), else
   * answers the kept one. The hub calls it when a device pairs or reconnects (a reinstall during a
   * long perf run).
   *
   * @returns The fingerprint, fresh or kept.
   * @throws {Error} The `engine()` lifecycle error before the first start.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The hub, when a phone pairs: publish the engine again only when its id changed.
   * const info = await ctx.require(filesPlugin).refreshEngine(); // { id: "0.14.13+1ab7f2", version: "0.14.13", dist: "1ab7f2…" }
   * ```
   */
  refreshEngine(): Promise<EngineInfo>;
};
~~~

### 7.9 hub — server, Complex

- depends: `[filesPlugin]`. Lifecycle: `onInit` (validate config, allowed origins), `onStart` (new token, silent check every `min(1000, silentAfterMs / 2)` ms, publishes `files.engine()` as `engine`), `onStop` (tears device mode down without emit, closes every socket with 1001 `editor stopping`).
- `serve` throws: before start, on a second call, with a `websocket` option, with `unix` or `tls`, with a hostname other than `127.0.0.1`/`localhost`, with a game route under the editor path.
- Guard modes: `upgrade` (Origin required), `same-origin` (Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site checked when present), `navigate`.
- Session choice for a game request without `session`: one open session wins; with several, the only embedded one wins; else -32003.
- Heartbeats (with a well-formed `heap` kept) and `tap { x, y, at }` notifications are forwarded to every tools connection with `session`. A malformed heartbeat, value or tap is one strike; ten strikes close with 1008.
- Liveness readout (M4): each `SessionInfo` of `sessions()` and of the `sessions` notification carries `heartbeat: { frame, paused, silent }` once the session has sent a heartbeat. The list is re-sent when a session's `paused` or `silent` flips, not on every frame.
- Manifest hash (D-37): on `hello` the hub sets `manifestHash = commandsHash(manifest)` on the session; every `SessionInfo` of `sessions()` and of the `sessions` notification carries it. The MCP bridge rebuilds its door tools only when it moves. A refused command (`allowed: false`) hashes with its `reason`, so a read-only build's hash differs from the dev page's.
- Deadline of a forwarded call: `callTimeoutMs`, plus `input.durationMs` for a `run` of `editor.series` and `input.frames × input.everyMs` for a `run` of `editor.sheet`, capped at +60 s (the same rule as bridge and link).
- `publish(method, params)`: `hotReload`, `selection`, `project`, `engine`, `devices` and `deviceTelemetry` (connect's) go to every tools connection now as `editor` notifications; the last value per method is kept and replayed right after each tools hello; the held `deviceTelemetry` is dropped when device mode stops.
- Run stamping (spec 11 § 5.1): an agent whose `hello` names `run-from` (`capsOf`) gets every `run` a tools connection sends as `{ id, input?, from, client? }`: `from: "page"` from the editor page, `"mcp"` from a plain tools connection, with `client`, the name its `client { name }` notification gave (`clientNameOf`). A `from` or `client` in the tools client's own params is dropped (`runParamsOf`); an agent without `run-from` gets `{ id, input? }`.
- Editor methods of other plugins (H2): `addEditorMethods({ "<plugin>.<verb>": handler })`, in `onInit`, before `serve()` / `listenDevices()`; reached by tools connections only (an agent's or a phone's request is -32007); order `selection` → the relayed requests → a registered method → -32601; a throw is answered through `toWireError`. connect registers `connect.*` with it.
- Project index: hooks `files:project` and publishes it as the `editor` notification `project`. The files channel routes `find { key }` to `files.find` (missing key -32602). The MCP bridge ignores `editor.project`.
- Device mode (`listenDevices({ confirm, routes? })`, the `moku-editor perf` command): an adb listener on `127.0.0.1:<devicePort>` (the tools page and `{path}/ws`) and, with `deviceLan`, a LAN listener on `<lanAddress>:<devicePort>` (`{path}/ws` only). A device upgrade needs `kind=agent role=device`, a Host of the listener and an Origin in `deviceOrigins`. Without credentials the socket pairs: `pair { code, device }` first within 5 s (`PAIR_FIRST_MS`), the person confirms (`confirm(request, signal)`, one ticket at a time; an adb phone under `pairing: "lan"` at once), then `paired { device, token, engine }`. A stale token is upgraded and closed 4401 `unpaired`. A paired socket is an ordinary agent session with `SessionInfo.device` plus `perf.lines` (checked: `log` `^[\w.-]{1,128}$`, `from` a safe integer, 1–5000 lines; duplicates below the next index skipped, a jump forward is a `gap`), always answered with `perf.ack { log, next, n }`. Limits: 16 paired devices, 4 waiting pairings, 4 open pairing sockets per address (429 `busy`), a 10 s cooldown after a refusal, 32 logs per device. `stopDevices()` emits `closed` per device, then `stopped`. `listenLan()` adds the LAN listener while device mode runs (on the adb listener's real port, `{path}/ws` only; idempotent; no LAN address or a taken port is an `Error`), `stopLan()` closes the LAN phones 1001 `lan off` (they stay paired) and keeps the phones by wire; both emit `listening` with the new `listen`. Every paired device connection is pinged once a second; the pong sets `LinkedDevice.latencyMs` (`null` before the first). A `pair` may carry `appId`; it is kept on `SessionDevice.appId`.
- Runtime-free `hub/protocol/`: the device-link and tools-link types and their parsers (section 3), imported by bridge, overlay, connect, the collector and the MCP bridge as `../hub/protocol`, never the hub index.
- Events: emits `hub:session` (global) and `hub:device` (per-plugin: `listening`, `connected`, `lines`, `closed`, `stopped`; the collector and connect hook it); hooks `files:project`. Logs also `hub:devices-lan` (info), `hub:tools-client` (debug). Logs: `hub:started`, `hub:refused`, `hub:session-open`, `hub:session-silent`, `hub:session-alive`, `hub:emit-failed`, `hub:devices-on`, `hub:devices-off`, `hub:paired`, `hub:pair-refused`, `hub:pair-failed`, `hub:device-unpaired`, `hub:engine-refresh-failed`, debug lines.

~~~ts
/**
 * Hub configuration.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ pluginConfigs: { hub: { devicePort: 47600, deviceLan: true } } });
 * ```
 */
export type HubConfig = {
  /** URL prefix of every editor route. Starts with "/", no trailing slash. */
  path: string;
  /**
   * Extra exact origins allowed to upgrade and to call same-origin routes (normal and adb
   * listener; never devices).
   */
  allowOrigins: readonly string[];
  /** Deadline of a forwarded call before it fails with -32002 (retryable). */
  callTimeoutMs: number;
  /** A session with no heartbeat for this long is marked silent (65 s after a paused beat, R6). */
  silentAfterMs: number;
  /** Port of the device listeners (127.0.0.1 and, with deviceLan, the LAN address); 0 = a random free port. */
  devicePort: number;
  /** Also listen on the computer's LAN address (device upgrades only, pairing confirmed by the person). */
  deviceLan: boolean;
  /** The LAN address to bind; undefined picks the first non-internal IPv4 (en*, wl*, eth* first). */
  lanAddress: string | undefined;
  /** Exact Origins a device's WebView sends (scheme + host, lower case). */
  deviceOrigins: readonly string[];
  /** "lan": only LAN phones are asked, an adb phone is confirmed at once; "always": every phone is asked. */
  pairing: "lan" | "always";
  /** How long a pairing waits for the person before it is refused, in ms. */
  pairTimeoutMs: number;
};

/**
 * Payload of the global server event `hub:session`, and params of the `session` notification.
 */
export type HubSession = {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly game: string;
  readonly open: boolean;
  readonly reason?: "bye" | "game_reloaded";
};

/**
 * Editor routes registered through addRoutes (pages) and merged by serve.
 */
export type EditorRoutes = Readonly<Record<string, Response | RouteHandler>>;

/**
 * Which request check guard applies (R3).
 */
export type GuardMode = "upgrade" | "same-origin" | "navigate";

/**
 * What the game passes to serve(). Unknown keys pass through to Bun untouched.
 */
export type ServeOptions = {
  readonly port?: number;
  readonly hostname?: string;
  readonly development?: boolean | { readonly hmr?: boolean; readonly console?: boolean };
  /**
   * The game's routes, passed to Bun as they are. Structural on purpose: this type ships in the
   * server `.d.mts`, and Bun's `Serve.Routes` is a namespace type the d.ts bundle drops
   * (skeleton-conventions §3); Bun.serve checks the values (HTML imports, files, method maps).
   */
  readonly routes?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
  readonly fetch?: (req: Request, server: HubServer) => Response | Promise<Response>;
  /** Refused at runtime too: the editor owns the one websocket handler. */
  readonly websocket?: undefined;
  readonly [key: string]: unknown;
};

/**
 * A method `publish` sends to the tools pages (R6, A5): `"hotReload"`, `"selection"`, `"project"`
 * or `"engine"`, the keys of the protocol's PublishParams. The hub publishes `project` (from
 * `files:project`) and `engine` (from `files.engine()`) itself. The protocol's PublishMethod,
 * re-exported under hub's name.
 */
export type { PublishMethod } from "../registry/protocol";

/**
 * What the CLI's pairing callback is asked: the code the phone shows (to compare with what the
 * person types), what the phone is and where it came from.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const request: PairRequest = { code: "4821", model: "SM-A266B", address: "192.168.1.23", link: "lan", engine: "0.14.12+9c41e0", build: "debug-20261014T160000Z" };
 * ```
 */
export type PairRequest = {
  /** The code the phone shows, to compare with what the person types. */
  readonly code: string;
  /** The normalized model, e.g. "SM-A266B"; null when the phone sent none. */
  readonly model: string | null;
  /** The phone's address as the hub saw it. */
  readonly address: string;
  readonly link: DeviceLinkKind;
  /** The phone's engine fingerprint, as it reported it. */
  readonly engine: string | null;
  /** The phone's build id, as it reported it. */
  readonly build: string | null;
  /** The phone's app id, as it reported it ("com.mokulabs.timber.debug"); absent when it sent none. */
  readonly appId?: string;
};

/**
 * Asks the person whether a phone may link. Resolves true to pair it. The signal aborts when the
 * phone leaves, the wait runs out or device mode stops; the answer is then ignored. A throw or a
 * rejection counts as a refusal.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const confirm: PairConfirm = async (request, signal) =>
 *   (await ask(`${request.model ?? "A phone"} at ${request.address} asks to link. Type its code: `, signal)) === request.code;
 * ```
 */
export type PairConfirm = (request: PairRequest, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<boolean>;

/**
 * Options of `listenDevices`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const options: DeviceListenOptions = { confirm: askInTerminal, routes: { "/": new Response("No game is served here.") } };
 * ```
 */
export type DeviceListenOptions = {
  /** The pairing callback (the CLI's terminal prompt). */
  readonly confirm: PairConfirm;
  /**
   * Non-editor routes of the adb listener (e.g. "/" for a page that says no game is served here).
   * Structural like ServeOptions.routes: no Bun namespace type in a shipped shape; Bun.serve
   * checks the values.
   */
  readonly routes?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
};

/**
 * Where device mode listens.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const listen: DeviceListen = { port: 47600, adb: "127.0.0.1:47600", lan: "192.168.1.5:47600" };
 * ```
 */
export type DeviceListen = {
  /** The real port of both listeners (the random one under `devicePort: 0`). */
  readonly port: number;
  /** The loopback listener, `127.0.0.1:<port>`. */
  readonly adb: string;
  /** The LAN listener, `<address>:<port>` (IPv6 in brackets); null without deviceLan. */
  readonly lan: string | null;
};

/**
 * A paired device as the hub reports it: a frozen copy, never the token.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const device: LinkedDevice = { id: "d-7f3a", model: "SM-A266B", link: "adb", address: "127.0.0.1", port: 47600, engine: "0.14.12+9c41e0", build: "debug-20261014T160000Z", pairedAt: 1791986083963, online: true, latencyMs: 9 };
 * ```
 */
export type LinkedDevice = SessionDevice & {
  /** Epoch ms of the pairing. */
  readonly pairedAt: number;
  /** Whether a connection is open now. */
  readonly online: boolean;
  /** The last WebSocket ping round trip in ms (pinged once a second); null before the first pong. */
  readonly latencyMs: number | null;
};

/**
 * A batch of a device's log, as the hub accepted it.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const lines: DeviceLines = { log: "perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl", from: 200, rx: 1791986090000, items: [], gap: 0, rejected: 0 };
 * ```
 */
export type DeviceLines = {
  /** The device log's name ("perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl"). */
  readonly log: string;
  /** Index of the first item in that log (after duplicates were skipped). */
  readonly from: number;
  /** Computer epoch ms when the batch arrived. */
  readonly rx: number;
  /**
   * The accepted PerfLogLine v1 objects, frozen. The hub's shallow guard vouches for `v` (a finite
   * number) and `kind` (1–32 characters) only, not a line's body: a reader switches on `kind` and
   * reads the fields it needs defensively.
   */
  readonly items: readonly PerfLogLine[];
  /** Lines the device lost before sending (from − next). */
  readonly gap: number;
  /** Items dropped as malformed. */
  readonly rejected: number;
};

/**
 * Why a device connection ended: a bye, a lost socket, a newer connection of the same device, or
 * device mode stopping.
 */
export type DeviceCloseReason = "bye" | "lost" | "replaced" | "stopped";

/**
 * Payload of the per-plugin event `hub:device`: device mode listening, a device connected, a log
 * batch, a device left, device mode stopped.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const event: HubDeviceEvent = { kind: "connected", device: { id: "d-7f3a", model: "SM-A266B", link: "adb", address: "127.0.0.1", port: 47600, engine: "0.14.12+9c41e0", build: "debug-20261014T160000Z", pairedAt: 1791986083963, online: true } };
 * ```
 */
export type HubDeviceEvent =
  | { readonly kind: "listening"; readonly listen: DeviceListen }
  | { readonly kind: "connected"; readonly device: LinkedDevice }
  | { readonly kind: "lines"; readonly device: LinkedDevice; readonly lines: DeviceLines }
  | { readonly kind: "closed"; readonly device: LinkedDevice; readonly reason: DeviceCloseReason }
  | { readonly kind: "stopped" };

/**
 * An editor-channel method another server plugin registers with `addEditorMethods` (H2). Only
 * tools connections (hub token, loopback Host and Origin) reach it; a throw or a rejection is
 * answered as a wire error.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // An editor method that answers its params and the tools connection that asked.
 * const echo: EditorMethod = async (params, caller) => ({ params: params ?? null, conn: caller.conn });
 * ```
 */
export type EditorMethod = (
  params: Json | undefined,
  caller: { readonly conn: number }
) => Promise<Json>;

/**
 * Editor methods by name, `<plugin>.<verb>`.
 */
export type EditorMethods = Readonly<Record<string, EditorMethod>>;

/**
 * The hub's per-plugin events, visible to plugins that list `hubPlugin` in `depends`.
 */
export type HubEvents = { readonly "hub:device": HubDeviceEvent };

/**
 * The hub api (`app.hub`, `ctx.require(hubPlugin)`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * Bun.serve(app.hub.serve({ port: 3000, routes: { "/": index }, fetch: serveAsset }));
 * ```
 */
export type HubApi = {
  /**
   * Wraps the game's `Bun.serve` options: `127.0.0.1` forced, then the game's routes, the routes
   * from `addRoutes` and `{path}/ws` merged, and the websocket handler added. Without a game
   * `fetch` the fallback answers 404. Unknown option keys pass through to Bun.
   *
   * @param options - The game's serve options.
   * @returns Options ready for `Bun.serve`.
   * @throws {Error} `[moku-editor] …` before start, on a second call, with a `websocket`, `unix` or
   * `tls` option, with a hostname other than `127.0.0.1` / `localhost`, and with a game route
   * under the editor path.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The game's dev server: one Bun.serve for the game and the editor, after await app.start().
   * Bun.serve(app.hub.serve({ port: 3000, routes: { "/": index }, fetch: serveAsset }));
   * ```
   */
  serve(options: ServeOptions): BunServeOptions;

  /**
   * The token of this start: 32 random bytes, base64url, 43 characters. A new one on every
   * start. Never logged.
   *
   * @returns The token.
   * @throws {Error} `[moku-editor] hub.token() needs a started app.` before start and after stop.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // pages puts the token into the tools boot JSON on every page request.
   * const hub = ctx.require(hubPlugin);
   * const token = hub.token(); // 43 characters, e.g. "Hk3…"
   * ```
   */
  token(): string;

  /**
   * A fresh list of the open game sessions ordered by `connectedAt`. Each carries `manifestHash`,
   * the `commandsHash` of its manifest computed on hello (D-37). A session that has sent a
   * heartbeat carries the readout `heartbeat: { frame, paused, silent }`; a device session (a paired
   * phone) carries `device` with the device listener's port. Mutating the result does not change
   * the next call.
   *
   * @returns The open sessions.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // After the game page connected its bridge and sent its first heartbeat.
   * app.hub.sessions(); // [{ id: "s-7f3a", game: "merge-game 0.0.0", page: "http://127.0.0.1:3000/", embedded: true, connectedAt: 1790000000000, manifestHash: "4f528e73", heartbeat: { frame: 1840, paused: false, silent: false } }]
   * // A paired phone's session adds: device: { id: "d-7f3a", model: "SM-A266B", link: "adb", address: "127.0.0.1", port: 47600, engine: "0.14.12+9c41e0", build: "debug-20261014T160000Z" }
   * ```
   */
  sessions(): SessionInfo[];

  /**
   * The `{path}/ws` upgrade handler; `serve` already mounts it. Checks the path (404), the start
   * (503), the upgrade request (426), `guard(…, "upgrade")` (403), the token (401), the kind and
   * the role (400: `role=page` only with `kind=tools`), then upgrades.
   *
   * @param req - The request.
   * @param server - The Bun server.
   * @returns `undefined` after an upgrade, else the plain-text refusal.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // A game with its own Bun.serve mounts the upgrade itself.
   * Bun.serve({
   *   fetch: (req, server) => app.hub.fetch(req, server) ?? new Response("upgraded"),
   *   websocket: app.hub.websocket
   * });
   * ```
   */
  fetch(req: Request, server: HubServer): Response | undefined;

  /**
   * The one websocket handler of the server: 32 MiB frames, 60 s idle, no deflate.
   *
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // A game's own Bun.serve passes the editor's handler on.
   * Bun.serve({
   *   fetch: (req, server) => app.hub.fetch(req, server) ?? new Response("upgraded"),
   *   websocket: app.hub.websocket
   * });
   * ```
   */
  readonly websocket: HubWebSocketHandler;

  /**
   * Registers editor routes, merged by `serve` and by the adb listener of `listenDevices` (R3).
   * Call it in `onInit`. Keys are checked first, so a refused batch registers nothing.
   *
   * @param routes - Routes keyed by `path` or under `path + "/"`.
   * @throws {Error} `[moku-editor] …` after `serve` or `listenDevices`, on a key registered before,
   * on `{path}/ws`, and on a key outside the editor path.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // pages registers its routes in onInit, before hub.serve() freezes them.
   * const hub = ctx.require(hubPlugin);
   * hub.addRoutes({ [`${hub.path()}/hello`]: helloRoute });
   * ```
   */
  addRoutes(routes: EditorRoutes): void;

  /**
   * The shared Host / Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site check (R3). `upgrade` requires an allowed Origin;
   * `same-origin` and `navigate` check it when present; `same-origin` also wants Sec-Fetch-Site
   * `same-origin` or `none` when present. The origin `null` never matches.
   *
   * @param req - The request.
   * @param server - The Bun server (its port).
   * @param mode - Which rules apply.
   * @returns A 403 response, or `undefined` when allowed.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // A pages route refuses a cross-site request before it answers.
   * const refused = ctx.require(hubPlugin).guard(req, server, "same-origin");
   * if (refused) return refused; // 403 "forbidden"
   * ```
   */
  guard(req: Request, server: HubServer, mode: GuardMode): Response | undefined;

  /**
   * Sends server state to every tools page as the editor-channel notification `<method>` and
   * keeps it: a tools page that connects later gets the last value right after its
   * `sessions {list}`. Works before start too; the value waits for the first tools page. The value
   * is stored through `toWireValue`. A `null` selection goes out as a `selection` notification
   * without params (the wire refuses null params).
   *
   * @param method - The state: `"hotReload"`, `"selection"`, `"project"`, `"engine"`, `"devices"`
   * or `"deviceTelemetry"`.
   * @param params - Its value: a HotReload, a SelectionInfo or null for the selection, a
   * ProjectState (the hub publishes `project` itself from `files:project`), an EngineInfo (the
   * hub publishes `engine` itself from `files.engine()` on start and when a phone pairs), or
   * connect's DeviceDirectory or DeviceTelemetry. The held `deviceTelemetry` is dropped when device
   * mode stops, so a tools page never gets one of an older run.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // pages tells every tools page whether Bun reloads the game page on a save.
   * ctx.require(hubPlugin).publish("hotReload", { hmr: true, owner: "bin" });
   * // each tools socket gets {"jsonrpc":"2.0","channel":"editor","method":"hotReload","params":{"hmr":true,"owner":"bin"}}
   * ```
   */
  publish<M extends PublishMethod>(method: M, params: PublishParams[M]): void;

  /**
   * Closes every open socket, agent, tools and device, with one code and reason (a phone reconnects
   * with its device token), and resolves when Bun
   * reported every close (at most 500 ms). The hub keeps running: the token stays, and each
   * connection is forgotten when Bun reports its close, so its session or subscriptions end as on
   * any close. Clients reconnect on their own. Stop a server only after it resolves: a stop before
   * drops the close frame, and the client sees 1006 instead of the code.
   *
   * @param code - The close code: 1012 (service restart) for the bin's restart.
   * @param reason - The close reason the clients see.
   * @returns When every socket closed, or the wait ran out.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The bin, right before Bun's stop on a Hot reload switch (pages serve.ts).
   * await editor.hub.closeAll(1012, "editor restarting");
   * // the bridge and every tools page see close 1012 "editor restarting", log it at info and reconnect
   * ```
   */
  closeAll(code: number, reason: string): Promise<void>;

  /**
   * The editor path, `config.path` (R3).
   *
   * @returns The URL prefix of every editor route.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // pages keys its routes under the hub path.
   * ctx.require(hubPlugin).path(); // "/__editor"
   * ```
   */
  path(): string;

  /**
   * Turns device mode on: listens on 127.0.0.1:<devicePort> (the editor routes, the tools page and
   * the socket) and, with deviceLan, on the LAN address (device upgrades only). Phones connect as
   * `kind=agent role=device` from a deviceOrigins Origin and pair through `confirm`. Freezes the
   * editor routes. Emits `hub:device { kind: "listening" }`.
   *
   * @param options - The pairing callback and extra non-editor routes of the adb listener.
   * @returns The real port and the two addresses.
   * @throws {Error} The two-line `[moku-editor] …` lifecycle errors before start, when device mode
   * is on already, when deviceLan finds no LAN address, on a route under the editor path, and when
   * the port is in use (the error keeps `code: "EADDRINUSE"`).
   * @throws {TypeError} When `options.confirm` is not a function.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // moku-editor perf --lan, after await editor.start().
   * const listen = await editor.hub.listenDevices({ confirm: askInTerminal });
   * // { port: 47600, adb: "127.0.0.1:47600", lan: "192.168.1.5:47600" }
   * ```
   */
  listenDevices(options: DeviceListenOptions): Promise<DeviceListen>;

  /**
   * Turns device mode off: pending pairings are refused, device connections close with 1001
   * "device mode off", device tokens are forgotten, both listeners stop. Emits `closed` per
   * connected device, then `stopped`. A call while device mode is off does nothing. The editor
   * routes stay frozen.
   *
   * @returns When both listeners stopped (at most 500 ms).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The perf command's Ctrl+C turns phones off before it stops the editor.
   * await editor.hub.stopDevices();
   * editor.hub.devices(); // []
   * ```
   */
  stopDevices(): Promise<void>;

  /**
   * The paired devices of this device-mode run, ordered by pairedAt, as fresh frozen copies
   * without tokens.
   *
   * @returns The devices; [] while device mode is off.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // After a Galaxy A26 paired over adb reverse.
   * editor.hub.devices(); // [{ id: "d-7f3a", model: "SM-A266B", link: "adb", address: "127.0.0.1", port: 47600, engine: "0.14.12+9c41e0", build: "debug-20261014T160000Z", pairedAt: 1791986083963, online: true, latencyMs: 9 }]
   * ```
   */
  devices(): LinkedDevice[];

  /**
   * Adds the LAN listener while device mode runs: the computer's LAN address on the device port,
   * device upgrades only, pairing confirmed by the person. The adb listener and its phones stay.
   * The address is found as for `deviceLan`: `lanAddress`, else the first non-internal IPv4 of a
   * Wi-Fi or wired card. With the LAN listener on already it starts nothing and answers the current
   * listen. Logs `hub:devices-lan` and emits `hub:device { kind: "listening" }` with the new `lan`.
   *
   * @returns Where device mode listens now.
   * @throws {Error} `[moku-editor] hub.listenLan() needs device mode.` with `Call
   * hub.listenDevices() first.` while device mode is off; the no-LAN-address and port errors of
   * `listenDevices`.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // connect's "On the network": device mode is on by wire, now the Wi-Fi path too.
   * await ctx.require(hubPlugin).listenLan();
   * // { port: 47600, adb: "127.0.0.1:47600", lan: "192.168.1.5:47600" }
   * ```
   */
  listenLan(): Promise<DeviceListen>;

  /**
   * Removes the LAN listener: every LAN device connection closes with 1001 "lan off" (a paired one
   * is announced `closed` with reason `stopped` and stays paired), the listener stops, `lan` becomes
   * null and `hub:device { kind: "listening" }` goes out. Phones by wire keep their sessions. Does
   * nothing without a LAN listener.
   *
   * @returns When the LAN listener stopped (at most 500 ms).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // connect turns the Wi-Fi path off; the Galaxy A26 by wire stays linked.
   * const hub = ctx.require(hubPlugin);
   * await hub.stopLan();
   * hub.devices().filter(device => device.online).map(device => device.link); // ["adb"]
   * ```
   */
  stopLan(): Promise<void>;

  /**
   * Registers editor-channel methods of another server plugin (`connect.scan` …). Only tools
   * connections reach them (hub token, loopback Host and Origin): a game page's or a phone's
   * request is refused -32007, and the LAN listener has no tools socket. A tools request
   * `editor.<name>` runs the handler with its params and the caller's connection, counted as a
   * pending call; a throw or a rejection is answered as a wire error, and the answer is dropped when
   * the connection closed meanwhile. The hub's own `selection` and its relayed methods come first.
   * Names are checked first, so a refused batch registers nothing.
   *
   * @param methods - Name (`<plugin>.<verb>`) → handler.
   * @throws {Error} After `serve()` or `listenDevices()` (frozen with the routes), for a name
   * registered before, a name without a dot, and for `selection`, `select`, `device`, `show` and
   * `node` (two-line messages).
   * @throws {TypeError} When a handler is not a function.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // connect registers its methods in onInit, before the server starts.
   * ctx.require(hubPlugin).addEditorMethods({ "connect.scan": async () => ({ wire: [] }) });
   * // a tools page's request editor.connect.scan is answered { wire: [] }
   * ```
   */
  addEditorMethods(methods: EditorMethods): void;
};
~~~

### 7.10 connect — server, Complex

- depends: `[hubPlugin]`. Lifecycle: `onInit` (checks the config, a two-line `TypeError` per field; registers the editor methods with `hub.addEditorMethods`), `onStart` (with `wire: "auto"` only: the adb listener when `adb version` answers and the port is free; timers, adb children, CDP sockets and forwards start in the editor methods), `onStop` (frees them; no emit).
- What it does (spec 11 § 3): the tools page connects a phone without an agent or a terminal. It turns the hub's device mode on and off on request, supplies the hub's pairing confirm so a LAN phone is confirmed in the tools page (`confirmIn: "page"` while device mode is connect's, `"terminal"` while it is `moku-editor perf`'s), keeps and publishes the device directory, and for a wired phone a tools page watches attaches CDP to its WebView and publishes the wired telemetry.
- Editor methods (tools sockets only; unknown params -32602): `connect.scan {}` (renews the scan lease, starts the scan loop; answers the `DeviceDirectory` after the first round), `connect.wire {}` (device mode on with the adb listener; `{ listen }`), `connect.network {}` (device mode on, then the LAN listener; `{ listen }` with `lan`), `connect.off { lan? }` (the LAN listener off, else device mode off, only while it is connect's), `connect.confirm { ticket, code }` (pairs the asking phone when `code.trim()` is its code; `{ paired }`), `connect.refuse { ticket }`, `connect.watch { device }` (renews this connection's telemetry lease, attaches a wired linked device; `{ wired, reason? }`, reason `not-wired`, `ios`, `not-linked`, `adb-missing`, `ambiguous`), `connect.unwatch { device }`. Errors `port_in_use`, `no_lan` (-32000), `not_owner` (-32007), `no_ticket` (-32602).
- Published: `editor.devices` (`DeviceDirectory`: device mode and its owner, `confirmIn`, adb's state, the phones of `adb devices -l` with their phase `unauthorized`, `offline`, `ready`, `waiting`, `no-agent`, `linked`, the pairings asking without their codes, the linked devices with their session; only when it changed, at most every 250 ms) and `editor.deviceTelemetry` (`DeviceTelemetry`, once per tick of a watched device; also the per-plugin event `connect:telemetry`).
- Matching a phone: a ready phone adb lists is linked to an online linked adb device by model (one device and one phone of the model), else by app id (the linked devices' `SessionDevice.appId` against the phones' processes from `ps`, `.debug` stripped with `baseAppId`), else every phone of the model is `match: "ambiguous"`; never a guess.
- Wired telemetry: GPU clock and busy % (`/sys/kernel/gpu` Mali, `/sys/class/kgsl/kgsl-3d0` Adreno, `/sys/kernel/ged/hal` MediaTek, `/sys/class/devfreq/<name>`), CPU % per process (`/proc/<pid>/stat`: the game, its renderer, surfaceflinger), memory per process (`dumpsys meminfo`, every `meminfoEveryMs`), the JS heap (`cdp Runtime.getHeapUsage`, every `heapEveryMs`) and GCs inferred from heap drops of at least `gcDropMb`. A reading that fails is `available: false` with its reason; the others stay. The WebView's `performance.memory` is never read: it is frozen on an Android WebView.
- adb allowlist: every call is built by `adbArgs` from the `AdbCommand` union (`version`, `devices -l`, `getprop`, `/proc/net/unix`, `ps -A -o PID,NAME`, `head` of the allowed paths, `ls /sys/class/devfreq`, `dumpsys meminfo <pid>`, `forward tcp:0 localabstract:<socket>`, `forward --remove`); a refused token throws `[moku-editor] connect: refused adb token "<t>".` before anything runs. `reverse` stays the collector's.
- CDP security: only for a phone by wire a tools page watches, over an `adb forward` on this computer's loopback, from Bun with no Origin header; the client sends only `Runtime.getHeapUsage`, `Performance.enable`, `Performance.getMetrics`, `Memory.getDOMCounters` (and with `gcTrace` `Tracing.start` / `Tracing.end`); any other method throws `[moku-editor] connect: CDP method <m> is not allowed.`. The socket closes and the forward is removed when the lease ends, the device leaves, adb stops listing it, or the app stops.
- Limits: telemetry is Android by wire only (no iOS debug build in `@moku-labs/native` 0.3.9); "discovered" means plugged in over adb, asking to pair, or linked (no mDNS, no QR in v1); two phones running the same game stay `ambiguous`.
- Events: emits `connect:telemetry` (per-plugin; the collector hooks it); hooks the hub's per-plugin `hub:device` (`listening` → device mode and the scan loop, `connected` → the directory, `closed` → that device's telemetry detached, `stopped` → device mode off, the pairings asking answered false, every attach detached).

~~~ts
/**
 * Connect configuration (spec 11 § 3 Config). Flat: per-plugin config merges shallowly.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ pluginConfigs: { connect: { adb: "/opt/android/platform-tools/adb", wire: "auto" } } });
 * ```
 */
export type ConnectConfig = {
  /** The adb command, a name on PATH or a path. */
  adb: string;
  /** One adb call is killed after this many ms. */
  adbTimeoutMs: number;
  /** `adb devices -l` period while a scan lease or device mode is on. */
  scanEveryMs: number;
  /** A ready phone with no device session for this long reads "no debug game answered". */
  answerTimeoutMs: number;
  /** A scan or watch lease not renewed for this long ends. */
  leaseMs: number;
  /** The wired telemetry tick. */
  telemetryEveryMs: number;
  /** `dumpsys meminfo` period. */
  meminfoEveryMs: number;
  /** CDP Runtime.getHeapUsage period. */
  heapEveryMs: number;
  /** A heap drop of at least this many MB between two samples is an inferred GC. */
  gcDropMb: number;
  /**
   * Exact GC events through CDP Tracing (heavier). The CDP client then also accepts
   * `Tracing.start` / `Tracing.end`; the trace reading itself waits for a measurement on the A26
   * (decision 2026-10-16), so GCs stay inferred.
   */
  gcTrace: boolean;
  /** "auto": turn the adb listener on at start when adb is on PATH and the port is free. */
  wire: "manual" | "auto";
};

/**
 * One allowlisted adb command (spec 11 C7, A0–A10). Nothing else reaches adb: `adbArgs` builds the
 * argv from this union only and validates every token first.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const tick: AdbCommand = { kind: "head", serial: "R5CX30ABCDE", lines: 1, paths: ["/proc/stat", "/proc/23811/stat", "/sys/kernel/gpu/gpu_clock"] };
 * ```
 */
export type AdbCommand =
  | { readonly kind: "version" }
  | { readonly kind: "devices" }
  | { readonly kind: "getprop"; readonly serial: string }
  | { readonly kind: "unix-sockets"; readonly serial: string }
  | { readonly kind: "processes"; readonly serial: string }
  | {
      readonly kind: "head";
      readonly serial: string;
      readonly lines: number;
      readonly paths: readonly string[];
    }
  | { readonly kind: "devfreq"; readonly serial: string }
  | { readonly kind: "meminfo"; readonly serial: string; readonly pid: number }
  | { readonly kind: "forward"; readonly serial: string; readonly socket: string }
  | { readonly kind: "forward-remove"; readonly serial: string; readonly port: number };

/**
 * connect's per-plugin events, visible to plugins that list `connectPlugin` in `depends`.
 */
export type ConnectEvents = { readonly "connect:telemetry": DeviceTelemetry };

/**
 * What `connect.watch` answers: whether wired telemetry runs for the device, and why not.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const answer: WatchAnswer = { wired: false, reason: "not-wired" };
 * ```
 */
export type WatchAnswer = { readonly wired: boolean; readonly reason?: TelemetryOffReason };

/**
 * The connect api (`app.connect`). The tools page uses the editor methods `connect.*`; this api is
 * for the bin, tests and a later MCP tool.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * editor.connect.directory().mode.on; // false until a tools page asks for device mode
 * ```
 */
export type ConnectApi = {
  /**
   * The device directory as the tools page sees it: device mode, where a LAN pairing is confirmed,
   * adb's availability, the phones adb lists, the pairings asking (never their codes) and the
   * devices linked with their open sessions.
   *
   * @returns A fresh frozen copy, built now.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // After "By wire" in the Connect panel, with a Galaxy A26 on USB that paired.
   * editor.connect.directory().wire[0]; // { serial: "R5CX30ABCDE", state: "device", transport: "usb", model: "SM-A266B", name: "Galaxy A26", os: "Android 15", phase: "linked", device: "d-7f3a" }
   * ```
   */
  directory(): DeviceDirectory;
  /**
   * The newest wired telemetry of a linked device a tools page watches.
   *
   * @param device - A device id from hub.devices().
   * @returns The record of the last tick, undefined when the device is not attached.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The Galaxy A26 is the source of a tools page: its Mali GPU at the bottom clock.
   * editor.connect.telemetry("d-7f3a")?.gpu; // { available: true, source: "/sys/kernel/gpu", value: { mhz: 221, busyPct: 63, minMhz: 221, maxMhz: 949 } }
   * ```
   */
  telemetry(device: string): DeviceTelemetry | undefined;
};
~~~

### 7.11 collector — server, Complex

- depends: `[filesPlugin, hubPlugin, connectPlugin]` (connect for its per-plugin `connect:telemetry` only). Lifecycle: `onInit` (checks the config; registers the mark route `{path}/perf/mark` on every server, before `serve()` or `listenDevices()` freeze the routes), no `onStart` (nothing runs before `hub:device { kind: "listening" }`), `onStop` (clears the adb and throttle timers, marks every log done, awaits every queue bounded by 2 s; a queue still running is recorded as `stopTimedOut`).
- One JSONL file per device log, `perf-<yyyymmdd-hhmm>-<model>.jsonl` under `out`: every line the hub hands over is appended with `rx` (the computer's epoch ms at receipt); a reconnect with the token appends to the same file; one write queue per log, at most 8 MiB waiting (`QUEUE_MAX_BYTES`; beyond, lines are dropped and counted `lost`); at most 32 live logs per device (`MAX_LIVE_LOGS`). A device gap becomes one `gap` line.
- adb, only while device mode is on: every `reverseEveryMs` `adb devices` and `adb -s <serial> reverse tcp:<port> tcp:<port>`; every `everyS` seconds `dumpsys battery` + `dumpsys thermalservice` (a `thermal` line, `source: "collector"`) and `dumpsys gfxinfo <appId>` (`<appId>.debug` preferred when installed; a `gfx` line), for a phone matched to exactly one live adb log of its model and of the configured app (a log whose app id differs from `appId` once `.debug` is stripped is left out; a log without an app id, from 0.15.0, stays in). Collector lines carry `t` on the phone's page clock and `rx` on the computer's. Without adb: `collector:adb-missing` once, no reverse, no heat or gfx lines; a LAN phone still logs.
- Wired telemetry: each `connect:telemetry` record becomes one computer-side `telemetry` line (`PerfTelemetryLine` `{ v: 1, kind: "telemetry", t, rx, build, device, serial, wired, gpu, cpu, memory, heap }`, about 1 KiB a second) in that device's newest live log, only while the log records (from its first batch until a `recorder` stop line, again from a start line); never in the phone's own log. `parsePerfLog` counts `telemetry` lines and keeps them out of every table.
- Clean text: every phone string passes `cleanText` (`perf/protocol/text.ts`: C0, C1, DEL and bidi controls dropped, 128 characters) before the editor shows it; the file keeps the lines as sent.
- The computer mark: `mark(label)` writes `{ v: 1, kind: "mark", t, build, rx, label, auto: false, from: "computer" }` into every live log and answers how many got it; the route `POST {path}/perf/mark` (hub guard same-origin, `authorization: Bearer <hub token>` compared timing-safe, plain-text body at most 4 KiB, label 1–200 characters) answers `{"marked":<n>}`; `moku-editor perf mark` posts it.
- `settled()` resolves when every step queued before the call is done (writes, closes, the `collector:session` that follows): the perf command awaits it between `hub.stopDevices()` and `editor.stop()`.
- Runtime-free `collector/report/` (imports only `perf/protocol` and its own files): `parsePerfLog`, `isPerfLog`, `bucketUpper`, `histPercentile`, `gfxPercentile`, `summarize` (one row per screen and rate; pool trims, warm-ups and the game's overlay changes per screen), `compare` / `COMPARE_THRESHOLD` (▲/▼ at ±10 %), `table`, `summaryText`, `compareText`, `primaryOf`, `headerRate`, `rankCauses`. pages' `perf summary` / `perf compare` print them.
- Events: emits `collector:session` (per-plugin: the first written batch at once, then at most once a second per log, and after `away` / `done`; pages hooks it); hooks the hub's `hub:device` and connect's `connect:telemetry`. Logs: `collector:reversed`, `collector:adb-missing`, `collector:adb-ambiguous`, `collector:reverse-failed` (info); `collector:write-failed`, `collector:queue-full`, `collector:log-cap` (warn, once per streak).

~~~ts
/**
 * Collector configuration.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ pluginConfigs: { collector: { out: "logs/perf", everyS: 5, appId: "com.example.garden" } } });
 * ```
 */
export type CollectorConfig = {
  /** Folder of the logs: relative to the files root, or absolute. Created on the first log. */
  out: string;
  /** Seconds between two adb readings (heat, system frames) of a phone. 1–3600. */
  everyS: number;
  /** Milliseconds between two `adb devices` + `adb reverse` rounds. ≥ 500. */
  reverseEveryMs: number;
  /** The adb command (a name on PATH or a path). */
  adb: string;
  /** The longest one adb command may run before it is killed. ≥ 500. */
  adbTimeoutMs: number;
  /**
   * The Android package of the game (its base identifier). The collector prefers `<appId>.debug` when
   * the phone has it (the debug build installs beside the store build), else `<appId>`. Undefined: no
   * gfx lines.
   */
  appId: string | undefined;
};

/**
 * The newest second of a device log, for a live line.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const last: SessionDigest = { t: 5917.4, path: "garden/boss", fps: 118, loopFps: 120, p90Ms: 9.1, gpuMs: 4.8, rate: 120, spikes: 1, causes: ["upload"], thermal: { status: 1, batteryC: 36.1 }, model: "SM-A266B", backend: "webgpu", engine: "0.14.12+9c41e0", build: "debug-20261014T160000Z" };
 * ```
 */
export type SessionDigest = {
  /** Page epoch ms of the newest sample. */
  readonly t: number;
  /** Flow path of the newest sample. */
  readonly path: string;
  /** Frames drawn per second (whole number). */
  readonly fps: number;
  /** Loop frames per second (whole number). */
  readonly loopFps: number;
  /** p90 of the loop gap of the newest second (its `gapMs.p90`), null when not measured. */
  readonly p90Ms: number | null;
  /** p50 GPU ms of the newest second, null without a GPU timer. */
  readonly gpuMs: number | null;
  /**
   * The loop's rate in fps now (the newest `rate` event's `to`, else the header's `rate.fps`, else
   * `header.config.maxFps` when > 0); null when unknown.
   */
  readonly rate: number | null;
  /** Spikes of the newest second. */
  readonly spikes: number;
  /** Primary causes of the spikes of the last 6 s, most frequent first. */
  readonly causes: readonly PerfCause[];
  /** The newest heat reading (device shell or adb). */
  readonly thermal: {
    readonly status: number | string | null;
    readonly batteryC: number | null;
  } | null;
  readonly model: string;
  readonly backend: "webgpu" | "webgl" | "none" | null;
  readonly engine: string | null;
  readonly build: string | null;
};

/**
 * The collector's computer-side line of a wired device's telemetry: one per `connect:telemetry`
 * tick while the device records, written only into the computer file (the phone's own log never
 * holds it). Editor-owned and additive to PerfLog v1, like `gap`. `serial`, `wired`, `gpu`, `cpu`,
 * `memory` and `heap` are the DeviceTelemetry fields verbatim: every reading keeps its `source`, or
 * its `reason` when it is not available, and `heap` holds every CDP sample and inferred GC of the
 * tick. `t` is the record's computer time on the log's page clock, through the log's offset (the
 * page clock is anchored once per log by the header's `timeOrigin`, `epochMs = timeOrigin + t`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const line: PerfTelemetryLine = { v: 1, kind: "telemetry", t: 5917.4, rx: 1791986084000, build: "debug-20261014T160000Z",
 *   device: "SM-A266B", serial: "R5CX30ABCDE", wired: true,
 *   gpu: { available: true, source: "/sys/kernel/gpu", value: { mhz: 221, busyPct: 63, minMhz: 221, maxMhz: 949 } },
 *   cpu: { cores: 8, app: { available: false, source: "none", reason: "not-found" },
 *     renderer: { available: false, source: "none", reason: "ambiguous" },
 *     surfaceflinger: { available: true, source: "/proc/612/stat", value: { pid: 612, name: "surfaceflinger", pct: 2.1, oneCorePct: 16.8 } } },
 *   memory: { app: { available: false, source: "dumpsys meminfo", reason: "warming-up" }, renderer: { available: false, source: "dumpsys meminfo", reason: "warming-up" } },
 *   heap: { available: false, source: "none", reason: "no-devtools-socket" } };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfTelemetryLine = {
  readonly v: 1;
  readonly kind: "telemetry";
  /** The record's `at` on the log's page clock (`at + offset`, 0.01 ms); `rx` while the log has no offset. */
  readonly t: number;
  /** Computer epoch ms when the collector wrote it. */
  readonly rx: number;
  /** The log's build. */
  readonly build: string | null;
  /** The log's normalized model. */
  readonly device: string;
  readonly serial: DeviceTelemetry["serial"];
  readonly wired: DeviceTelemetry["wired"];
  readonly gpu: DeviceTelemetry["gpu"];
  readonly cpu: DeviceTelemetry["cpu"];
  readonly memory: DeviceTelemetry["memory"];
  readonly heap: DeviceTelemetry["heap"];
};

/**
 * What the adb loop knows of one phone.
 */
export type AdbPhone = {
  readonly serial: string;
  /** getprop ro.product.model, normalized; null until read. */
  model: string | null;
  reversed: boolean;
  /** The resolved app package, re-read after 60 s. */
  package: { name: string | null; at: number } | undefined;
  /** The previous gfxinfo reading. */
  gfx: { totals: GfxTotals; at: number } | undefined;
};

/**
 * Payload of the collector's per-plugin event `collector:session`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * ctx.emit("collector:session", { device, file: "/game/.moku/perf/perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl", state: "live", lines: 1840, lost: 0, last: null });
 * ```
 */
export type CollectorSessionEvent = {
  readonly device: LinkedDevice;
  readonly file: string;
  /** live: the phone is connected; away: it left and may come back; done: device mode stopped. */
  readonly state: "live" | "away" | "done";
  readonly lines: number;
  readonly lost: number;
  readonly last: SessionDigest | null;
};

/**
 * The collector's per-plugin events, visible to plugins that list `collectorPlugin` in `depends`.
 */
export type CollectorEvents = { readonly "collector:session": CollectorSessionEvent };

/**
 * A log as the API reports it (fresh copy).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const info: CollectorSessionInfo = { device, log: "perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl", file: "/game/.moku/perf/perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl", state: "done", lines: 1840, lost: 0, last: null, stopTimedOut: false };
 * ```
 */
export type CollectorSessionInfo = {
  readonly device: LinkedDevice;
  readonly log: string;
  readonly file: string;
  readonly state: "live" | "away" | "done";
  readonly lines: number;
  readonly lost: number;
  readonly last: SessionDigest | null;
  /**
   * True when the app stopped while this log was still being written (onStop's 2 s bound ran out);
   * its last lines may be missing from the file. False otherwise.
   */
  readonly stopTimedOut: boolean;
};

/**
 * What the adb loop sees now.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const status: AdbStatus = { state: "on", phones: [{ serial: "R5CX30ABCDE", model: "SM-A266B", reversed: true }] };
 * ```
 */
export type AdbStatus = {
  readonly state: "off" | "on" | "missing";
  readonly phones: readonly {
    readonly serial: string;
    readonly model: string | null;
    readonly reversed: boolean;
  }[];
};

/**
 * The collector api (`app.collector`, `ctx.require(collectorPlugin)`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * await editor.collector.mark("boss"); // 1
 * ```
 */
export type CollectorApi = {
  /**
   * Every device log of this run, oldest first, as fresh copies. Still answers after `stop()`: a
   * log whose writes outlived onStop's 2 s flush bound carries `stopTimedOut: true` (teardown
   * cannot log it, so this is where it shows).
   *
   * @returns The logs; [] before any phone sent a line.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The perf command, after Ctrl+C, prints the summary of each file written in this run.
   * editor.collector.sessions().map(session => session.file);
   * // ["/game/.moku/perf/perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl"]
   * ```
   */
  sessions(): CollectorSessionInfo[];

  /**
   * Writes a mark from the computer into every live log: `{ v: 1, kind: "mark", t, build, rx,
   * label, auto: false, from: "computer" }`, with `t` on that log's page clock. The label is
   * trimmed.
   *
   * @param label - 1–200 characters after trimming.
   * @returns How many logs got the mark (0 when no phone is live).
   * @throws {TypeError} `[moku-editor] collector.mark: the label must be 1-200 characters.` with the
   * fix `Give a short name, for example "boss".` for an empty or long label.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // `moku-editor perf mark "boss"` reaches this through the mark route.
   * await editor.collector.mark("boss"); // 1
   * ```
   */
  mark(label: string): Promise<number>;

  /**
   * The adb loop now: off while device mode is off, missing when adb could not run, else the
   * phones it sees.
   *
   * @returns A fresh status.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The perf command names the phones whose port it reversed.
   * editor.collector.adb(); // { state: "on", phones: [{ serial: "R5CX30ABCDE", model: "SM-A266B", reversed: true }] }
   * ```
   */
  adb(): AdbStatus;

  /**
   * Resolves when every step queued on a log before the call is done: its writes, the close of
   * its file and the `collector:session` that follows. After `hub.stopDevices()` that is every
   * log's `done` event, which the collector emits from the log's queue a few ticks after the hub's
   * `stopped`. Resolves at once when nothing is pending.
   *
   * @returns When the logs' queues have drained.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The perf command's Ctrl+C: device mode off, every done line printed, then the editor stops.
   * await editor.hub.stopDevices();
   * await editor.collector.settled(); // each log's collector:session { state: "done" } went out
   * await editor.stop();
   * ```
   */
  settled(): Promise<void>;
};
~~~

### 7.12 pages — server, Complex

- depends: `[filesPlugin, hubPlugin, collectorPlugin]`. Lifecycle: `onInit` only (`initPages`: check config, find the built page, `hub.addRoutes`).
- Routes (`P = hub.path()`): `P` → 308 to `P/`; `P/` → tools page with the boot tag (503 when not built or before start); `P/hello` → `HelloBody` JSON (same-origin); `P/hmr` → `HotReload` JSON on GET, a change on POST `{ hmr: boolean }` with `Authorization: Bearer <boot.token>` (200 with the state afterwards: the asked state when the bin switches, the unchanged one for a refused change, which the caller compares with what it asked, round 2b R16; 400 for a bad body; 401 without the token); `P/assets/*` → hashed assets, immutable cache. With `toolsPage: false` (`moku-editor perf --no-ui`) `P`, `P/` and `P/assets/*` answer 404 after the guard.
- Hot reload (D-23, round 2 R6): the bin serves with `development: { hmr: true, console: true }` (`--no-hmr`: `hmr: false`) and calls `attachServer(options)` right after `Bun.serve`. `hotReload()` is `{ hmr, owner }`, owner `"server"` with `hmr: false` until `attachServer`. Bun 1.3.14 cannot apply `development.hmr` on `server.reload` (spike in the pages README), so the bin passes `attachServer(options, restart)` and `setHotReload(on)` restarts its server with HMR flipped on the same port (D-32, `serve.ts`: stop bounded to 500 ms, then, only before a server with HMR, a wait of at most 5 s until Bun's bundler is idle (D-57, `waitForBundler`: an empty in-memory `Bun.build` that Bun queues behind a page rebundle still in flight; a wait that is cut or fails is one warning and the restart goes on), then `Bun.serve`); it answers true, sets and publishes the asked state at once and restarts after the answer went out (A1); a failure logs `pages:hot-reload-restart-failed`, publishes the old state and serves the old options again. A game's own server answers false.
- Boot tag: `<script type="application/json" id="moku-editor-boot">` with `ToolsBoot` `{ v: 1, ws, token, path, title, editorUrl, gameUrl, root }`.
- `PAGE_CSP` (exported from `routes.ts`): `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; worker-src 'self' blob:; img-src 'self' data: blob:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; connect-src 'self' ws://127.0.0.1:* ws://localhost:*; frame-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'`.
- Home of the `moku-editor` bin, its `mcp` and `mcp-config` subcommands, the `.moku/editor.json` discovery file and the stdio MCP bridge in `mcp/` (which names its MCP client to the hub with `client { name }`), and of the perf CLI in `perf/` (`perf`, `perf mark`, `perf summary`, `perf compare`; see "Bin" in section 6). `attachPerf(output)` (called once by `runPerf` after `hub.listenDevices`) makes each `collector:session` print the live lines through the bin's console.
- Events: hooks the collector's per-plugin `collector:session`. Logs: `pages:not-built` (warn at init, error at first request), `pages:hot-reload` (info, `attachServer`), `pages:hot-reload-read-only` (info, a refused change).

~~~ts
/**
 * Pages configuration.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ pluginConfigs: { pages: { editorUrl: "cursor://file/{path}:{line}", toolsPage: false } } });
 * ```
 */
export type PagesConfig = {
  /** Tools page <title> and boot title. */
  title: string;
  /** "Open in editor" link template (D-08): {path} absolute file path, {line} 1-based line. */
  editorUrl: string;
  /** Folder with the built tools page; undefined = dist/tools next to the module. */
  pageDir: string | undefined;
  /** Same-origin URL of the game page the tools page embeds (R3). */
  gameUrl: string;
  /** Serve the tools page and its assets; false answers 404 there (moku-editor perf --no-ui). */
  toolsPage: boolean;
};

/**
 * The server the bin attaches: Bun's Server is one. Pages reads nothing of it; a Hot reload switch
 * goes through the bin's restart, which reaches the current server (A9).
 */
export type AttachedServer = {
  /** The real port, undefined for a unix socket. */
  readonly port?: number | undefined;
  /**
   * Stops the server.
   *
   * @param closeActiveConnections - True closes the open connections at once.
   * @returns Resolves once the server stopped.
   */
  stop(closeActiveConnections?: boolean): Promise<void>;
};

/**
 * The bin's restart (D-32): stops its game server and serves these options on the same port. The
 * hub keeps running, so its token stays. Rejects when the new server cannot start.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const restart: RestartServer = next => game.restart(next);
 * await restart({ ...options, development: { hmr: false, console: true } });
 * ```
 */
export type RestartServer = (options: BunServeOptions) => Promise<void>;

/**
 * The pages api (`app.pages`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * Object.keys(app.pages.routes()); // ["/__editor", "/__editor/", "/__editor/hello", "/__editor/hmr", "/__editor/assets/*"]
 * ```
 */
export type PagesApi = {
  /**
   * A copy of the routes this plugin registered with the hub in onInit, keyed by URL path under
   * the hub path.
   *
   * @returns The five routes `P`, `P/`, `P/hello`, `P/hmr` and `P/assets/*`.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // Check which editor URLs the server answers.
   * Object.keys(app.pages.routes()); // ["/__editor", "/__editor/", "/__editor/hello", "/__editor/hmr", "/__editor/assets/*"]
   * ```
   */
  routes(): EditorRoutes;
  /**
   * Tells pages that the moku-editor bin serves the game with these options: the bin owns hot
   * reload from now on, HMR is read from `options.development`, and the state goes to every tools
   * page through `hub.publish("hotReload", …)`. With `restart`, `setHotReload` can switch HMR by
   * restarting the server (D-32). The bin calls it right after its first `Bun.serve`.
   *
   * @param options - The options it was started with (the result of `hub.serve`).
   * @param restart - Stops the bin's current server and serves new options on the same port.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The bin, after it started the game server.
   * const options = editor.hub.serve({ port, development: { hmr: true, console: true }, routes });
   * const game = createGameServer(options, (code, reason) => editor.hub.closeAll(code, reason), {
   *   warn: message => ui.warn(message)
   * });
   * editor.pages.attachServer(options, next => game.restart(next));
   * editor.pages.hotReload(); // { hmr: true, owner: "bin" }
   * ```
   */
  attachServer(options: BunServeOptions, restart?: RestartServer): void;
  /**
   * The hot reload state: whether Bun reloads the game page on a source change, and who owns the
   * server. A game's own `Bun.serve` (no `attachServer` call) is owner "server" with HMR off.
   *
   * @returns A fresh `{ hmr, owner }`.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // A game's own dev server that never attached it.
   * app.pages.hotReload(); // { hmr: false, owner: "server" }
   * ```
   */
  hotReload(): HotReload;
  /**
   * Asks for Bun HMR on or off, and publishes the state. Bun cannot switch HMR on a running
   * server, so the bin's server restarts with HMR flipped on the same port (D-32): the asked state
   * is set and published at once, and the restart runs after the answer went out (A1). A failed
   * restart is logged, the old state is published again and the old options are served again. A
   * game's own server always answers false; a bin attached without a restart answers true only
   * when its HMR already equals `on`.
   *
   * @param on - The asked value.
   * @returns True when the bin owns the server and its HMR equals `on` or is switching to it; false
   * otherwise (a game's own server always answers false).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The bin serves with HMR on; the tools page asks for it off.
   * await editor.pages.setHotReload(false); // true: the server restarts without HMR
   * editor.pages.hotReload(); // { hmr: false, owner: "bin" }
   * ```
   */
  setHotReload(on: boolean): Promise<boolean>;
  /**
   * Prints a live line per phone log from now on: each `collector:session` becomes the lines of
   * the perf command (header with engine and build, STALE warning, a stats line at most every 5 s,
   * left / done). Call it once, after hub.listenDevices; without it the collector's events print
   * nothing.
   *
   * @param output - Where the lines go: the bin's brand console.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // runPerf, after the device listener is up: the lines go to any sink with line and warn.
   * const lines: string[] = [];
   * editor.pages.attachPerf({ line: text => lines.push(text ?? ""), warn: text => lines.push(`! ${text}`) });
   * // on the first log batch of a phone: "◉ SM-A266B · webgpu · engine 0.14.12+9c41e0 · build debug-20261014T160000Z · adb 127.0.0.1"
   * ```
   */
  attachPerf(output: PerfOutput): void;
};

/**
 * Arguments of `moku-editor [<game-html>] [--port 3000] [--root .] [--no-hmr] [--preload FILE]…
 * [--serve-plugin FILE]…`: serve the game. Without `html` the engine writes the page of the
 * moku-game folder at `root` (the engine page); the two lists feed only that page.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // moku-editor --root games/timber --serve-plugin plugins/marker.ts
 * const args: RunArgs = { kind: "run", port: 3000, root: "games/timber", hmr: true, preload: [], servePlugins: ["plugins/marker.ts"] };
 * ```
 */
export type RunArgs = {
  readonly kind: "run";
  /** The game HTML file, when given; the key is left out for the engine page. */
  readonly html?: string;
  /** The port on 127.0.0.1: 3000 by default, 0 for a random free port. */
  readonly port: number;
  /** The project root as given (default "."): the editor reads and writes there. */
  readonly root: string;
  /** False with `--no-hmr`: Bun serves the game without hot reload. */
  readonly hmr: boolean;
  /** Every `--preload`, as given: files Bun preloads in the serving process (engine page only). */
  readonly preload: readonly string[];
  /** Every `--serve-plugin`, as given: Bun plugins the page bundles with (engine page only). */
  readonly servePlugins: readonly string[];
};

/**
 * `run` arguments with the game HTML file: what the bin serves, itself or from a re-spawned bin.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const args: ServeArgs = { kind: "run", html: "/g/.moku/index.html", port: 0, root: "/g", hmr: true, preload: [], servePlugins: [] };
 * ```
 */
export type ServeArgs = RunArgs & { readonly html: string };

/**
 * Arguments of `moku-editor mcp [<game-html>] [--port N] [--root DIR] [--no-hmr]`: the stdio MCP
 * bridge. `html`, `port` and `hmr` only feed the bin the bridge starts when none runs; a live
 * `.moku/editor.json` under `root` wins.
 */
export type McpArgs = {
  readonly kind: "mcp";
  /** The game HTML file, when given. */
  readonly html?: string;
  /** The port, when `--port` was given. */
  readonly port?: number;
  /** The project root (default "."): where `.moku/editor.json` is read. */
  readonly root: string;
  /** False with `--no-hmr`. */
  readonly hmr: boolean;
};

/**
 * Arguments of `moku-editor mcp-config [<game-html>] [--port N]`: print the `.mcp.json` snippet
 * and the `claude mcp add` line for the same `mcp` arguments.
 */
export type McpConfigArgs = {
  readonly kind: "mcp-config";
  /** The game HTML file, when given. */
  readonly html?: string;
  /** The port, when `--port` was given. */
  readonly port?: number;
};

/**
 * Arguments of `moku-editor e2e -c <playwright config> [playwright args…]`: one Playwright run per
 * project and spec file of the config, each on its own `PORT` (D-52, D-53). Only `-c` / `--config`
 * is read here; `e2e.ts` sorts the other words for the list run and the runs.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // moku-editor e2e -c tests/browser/playwright.config.ts -g pick --headed
 * const args: E2eArgs = { kind: "e2e", config: "tests/browser/playwright.config.ts", rest: ["-g", "pick", "--headed"] };
 * ```
 */
